Hehir attributes the team's strong start to a combination of home-grown talent and key professional signings, including Sebastian Cole, Peter Turay, and Tiras Morton. The squad has also been bolstered by the addition of underage players Callum Keys, Hubert Gocek, and Max Turski.

The rise of Limerick basketball is further highlighted by the competitive performances of the Limerick Eagles, fostering a local rivalry that recently drew a substantial crowd to the UL Arena. Celtics will look to defend their league-leading position when they face UCC Demons in Round Seven on November 14.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.localAngle: The Celtics' success and the emerging derby rivalry with Limerick Eagles are drawing strong local crowds and boosting the profile of indoor sport in the city.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.originalTitle: ‘Limerick basketball on the rise’ as Celtics take top spot in Super League

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.headline: Shannon Airport Group shortlisted for Public Enterprise of the Year
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.summary: The Shannon Airport Group has been named a finalist for Public Enterprise of the Year at the 2026 Business & Finance Awards. The winners will be announced at a gala ceremony in Dublin on December 10.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.story:
The Shannon Airport Group has secured a shortlist nomination for Public Enterprise of the Year at the upcoming 2026 Business & Finance Awards. This marks the second consecutive year the group has reached the final stage in the category.

In the running for the top prize, The Shannon Airport Group is joined by fellow nominees An Post, Fáilte Ireland, and Údarás na Gaeltachta. The category recognises excellence in operations, stakeholder engagement, and the delivery of sustainable public value.

Ray O’Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, welcomed the announcement, noting that the recognition reflects recent progress in passenger growth, facility investment, and sustainability. "As Shannon Airport and the Shannon Airport Business Park continue to grow, we’re proud of the role we play in supporting tourism, investment and job creation across the West of Ireland," he said.

The overall winners of the 52nd annual Business & Finance Awards will be revealed during a gala ceremony at the Convention Centre in Dublin on Thursday, December 10.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.localAngle: The Shannon Airport Group plays a vital role in supporting tourism, investment, and job creation across Limerick and the wider Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.originalTitle: Airport on runway for Public Enterprise Awards

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.headline: O’Donovan Seeks Council Answers After Adare Feral Cat Habitat Paved Over
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.summary: Limerick City and County Council has paved over a wooded area in Adare used by a feral cat colony to install a rainwater system. While shelters remain accessible, Councillor Elisa O’Donovan is calling for assurances regarding the cats' welfare and ecological impact assessments.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.story:
A wooded area in Adare that served as a long-standing home for a colony of feral cats has been paved over, prompting calls for clarification from local representatives. The council-owned site was altered to accommodate a rainwater-harvesting system installed by Adare Tidy Towns, alongside the replacement of surrounding fencing for health and safety reasons.

Councillor Elisa O’Donovan raised the issue with Limerick City and County Council after learning of the works. While the local authority has confirmed that the cats' shelters remain in place and that the new fencing allows continued access for both the animals and the volunteers who feed them, Cllr O’Donovan argues that the broader environmental impact requires scrutiny.

Speaking to the Limerick Voice, Cllr O’Donovan said she is seeking assurances regarding the suitability of the current shelters and whether any ecological assessments were conducted before the project began. She emphasized that even small green spaces function as vital local habitats that demand careful planning.

The councillor has urged the local authority to consult directly with the volunteers who have cared for the Adare colony over the years, ensuring the animals retain secure living conditions and that greenery is restored where possible. She noted that supporting community volunteers and protecting vulnerable local wildlife are important responsibilities for the local community.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.localAngle: The issue involves council-owned land and local animal welfare volunteers in the County Limerick town of Adare.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.originalTitle: Concern over welfare of Limerick cats after habitat is paved over

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.headline: Tributes Paid Following Passing of Garryowen Stalwart John Fahey
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.summary: Garryowen Football Club has paid warm tributes following the death of former President, Chairman, and Trustee John Fahey. Fahey, a familiar face around the club, presided over the historic 2006/07 season when the club achieved a unique clean sweep of four major trophies.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.story:
Garryowen Football Club is mourning the loss of John Fahey, a prominent club stalwart who served as President, Chairman, and Trustee. Tributes have poured in from across the local rugby community following his passing.

Honorary Secretary Sandra Maher remembered Fahey for his immense contribution to the club and Irish rugby. She noted that as recently as the previous Saturday, he had been supporting the senior team, enjoying a pre-match meal with friend Steve McDonagh, and looking forward to an upcoming trip to Armagh. 

"We will miss his gentle manner, his kindness, his friendship and the genuine interest he took in everyone around him," Ms Maher said in a statement. She added that he was reunited in death with his dearest wife, Kathleen.

Recalling his leadership, past President Billy Purcell noted on rip.ie that during Fahey’s tenure as Chairman in the 2006/07 season, Garryowen accomplished a nationwide unique feat by winning the Grand Slam, All-Ireland League, All-Ireland Cup, Munster Senior Cup, and Munster Junior Cup. Outside of his deep involvement in local rugby, Fahey was widely known in Limerick for his many years working as General Manager at the Limerick Inn.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.localAngle: John Fahey was a deeply embedded figure in Limerick rugby and hospitality, having served as General Manager of the Limerick Inn and leader of Garryowen FC.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.originalTitle: Tributes after passing of Garryowen stalwart

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.headline: Folk Band Kingfishr Surprise Limerick Fans with Pop-Up Gig on Cruises Street
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.summary: Limerick shoppers got a surprise treat when folk trio Kingfishr performed an impromptu gig on Cruises Street as part of a four-city whistle-stop tour to announce their upcoming second album.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.story:
Shoppers on Cruises Street were treated to an unexpected performance on Saturday afternoon as folk band Kingfishr arrived in the city for a surprise pop-up gig.

The trio—made up of Eddie Keogh, Eoghan McGrath and Eoin Fitzgibbon—took to the Limerick street at approximately 1.30pm as part of a whirlwind tour across four Irish cities in one day. The band kicked off their schedule in Galway at 10.30am before heading to the Treaty City, with subsequent stops planned for Cork at 5pm and Dublin at 9.30pm.

The surprise visit was organised to celebrate the announcement of their second album, 'Weight of the Feather', which is scheduled for release on April 9, 2027. The album's title track will be released next Friday, November 13.

The appearance carried a strong local resonance for the band, who are former University of Limerick students. The visit comes ahead of two major homecoming concerts at Thomond Park scheduled for July 2027, following a string of successes that includes their breakthrough hit 'Killeagh' and their debut album, 'Halcyon'.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.localAngle: The band have strong ties to Limerick as former University of Limerick students and are returning to the city for major concerts at Thomond Park in July 2027.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.originalTitle: Kingfishr take over Cruises Street today for surprise pop-up

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.headline: TUS President Vincent Cunnane oversees final graduation before January retirement
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.summary: Founding TUS President Professor Vincent Cunnane conferred his final student in Limerick on Friday, bringing an estimated 35,000 graduates to his total over his career.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.story:
Technological University of the Shannon (TUS) founding President Professor Vincent Cunnane presided over his final conferring ceremony in Limerick on Friday, marking the end of a tenure that has seen him personally confer an estimated 35,000 graduates across three higher education institutions.

Fittingly for an academic who began his career in scientific research, the final student to cross the stage was James Ryan from Mungret, Limerick. Ryan was awarded a Doctor of Philosophy for his research into how advanced technology can make workplaces safer. Professor Cunnane, who will retire at the end of January, admitted he felt emotional during the ceremony and said graduation events had been among the most rewarding parts of his presidency.

"Graduations are where it all comes together, where all those stories culminate in success. They walk across the stage as equals, as professionals, as people with a future," Professor Cunnane said. "And for me, that's just the magic of being in this role. And I'm going to miss it terribly."

In his final address, he told the Class of 2026 that human judgement and critical thinking would become increasingly valuable in a world shaped by Artificial Intelligence. Professor Cunnane will be succeeded by Professor Paul Connolly, who takes up the role in spring 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.localAngle: The final graduation ceremony took place in Limerick, concluding with a local PhD recipient from Mungret.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.headline: Major Irish Banks Launch Professional Banking Apprenticeship Offering NFQ Level 8 Degree
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.summary: AIB, Bank of Ireland, and PTSB have partnered with the IOB to launch a new banking apprenticeship. The programme gives 75 participants paid experience alongside studying for a Level 8 degree.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.story:
A new professional banking apprenticeship has been launched by the IOB in a major partnership involving AIB, Bank of Ireland, and PTSB. The initiative offers participants the opportunity to earn an NFQ Level 8 degree while gaining paid, practical experience within the banking sector.

Apprentices will split their time between working in the industry and studying with the IOB, which is a recognised college of UCD. The scheme is open to school leavers and anyone looking for a career change, provided applicants are at least 18 years old on or before August 31, 2027.

A total of 75 places will be made available for the first intake of students. Applications are now open, with the successful candidates set to commence the programme in October 2027. Further details and application information can be found at apprenticeship.ie or via the IOB website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.localAngle: The nationwide apprenticeship programme provides training and employment pathways for prospective banking professionals in Limerick and across the country.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.originalTitle: New apprenticeship programme for Limerick bankers

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.headline: Council to assess feasibility of new Castleconnell to Nelsons Cross walkway
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.summary: Independent Councillor Ursula Gavan has called for a new pedestrian route connecting Castleconnell Campsite to the village via Nelsons Cross. The local authority has agreed to carry out a preliminary assessment of the route.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.story:
Limerick City and County Council has agreed to examine the feasibility of building a new walkway linking the Castleconnell Campsite to the village via Nelsons Cross.

The project was pushed forward by Independent Councillor Ursula Gavan during this month's Metropolitan District meeting, where she urged the local authority to prioritise the infrastructure.

Responding to the proposal, council officials noted that the route could significantly improve pedestrian connectivity and encourage greater access between the campsite and local amenities.

The Council's Transportation, Mobility & Public Realm Directorate confirmed that the local Area Office will now conduct a preliminary assessment. This initial phase will look at the feasibility of the route, required land, and estimated construction costs before potential funding streams are explored.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.localAngle: The proposed walkway aims to improve pedestrian access and local amenities for residents and visitors in Castleconnell.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.originalTitle: Cllr Gavan calls for walkway from Castleconnell to Nelsons Cross

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.headline: Banned 1971 Masterpiece 'The Devils' Finally Sees Irish Release After 50 Years
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.summary: Ken Russell's controversial 1971 film 'The Devils' is finally screening in Ireland in a landmark director's cut. The film was banned for over half a century due to its depictions of religious persecution and institutional corruption.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.story:
Cinema history's most notorious and controversial film, Ken Russell’s 1971 masterpiece 'The Devils', is finally seeing the light of day in Ireland after being banned for over half a century. The film has returned in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of the original vision.

Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, played by Oliver Reed, the film explores his accusation of bewitching a convent of nuns. Grandier's unorthodox views on sex and religion draw a passionate following, including the sexually obsessed Sister Jeanne, played by Vanessa Redgrave. To gain control of France, power-hungry Cardinal Richelieu, played by Christopher Logue, works to eliminate Grandier by portraying him as a satanist and sparking public outrage.

Upon its release over 50 years ago, the work was condemned as sacrilegious and reprehensible, sparking scandal over its depiction of institutional religion and possessed nuns. The explosive fever dream features surrealistic sexual defilement, manic spiritual elation, and medieval violence and torture.

While the film might not stir the same level of outrage by today’s standards, its core message concerning the collusion of church and state, religious persecution, and institutional corruption continues to strike a chord with modern audiences.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.localAngle: Film enthusiasts across Limerick can now view the landmark director's cut of Ken Russell's notorious 1971 work following its long-awaited Irish release.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.headline: Over €150,000 Allocated for Youth Facilities and Equipment Across Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.summary: More than €150,000 in funding has been secured for youth facilities and equipment across Limerick, supporting projects from Rathkeale to the city. The investment will fund minor works, digital equipment, and safety upgrades.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.story:
More than €150,000 in funding has been secured for youth facilities and equipment across Limerick, following an announcement made last month by Minister Patrick O'Donovan.

The funding package includes €8,530 for Limerick Youth Service’s Rathkeale/Askeaton project and a combined €24,739 for the two Foróige Loobagh projects. Additional allocations will go to Limerick Sports Partnership, Limerick Youth Theatre, Bluebox Creative Learning, and various youth services operating across Limerick city.

The investment is earmarked to support a range of improvements, including minor building works, digital equipment, recreation resources, arts and music equipment, accessibility improvements, and safety upgrades.

“This is a practical investment in our young people,” Minister O’Donovan said. “It will help youth services across Limerick replace ageing equipment, improve their buildings and provide welcoming spaces.”
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.localAngle: The funding directly benefits youth clubs, organizations, and services across Limerick city and county, including Rathkeale, Askeaton, and the Loobagh projects.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.originalTitle: Over €150,000 announced in youth facilities and equipment in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.headline: Contracts Signed for €28M Limerick Level Crossing Overhauls
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.summary: Iarnród Éireann has signed a €28 million contract to upgrade seven public road level crossings, including the closure of crossings at Fantstown and Thomastown in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.story:
Contracts have officially been signed for a major €28 million improvement project affecting seven manned public road level crossings, including key locations in County Limerick. 

Under the works funded by the Department of Transport through the National Transport Authority, the level crossings at Fantstown and Thomastown will be permanently closed. In their place, new replacement bridges or alternative road solutions will be provided at both Limerick locations.

Following a recent procurement and tendering process, contractor Jons Civil Engineering Ltd is expected to arrive on site in the coming days to begin the infrastructure upgrades. 

Irish rail authorities have confirmed that the extensive improvement project is scheduled for completion by April 2028.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.localAngle: The project directly impacts local transport infrastructure in Limerick with the permanent closure and replacement of level crossings at Fantstown and Thomastown.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.originalTitle: Contracts signed for road levels crossings in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.headline: Two Arrested in Enniskillen Over Murder of Limerick Mother Carrie Mullane
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.summary: Two more people have been arrested by the PSNI on suspicion of the murder of 39-year-old Limerick mother-of-four Carrie Mullane, whose remains are currently being searched for in County Fermanagh. A man has already appeared in court charged in connection with her disappearance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.story:
Two additional people have been arrested in connection with the ongoing murder investigation into Limerick woman Carrie Mullane. A woman in her 60s and a man in his 30s were taken into custody in Enniskillen as part of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) probe.

Ms Mullane, a 39-year-old mother of four, was last seen on October 10 after travelling to County Fermanagh. The PSNI believe she was killed shortly after arriving in the area. Authorities are actively searching for her remains, with police divers focusing efforts on a section of Upper Lough Erne near Enniskillen over the weekend.

A 35-year-old man was arrested last week in connection with the case and has already appeared in court charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a corpse.

Detectives are continuing to appeal for public assistance. The PSNI has asked anyone with information, or who may have captured CCTV, phone, or dash-cam footage that could aid the investigation, to come forward.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.localAngle: The victim is a 39-year-old mother of four from Limerick who travelled to County Fermanagh before her disappearance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.originalTitle: Two further arrests in Limerick mother of four murder probe

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.headline: New residents group backs six-week traffic closure of The Crescent for Christmas
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.summary: A newly formed residents group supports closing The Crescent on O'Connell Avenue to traffic for six weeks this Christmas for a festive fayre. However, local traders warn the closure could cause severe traffic congestion and harm Christmas trade.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.story:
A newly formed Limerick residents group has thrown its weight behind proposals to close The Crescent on O'Connell Avenue to traffic for six weeks this Christmas. The Limerick City Centre Residents’ Voice (LCCRV), which was formed a month ago and recently hosted Mayor John Moran at a meeting, described the festive plans for Christmas 2026 as "ambitious". The proposed Christmas Fayre would span The Crescent, O'Connell Avenue, and Arthur’s Quay Park.

In a statement, LCCRV argued that vibrant public events help support economic activity and strengthen community spirit in the city. "As people who live, work and raise families in this area, we look forward to experiencing the buzz, atmosphere and sense of occasion that these events can bring," the group said, comparing the prospect to historic festive celebrations in cities like Prague and London.

However, the plans have met resistance from local business owners concerned about traffic disruption during the busiest retail period of the year. Fifth-generation city shop owner Shane Gleeson urged the local authority to vary the event licence and relocate the Christmas Market to Arthur’s Quay or Honan’s Quay.

Mr Gleeson warned that holding the event at The Crescent would lead to severe traffic congestion and negatively impact trade when maximum traffic flow is vital for businesses. He added that relocating the fayre to Honan's Quay would better complement the existing ice rink and offer easier access to nearby parking facilities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.localAngle: The proposed traffic closure of The Crescent and the staging of a major Christmas Fayre directly impacts city centre residents, motorists, and local traders in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.originalTitle: Newly formed group welcomes closure of Crescent despite traders concerns

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.headline: Shannon Man Charged with Race Hate Crime and Threating Security at UHL
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.summary: A 38-year-old man has appeared in court charged with a racially motivated hate crime and breaching the peace at University Hospital Limerick on Halloween night. The judge granted bail with conditions after hearing the accused is seeking help for drug addiction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.story:
A man appeared before Ennis District Court on Monday charged in connection with an alleged race hate crime committed against a Pakistani security guard at University Hospital Limerick (UHL) on Halloween night. 

At the court hearing, Garda Roisín Moran stated that Martin O’Callaghan (38), of High Street, Lissycasey, tried to flee Garda custody at the hospital's A&E Department on Saturday, October 31st. Garda Moran alleged that Mr O’Callaghan called a security staff member, who is a Pakistani national, 'monkey face' in the presence of Gardaí, made a sound of pooling saliva as if to spit, and claimed he was HIV positive.

Gardaí had arrested Mr O’Callaghan earlier that day in Kilrush over a separate public order incident. He was brought to UHL after telling officers he had swallowed a bag of cocaine, though he ultimately refused medical assistance at the hospital. He is formally charged with provoking a breach of the peace and demonstrating hatred towards the security guard on account of his race, colour, or nationality.

Defence counsel Elaine Davern Wiseman BL told the court that her client's wish is to get help for a long-standing drug abuse struggle. Judge Catherine Ryan granted bail, noting the allegations are of particular concern given they occurred in a hospital setting. Mr O’Callaghan was remanded on bail to appear again in Ennis District Court on November 25, under conditions that include staying out of Kilrush and residing at a bail address in Rossbracken, Shannon.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.localAngle: The alleged incident took place at University Hospital Limerick, a vital regional healthcare facility serving the local community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.originalTitle: Court appearance on charge of ‘monkey face’ taunt at security guard

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.headline: Pedestrian killed in single-car collision on M20 northbound outside Limerick City
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.summary: A pedestrian was struck and killed by a car on the M20 motorway between Raheen and Dooradoyle on Sunday evening. Gardaí have launched an investigation and are appealing for witnesses and dash-cam footage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.story:
Gardaí are investigating a fatal traffic incident after a pedestrian was killed in a single-car collision on the M20 motorway outside Limerick City on Sunday evening (November 8).

The incident occurred at approximately 5.20pm on the northbound stretch of the motorway between Junction 3 (Raheen) and Junction 2 (Dooradoyle). The pedestrian was pronounced dead at the scene, and no other injuries were reported.

The M20 was temporarily closed following the collision to allow Garda Forensic Collision Investigators to conduct a technical examination. The local coroner has been notified, and arrangements are being made for a post-mortem examination.

Authorities are urging anyone who was travelling on the M20 between Junctions 3 and 2 on Sunday evening from 5pm to 5.30pm, particularly those with dash-cam or other camera footage, to contact Henry Street Garda Station on 061 212 400 or the Garda Confidential Line on 1800 666 111.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.localAngle: The fatal collision occurred on a major commuter route just outside Limerick City, prompting a local appeal for witnesses by Henry Street Gardaí.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.originalTitle: Pedestrian killed in crash on motorway outside Limerick City

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362993.headline: Limerick-Based Rugby Legend Niamh Briggs Inducted into Hall of Fame
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362993.summary: Former Ireland captain and UL Bohemians star Niamh Briggs has been inducted into the Heineken Rugby Players Ireland Hall of Fame at a ceremony in Dublin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362993.story:
Limerick-based rugby great Niamh Briggs was officially inducted into the Heineken Rugby Players Ireland Hall of Fame during a special luncheon at Dublin’s InterContinental Hotel last week. Briggs was joined by fellow rugby figures Rory Best and John Muldoon in receiving the prestigious recognition.

Established in 2003, the Hall of Fame honors individuals who have made an outstanding contribution to the sport, factoring in both on-field achievements and their wider influence on teammates, the game, and the community. Briggs earned over 60 international appearances and stood at the heart of a transformative era for Irish women’s rugby, featuring prominently in the historic 2013 Grand Slam, the 2014 World Cup semi-final run, and captaining the team to a Six Nations title in 2015.

Domestically, her career was defined by five Interprovincial titles with Munster and her standout performances for UL Bohemians. After stepping away from playing, Briggs has remained active in the sport locally through coaching and player development.

The Hall of Fame luncheon celebrated three distinct careers marked by leadership and a lasting connection to the teams and people they represented.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362993.localAngle: Niamh Briggs is a long-term Limerick resident, former UL Bohemians player, and five-time Interprovincial winner with Munster.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362993.originalTitle: Hall of Fame inductee Niamh Briggs

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362912.headline: Teen sent to Circuit Court over Shannon assaults including head-stamping incident
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362912.summary: A teenager accused of carrying out violent attacks in Shannon—including stamping on a victim's head and taking a photo—will face trial at Ennis Circuit Court after a judge declined jurisdiction in the Children's Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362912.story:
A 17-year-old accused of a series of violent attacks in County Clare, including an incident where a victim was photographed on the ground before being stamped on, has been sent forward for trial at the Circuit Court.

At the Children’s Court in Ennis, Detective Garda Paul Coleman outlined the State's case concerning three alleged assaults in Shannon during May and October 2025. Det Garda Coleman told Judge Adrian Harris that the level of violence used was "considerable" and that the accused was "front and centre" in the attacks on two men on October 26, 2025, at Brú na Sionna. The court heard that one victim was dragged from grass to a pavement before being stamped on the head, with mobile phone footage capturing the accused taking a photo of the man on the ground before striking him again.

A separate incident on May 5, 2025, involved the alleged assault of an off-licence owner in Drumgeely after he gave chase following a theft. Garda Colette Acton stated the teenager attempted to bite the owner, pulled him down by the head, and struck him three times with a hurley.

Defence solicitor Stiofán Fitzpatrick told the court his client was in the throes of addiction at the time, was now in gainful employment, and had not come to Garda attention since. Following the evidence, Judge Harris declined jurisdiction, meaning the youth will now face the charges at Ennis Circuit Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362912.localAngle: The case involves serious criminal proceedings in the region handled through the local court system serving neighboring County Clare.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362912.originalTitle: Teen accused of assault took photo of alleged victim on the ground

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363020.headline: Body recovered from Lough Erne in search for missing Limerick mother Carrie Mullane
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363020.summary: Gardaí and the PSNI are liaising with the family of missing Limerick mother-of-four Carrie Mullane after a specialist team recovered a body from Lough Erne in County Fermanagh. Two people remain in police custody being questioned on suspicion of murder, while another man has already appeared in court charged with murder.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363020.story:
Gardaí and the Police Service of Northern Ireland are liaising with the family of a missing Limerick mother after a body was recovered this afternoon from Lough Erne in County Fermanagh. Specialist police search teams located the remains in Upper Lough Erne near the village of Carrybridge during the search for 39-year-old Carrie Mullane, who had not been seen since October 10.

Investigators believe Ms Mullane was killed shortly after arriving in Enniskillen. While formal identification of the recovered remains has not yet taken place, the PSNI confirmed that officers have been in contact with her family to inform them of the development and to provide ongoing support. Detective Superintendent Richard Thornton from the Serious Crime Branch appealed for anyone with information to contact police on 101, referencing number 272 of 29/10/26, or to share footage through the Major Incident Public Portal.

Meanwhile, the murder investigation continues with two additional suspects currently being questioned. Detectives have been granted an extra 36 hours to question a man in his 30s and a further 24 hours to question a woman in her 60s, both of whom were arrested yesterday on suspicion of murder. Over the weekend, a 35-year-old man appeared in court charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a corpse.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363020.localAngle: The search and ongoing murder investigation centre on the disappearance and death of Carrie Mullane, a mother of four from Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363020.originalTitle: Body recovered in search for missing Limerick mother of four

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363018.headline: Limerick woman Scarlett Faulkner died from catastrophic brain injuries after iron bar beating
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363018.summary: A murder trial has heard that Limerick woman Scarlett Faulkner died from catastrophic brain injuries following an attack with a metal iron bar in Co Tipperary earlier this year. The 17-year-old defendant has pleaded guilty to manslaughter, while a 41-year-old co-accused denies murder.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363018.story:
A post-mortem examination revealed that Limerick native Scarlett Faulkner died from a "catastrophic brain injury" caused by blunt force trauma from a metal iron bar, the Central Criminal Court was told on Monday.

Assistant State Pathologist Dr Margaret Bolster told the judge and jury that Ms Faulkner, who had an address at Longpavement in Limerick, sustained severe injuries during an incident in Birdhill, Co Tipperary, on March 21. She was transferred from University Hospital Limerick to Cork University Hospital on March 27, where she remained in a deeply comatose state until life support was withdrawn on April 13.

Dr Bolster detailed extensive injuries, including a bleed to the brain, skull fractures, facial trauma, and a ruptured right eyeball. Toxicology reports showed the presence of cocaine, benzodiazepines, and fentanyl in her system, though the pathologist noted that her history of drug abuse did not contribute to her death.

A 17-year-old girl has pleaded not guilty to murder but guilty to manslaughter in connection with the attack. A 41-year-old woman has also pleaded not guilty to murder, along with separate charges of burglary and assault causing harm. The trial continues before Mr Justice Kerida Naidoo and a jury.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363018.localAngle: The victim, Scarlett Faulkner, was originally from the Longpavement area of Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363018.originalTitle: Limerick woman died from catastrophic brain injury after beating with an iron bar

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362990.headline: Garryspillane Farmer Jailed for Two and a Half Years Over Neglect of Hundreds of Calves
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362990.summary: Seamus Looby, 68, pleaded guilty to 173 animal cruelty charges after dead and rotting calves were discovered across his 100-acre farm in County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362990.story:
A 68-year-old Co Limerick farmer has been jailed for almost two and a half years after admitting to 173 animal cruelty offences following the discovery of numerous dead and rotting calves on his land. Seamus Looby, of Raheen, Garryspillane, was sentenced at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court after Department of Agriculture inspectors uncovered a devastating scene of neglect across his 100-acre farm.

Judge Fiona O’Sullivan described the situation as a “shocking level of neglect” that caused a high level of distress, suffering, and death. The court heard that spinal cords, jawbones, and leg bones belonging to dead calves were found scattered across the property. Of the 420 calves connected to the farm, only 84 were found alive, with 66 of those having to be euthanised.

Department of Agriculture veterinary inspector Chris Normoyle told the court that in his 21 years of experience, it was one of the worst cases of animal neglect he had ever encountered. Investigators found surviving animals severely dehydrated and exhausted, while others had succumbed after becoming too weak to escape a water source. 

Judge O’Sullivan reduced a headline sentence of four and a half years to three years and four months, suspending the final 12 months, noting that Looby was socially isolated, vulnerable, and manipulated by others. Looby previously received a fine for causing unnecessary suffering to more than 30 dogs delivered to his farm in a similar manner.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362990.localAngle: The case was prosecuted at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court following an investigation into a farm in Garryspillane, County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362990.originalTitle: Farmer jailed after calf skeletons found in ‘shocking’ animal cruelty case

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362917.headline: Archers of Limerick launches beginner archery courses in Cappamore
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362917.summary: Archers of Limerick is hosting two beginner training programmes at Cappamore Sports Hall this November, with options for both a one-day intensive session and a four-week course.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362917.story:
Local residents looking to try a medieval skill can sign up for two new beginner courses announced by Archers of Limerick. The training sessions will be held at Cappamore Sports Hall.

Participants can choose between a one-day intensive course running on Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 5pm, or a four-week evening programme starting on Wednesday, November 25, at 6pm. 

No prior experience is necessary, and all required equipment will be provided. Attendance costs €80 for adults and €60 for juniors, with class sizes strictly capped at eight participants. Parents or guardians are required to remain present during all junior sessions.

Anyone interested in securing a place or seeking further information can contact Richard directly by phone at 086 340 2334 or via email.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362917.localAngle: The training sessions provide an accessible local sporting opportunity for Limerick residents interested in learning archery.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362917.originalTitle: Archers beginners course for Limerick juniors

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362986.headline: Crowds turn out as Limerick Greyhound Stadium hosts Irish St Leger Round 2
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362986.summary: Round 2 of the Bet Irish St Leger 550 got underway at Limerick Greyhound Stadium over the weekend, drawing crowds of local racegoers and supporters. The event featured notable wins, including Myles Cummins' dog Snuggie Battie taking victory in the Limerick and Clare GOBA A2 525.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362986.story:
Racing fans and local supporters descended on Limerick Greyhound Stadium over the weekend as the second round of the prestigious Bet Irish St Leger 550 got underway.

Among the highlights of the weekend's action was Myles Cummins' greyhound, Snuggie Battie, which secured victory in the Limerick and Clare GOBA A2 525 Round 1 Heat 4. Trackside cameras captured local attendees getting in on the action and enjoying the atmosphere across the race card.

Racegoers spotted at the stadium over the weekend included Patrick and Mikey, Mary and Ellie Regan, as well as Peter Hayes, Barry Morrissey, Sarah Greene, and Peter, Robert, and Luke O'Brien.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362986.localAngle: The event brought local greyhound racing enthusiasts together at Limerick Greyhound Stadium for the latest round of the prestigious competition.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362986.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Out the traps again for Irish St Leger

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53708.headline: University of Limerick football squad travels to Maynooth for CUFL quarter-final
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53708.summary: The University of Limerick senior team takes on Maynooth this afternoon at 2pm with a place in the CUFL Premier Division semi-finals on the line.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53708.story:
University of Limerick's senior football squad faces Maynooth away this afternoon in the CUFL quarter-final, aiming to secure a spot in the competition's semi-finals.

UL head into the clash looking for their second win from four games this season. Their campaign began with a tightly contested opening-day defeat to UCC in Cork, where Liam O’Sullivan found the scoresheet. They bounced back in their second outing with a 2-0 away victory against SETU Carlow, courtesy of goals from Matt Jones and Colin Doody. Two weeks ago, UL hosted their first home game of the season at Maguires Astro against TU Dublin, falling 2-1 despite an Oisín Breen goal and a sensational free-kick from the visitors.

Speaking ahead of the fixture, UL Senior Team member Conor Carew highlighted the opportunities given to emerging players. "Plenty of fresh faces have got the chance to play intervarsity football," Carew said, adding that this "bodes well as we look forward to the major competitions being held in semester two."

UL have enjoyed a strong start overall, with all four of the university's teams progressing to the knockout stages of their respective leagues. Kick-off for this afternoon's crucial quarter-final is at 2pm.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53708.localAngle: The University of Limerick's senior team is representing the county in the intervarsity CUFL quarter-final.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53708.originalTitle: UL look to reach CUFL semi-finals with Maynooth test

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53697.headline: Six Treaty United Players Named on PFAI Transfer Lists Ahead of 2027 Season
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53697.summary: Six players with links to Treaty United have been placed on the PFAI transfer lists as preparations begin for the 2027 League of Ireland season. The inclusions highlight ongoing concerns over player security in the First Division.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53697.story:
Five men's players and one women's representative with links to Treaty United have been named on the Professional Footballers’ Association of Ireland’s (PFAI) transfer lists ahead of the 2027 League of Ireland season. The men's list, released on November 9, includes defender Darren Nwankwo, midfielders Colin Conroy, Steven Healy and Ronan Manning, and attacker Brian Cunningham. Goalkeeper Katherine Hess represents the club on the women's list, which was published the previous week.

Inclusion on the lists does not necessarily mean a player has been released or intends to leave their current club. Instead, it allows players to make themselves available to other interested clubs who can make contact through the PFAI. Also featuring on the men's list is 20-year-old forward Jason Folarin Oyenuga, who spent the 2026 season on loan at Treaty from St Patrick’s Athletic and scored eight league goals before his contract expired.

Former Limerick FC player and academy coach Jason O’Connor said the transfer lists expose a lack of security for players operating on year-to-year contracts in the First Division. O'Connor noted that more Treaty players might have been expected on the list following a difficult 2026 campaign, and questioned whether the club remains an attractive destination for local talent as the Limerick FC name prepares to return to senior football in 2027.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53697.localAngle: Six players with ties to Treaty United have been named on PFAI transfer lists, as local figures debate the club's appeal to regional talent ahead of Limerick FC's return in 2027.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53697.originalTitle: Six Treaty United players feature on PFAI transfer list ahead of 2027 season

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53696.headline: Hans Zimmer tribute, Andy Irvine and Twilight rave head up Limerick's weekly events
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53696.summary: Limerick venues are hosting a packed week of entertainment, featuring folk music at Dolans, a Candlelight concert at St. Mary's Cathedral, and a Twilight-themed rave.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53696.story:
Music and theatre lovers across Limerick have an eclectic lineup of events to look forward to this week, ranging from cinematic orchestral tributes to contemporary folk performances.

Traditional music gets underway on Thursday as renowned Irish musician Andy Irvine takes to the stage at Dolans Bar and Restaurant, accompanied by Swedish band Quilty to showcase a unique blend of Irish and Swedish folk. On the same night, the Belltable theatre will screen a live stage recording of 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses' from the National Theatre, bringing Christopher Hampton’s classic tale of social warfare to local audiences.

The weekend kicks off on Friday, November 13th, with St. Mary’s Cathedral hosting the first in a series of immersive Candlelight concerts. Organised by live entertainment company Fever, the opening night features a multisensory tribute to composer Hans Zimmer, with performances of iconic film scores from 'Pirates of the Caribbean' and 'The Dark Knight'. Fever representatives noted that the series aims to broaden classical music access through fresh interpretations of popular artists like ABBA and Queen.

For pop culture fans, Friday night also brings the fan-made "Hoa-Hoa-Hoa Rave" to Dolans, celebrating the 'Twilight' saga with soundtrack anthems, dark pop, and 2000s hits alongside visuals from the films.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53696.localAngle: A diverse lineup of live music, theatre, and themed events is taking place across prominent Limerick venues including Dolans, St. Mary's Cathedral, and the Belltable.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53696.originalTitle: Music by Candlelight and More: What’s Happening in Limerick This Week

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363022.headline: Maigue Rivers Trust hosts Limerick farming info evenings on water grants
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363022.summary: Local farmers are invited to attend upcoming information evenings in Granagh and Lough Gur to learn about grant funding and practical measures to improve water quality in the River Maigue catchment.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363022.story:
Farmers across the Maigue catchment are being invited to attend two upcoming information evenings hosted by the Maigue Rivers Trust to learn about grant funding and practical steps to improve local water quality.

The events will introduce Aidan Suart, the Trust’s newly appointed Farming for Water Agricultural Community Animator. Suart will work directly with farmers to explain available measures under the Farming for Water programme, outline financial supports, and assist with grant applications.

Two information sessions are scheduled in County Limerick. The first takes place on Monday, November 2, at Granagh Community Hall (V35 C584), followed by a second session on Tuesday, November 10, at the Lough Gur Visitor Centre (V35 ED96).

Both evenings begin with an opportunity to meet Suart from 6pm, followed by food and refreshments at 6.30pm and an information talk at 7pm. Interested farmers can contact Aidan Suart directly on 086 172 2537 for further details.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363022.localAngle: The initiative directly supports farmers and waterways across the River Maigue catchment in County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363022.originalTitle: Farmers Invited to Learn About Funding to Improve Local Water Quality

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363004.headline: Infinity Aviation Support Expands With New Shannon Offices Marking Second Anniversary
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363004.summary: International aviation consultancy Infinity Aviation Support has celebrated its second anniversary by opening new offices at Westpark Business Campus in Shannon, having completed over 50 projects across 15 countries since 2024.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363004.story:
Shannon-based aviation company Infinity Aviation Support has marked its second anniversary with the official opening of a new base of operations at the Westpark Business Campus. Founded in 2024 by aviation industry expert Anthony Attoumani, the international consultancy provides specialized services in aircraft design, engineering, certification, risk analysis, and training.

The company celebrated the milestone and office opening at an event attended by regional business, government, and aviation representatives, including Shannon Chamber Chief Executive Helen Downes, Honorary Consul of France in Limerick Loïc Guyon, and Clare TD Cathal Crowe. Over the past two years, the firm has delivered more than 50 projects across 15 countries to support its international growth.

Speaking at the event, founder and CEO Anthony Attoumani said that opening the new Shannon offices is an important step in the firm's development. "We are ambitious for the future and excited to continue growing our business from one of Europe’s leading aviation hubs," he stated.

Local representatives welcomed the expansion as a testament to the strength of the Mid West region's aviation cluster. Deputy Cathal Crowe praised the company's rapid global growth, noting that Shannon serves as a key location for specialized aviation services and international connections.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363004.localAngle: The expansion reinforces the Mid West region's status as a leading European aviation hub and centre of excellence for specialized industry services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363004.originalTitle: Infinity marks second anniversary with opening of new Shannon offices

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363057.headline: Limerick Council Appoints Arup to Drive Colbert Quarter Infrastructure
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363057.summary: Limerick City and County Council has appointed Arup as the project management, design, and engineering team to advance infrastructure packages for the Colbert Quarter. The project will unlock land for new housing, a public park, and improved walking and cycling routes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363057.story:
Limerick City and County Council has taken a major step forward in the development of the Colbert Quarter by appointing Arup as its multi-disciplinary project management, design, and engineering team. The appointment was marked at a formal contract signing attended by Mayor of Limerick John Moran alongside representatives from the local authority and Arup.

Arup will oversee a rolling programme of infrastructure packages, which include sustainable urban drainage systems, new roads, utilities, and enhanced pedestrian and cycling connections. These works are designed to unlock land for housing, investment, and economic activity, while better connecting established communities to public transport and future development zones.

Mayor John Moran said the project offers an opportunity to build a new part of Limerick correctly from the start. "It will bring new homes, but also a major park at its heart, safe routes to walk and cycle, and the sports facilities and public spaces that build real community. Appointing Arup means the plans now move towards boots on the ground," he said.

The initiative builds on the Colbert Quarter Spatial Framework 2022–2042, which was developed for the council in partnership with the Land Development Agency, CIÉ, and the HSE. Key elements of the broader programme include a proposed public park and sustainable urban drainage scheme, featuring recreation facilities and biodiversity enhancements.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363057.localAngle: The development will transform a major urban area in Limerick, bringing new homes, parks, and infrastructure to the city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363057.originalTitle: Major developments as Colbert Quarter on the starting block

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53665.headline: Treaty United star Madison McGuane trials with WSL side Brighton
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53665.summary: Limerick teenager and Republic of Ireland international Madison McGuane is drawing heavy interest from English clubs, recently featuring on trial with Women's Super League side Brighton & Hove Albion.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53665.story:
Treaty United midfielder Madison McGuane is on the radar of several English clubs, with the 17-year-old recently spending time on trial at Women’s Super League side Brighton & Hove Albion. The Limerick native, who made her League of Ireland debut at just 15, has also visited WSL 2 side Newcastle United as English clubs monitor her development.

McGuane's rise through the ranks has seen her collect multiple accolades, including the 2025 SSE Airtricity Women’s Premier Division Young Player of the Year and PFA Ireland Women’s Young Player of the Year awards. She was also named in the 2026 PFA Ireland Women’s Premier Division Team of the Year and claimed the Player of the Month award for April, alongside balancing her Leaving Certificate studies at St Mary’s Secondary School in Limerick City.

On the international stage, the St Mary's student has represented the Republic of Ireland from U15 to U19 level. She recently captained the U19 squad during their European Championship qualifying campaign in October, scoring four goals in three matches, and has already caught the attention of senior Ireland manager Carla Ward.

Because McGuane does not turn 18 until August 2027, any permanent transfer to an English club will have to wait until she reaches adulthood. Until then, the young talent remains focused on her commitments with Treaty United and her studies in Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53665.localAngle: Madison McGuane is a Treaty United player, a student at St Mary’s Secondary School in Limerick City, and a standout local talent in Irish women's football.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53665.originalTitle: Treaty United teenager Madison McGuane on the radar of English clubs

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363013.headline: Tredwell Electrical opens 18,000 sq. ft. Shannon facility as part of 35-year milestone
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363013.summary: Tredwell Electrical has marked its 35th anniversary by opening an 18,000 sq. ft. manufacturing facility at Shannon Airport Business Park. The expansion brings the company's total manufacturing footprint to 37,200 sq. ft. alongside its existing Limerick operation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363013.story:
Tredwell Electrical, part of the Induchem Group, has officially opened its new 18,000 sq. ft. manufacturing facility at the Shannon Airport Business Park in County Clare. The plant was officially opened by Minister of State Timmy Dooley TD, complementing the firm's existing 19,200 sq. ft. operation in Limerick and bringing its total manufacturing footprint to 37,200 sq. ft.

Glenn Bain, General Manager of Tredwell Electrical, said: "We are very excited to open the new state of the art facility in Shannon, to help meet future expansion and production requirements." The new facility was established with the support of The Shannon Airport Group in a business park that currently houses over 300 companies and employs more than 10,000 people.

The company has experienced significant growth in recent years, doubling both its turnover and workforce, with plans to create 80 new engineering jobs over the next three years. Founded in 1991 by Stefan Uhlemann in a 100 sq. ft. garage, Tredwell Electrical now specialises in electrical control and distribution panels, machine integration, and wiring looms for customers across Ireland, Europe, and the US in sectors including pharmaceuticals, data centres, and water treatment.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363013.localAngle: The new Shannon facility complements Tredwell Electrical's existing Limerick operation, significantly expanding the company's manufacturing footprint in the Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363013.originalTitle: Tredwell Electrical celebrates 35 years with new Shannon manufacturing facility

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363063.headline: Nenagh man found guilty of murdering 89-year-old Josie Ray following Limerick trial
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363063.summary: A Central Criminal Court jury sitting in Limerick has convicted Hasan Ali Gori of murdering 89-year-old Josephine Ray at her Tipperary home in August 2024. The 52-year-old showed no emotion as the majority verdict was delivered following a three-week trial.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363063.story:
A jury at the Central Criminal Court has found 52-year-old Hasan Ali Gori guilty of murdering his then-girlfriend's 89-year-old mother, Josephine “Josie” Ray, two years ago. Gori, a native of Chad with an address in Nenagh, Co Tipperary, showed no reaction when the 11-1 majority verdict was delivered following a three-week trial held in Limerick.

During the trial, the court heard that the great-grandmother died of strangulation and smothering after sustaining 44 bruises and two broken bones in her neck. Senior prosecuting counsel Lorcan Connolly told the jury that Ms Ray had tried to "fight off" her attacker, with state evidence showing Gori's DNA under the victim's fingernails and damage to her forearms from the struggle.

Prosecutors argued that Gori, who had been living in a hostel before moving in with Ms Ray and her vulnerable daughter Mary, had both motive and opportunity to commit the murder. The court heard neighbours had previously reported constant rows at the property, and that Gori was at risk of losing his housing and associated social welfare payments after facing potential eviction.

Following the verdict, the matter was concluded at the Central Criminal Court, where the jury delivered its decision after hearing extensive evidence from forensic experts, Gardaí, and neighbours regarding the events leading up to the August 2024 tragedy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363063.localAngle: The trial took place before a Central Criminal Court jury sitting in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363063.originalTitle: Guilty verdict in trial of man accused of murdering Josie Ray

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363010.headline: Limerick Bus Driver Derek Lane Wins Regional Excellence Award After 36 Years
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363010.summary: Long-serving Limerick bus driver Derek Lane has been honoured at the 2026 GEM Awards, taking home the RP Driver Excellence Award for the West after 36 years of service with Bus Éireann.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363010.story:
A Limerick bus driver with nearly four decades behind the wheel has been recognised for his outstanding service and reliability at the 2026 GEM Awards.

Derek Lane was awarded the RP Driver Excellence Award in the West by Bus Éireann, marking 36 years of service to the company. The accolade recognises excellence in core road passenger driving responsibilities, including punctuality, customer care, professional presentation, cashing in, and collaboration with colleagues and supervisors.

Mr Lane was singled out by company leadership for his flawless attendance record, which officials pointed to as an example of exceptional reliability in keeping local communities connected. 

Allen Parker, Chief Customer Officer at Bus Éireann, praised the Limerick driver's long-standing contribution. "Derek’s 36 years of service represent a remarkable commitment to Bus Éireann and the communities we serve," Mr Parker said, adding that his consistent standards reflect the professionalism expected of road passenger drivers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363010.localAngle: A Limerick-based Bus Éireann driver with 36 years of service was honored for his exceptional reliability and connection to local communities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363010.originalTitle: Limerick bus driver recognised at GEM Awards

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362994.headline: Ballingarry's Billy Lee and Abbeyfeale's Paddy Hartnett crowned Irish racing champions
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362994.summary: Billy Lee secured his first Champion Jockey title with 99 winners, while fellow Limerick native Paddy Hartnett claimed the Champion Apprentice crown at the Curragh.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362994.story:
Limerick racing celebrated a historic double after Billy Lee of Ballingarry was crowned Ireland’s Champion Jockey and Abbeyfeale's Paddy Hartnett secured the Champion Apprentice title at the Curragh.

At 40 years old, Lee realised a lifetime ambition by finishing the calendar year with 99 winners from nearly 650 rides, making him the oldest first-time title winner since 1978. His success was bolstered by over 30 winners from Tipperary trainer Paddy Twomey, including a lucrative victory in the Goffs Million on Trean. Lee is the first Limerick jockey to capture the senior crown since the late Liam Ward of Rathkeale in 1961.

Meanwhile, 24-year-old Paddy Hartnett clinched the Champion Apprentice category with 29 wins, sealing the title following a late-season surge that featured a treble at Punchestown.

"This championship is as much for the people supporting me as it is for me," Lee said following his achievement. Hartnett added: “It’s crazy. I just want to thank absolutely everybody that’s followed me and supported me; owners, trainers, even jockeys. It’s massive to me and my career.”
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362994.localAngle: Billy Lee and Paddy Hartnett brought two of Irish horse racing's top titles home to County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362994.originalTitle: A racing double to savour for Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363016.headline: Limerick School of Art and Design to host university futures exhibition
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363016.summary: An exhibition exploring higher education in Limerick in the year 2070 arrives at the Limerick School of Art and Design this Thursday as part of Irish Design Week.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363016.story:
What higher education in Limerick could look like by 2070 is the central question behind a new exhibition coming to the city this week.

Created by Studio Saol, 'The Pluriversity' will be hosted at the Limerick School of Art and Design (LSAD) this Thursday, November 12, as part of the nationwide Irish Design Week events.

The project arrives in Limerick following previous exhibitions in Copenhagen and at Dutch Design Week. Developed in collaboration with the University of Limerick Foundation and Rethink Ireland, the showcase draws on research and direct engagement with students, academic staff, and local communities to explore the future evolution of higher education.

Locals and visitors interested in attending can find booking and event details through the Design & Crafts Council Ireland (DCCI) event listing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363016.localAngle: The exhibition examines the future evolution of higher education specifically in Limerick, hosted locally at the Limerick School of Art and Design.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363016.originalTitle: New exhibition exploring future of Limerick

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53720.headline: Rape Crisis Midwest Reveals 85% of Sexual Violence Victims Still Do Not Report
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53720.summary: Rape Crisis Midwest says 85% of sexual violence victims still do not report their experiences. The centre's helpline remains busy despite low formal reporting rates.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53720.story:
Eighty-five percent of people who experience sexual violence still do not report it, according to Siobhán O’Leary, Executive Director of Rape Crisis Midwest. Speaking to the Limerick Voice, O'Leary said society remains “very far away” from a point where survivors feel comfortable coming forward with formal reports.

The comments follow the sentencing of British actor Russell Brand to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault, a high-profile case that has renewed public conversation surrounding sexual violence and the barriers victims face in reporting.

Despite the low reporting statistics, O’Leary noted that the regional centre's helpline remains consistently busy, with high volumes of engagement occurring online through social media direct messages and email inquiries. She added that long-term staff members have not observed a significant shift in reporting patterns over decades of service.

For anyone affected by sexual violence, support services remain available across the region. O'Leary stressed that local services are ready to assist survivors. Anyone seeking support can visit rapecrisis.ie or email info@rapecrisis.ie.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53720.localAngle: The figures highlight the ongoing challenges faced by Rape Crisis Midwest in supporting survivors across the region.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53720.originalTitle: ‘85% of people still do not report sexual violence’ says Executive Director at Rape Crisis Midwest

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363138.headline: Gardaí Confirm Limerick School Bomb Threats Are A Nationwide Hoax
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363138.summary: Schools in Limerick and across the country received emailed bomb threats on Wednesday, but Gardaí and the Department of Education have confirmed the messages are bogus and evacuations are unnecessary.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363138.story:
A number of schools in Limerick received emailed bomb threats on Wednesday, though Gardaí have confirmed they believe the alerts are entirely bogus. 

The threatening messages, described as generic emails warning of a bomb hidden in a plastic bag on school grounds, were sent to approximately 300 schools nationwide, including institutions in Limerick, Cork, and Dublin. While some schools in Cork initially evacuated pupils and staff, Gardaí subsequently informed educational facilities across the country that the threats are a hoax and advised that full evacuations are not required beyond precautionary general security checks.

The Department of Education issued a communication to schools following consultations with senior Gardaí, confirming that institutions need not evacuate. 

Wednesday's incident follows a series of similar bomb threats reported across Ireland in recent days, which have included emergency aircraft diversions and the evacuation of media organizations, notably forcing the national broadcaster RTÉ off air briefly last week.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363138.localAngle: Limerick schools were among the approximately 300 institutions nationwide targeted by the bogus emailed bomb threats on Wednesday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363138.originalTitle: Schools bomb threats declared a hoax

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363044.headline: Cocaine Surges to Nearly Half of All Treatment Cases in the Mid West
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363044.summary: Powder and crack cocaine accounted for 43 per cent of addiction treatment presentations at Coolmine's Mid West services in the first nine months of 2026, driven by a sharp rise in powder cocaine use.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363044.story:
Powder cocaine accounted for almost one third of addiction treatment presentations at Coolmine’s Mid West services during the first nine months of 2026, according to the organisation's latest report. Combined with crack cocaine, the substances made up 43 per cent of all treatments at the regional centre, a significant increase from 32 per cent during the same period last year.

The surge in powder cocaine—which rose to 29 per cent of presentations, up from 18 per cent previously—brings it close to alcohol, which accounted for 31 per cent of regional cases. Crack cocaine remained steady at 14 per cent. Notably, the regional findings contrast with national figures, where the combined share of both drugs remained stable at 34 per cent. The data also revealed that women accounted for 97 per cent of those presenting to the Mid West services.

David McPhillips, Coolmine’s Mid West Services Manager, emphasized that regional trends require tailored responses. "The rise in powder cocaine’s share of presentations in the Mid West is a reminder that national trends do not tell the whole local story," he said. McPhillips added that treatment services must account for family and maternal circumstances, noting that "delivering the National Drugs Strategy 2026–2030 in the Mid West will depend on services having the resources to respond to changing needs."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363044.localAngle: The report highlights shifting addiction treatment trends and resource demands specific to Coolmine's services across the Mid West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363044.originalTitle: Cocaine responsible for nearly half of the addicts seeking treatment in the Mid West

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363075.headline: New Book Explores How Limerick Hosted U2's Historic First Gig in 1978
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363075.summary: A newly published book by Brian O'Connell details the night a young Dublin band won the Pop Group '78 competition at the Stella Ballroom, marking their official debut under the name U2.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363075.story:
A new book exploring the origins of one of the world's biggest rock bands has been released, focusing on the night a young Dublin group performed under the name U2 for the very first time in Limerick.

*Becoming U2* by Brian O'Connell, published on November 8, examines the Pop Group ’78 competition held at the Stella Ballroom during Limerick Civic Week. The Harp Lager-sponsored event saw the group—then known as The Hype—change their name before taking to the stage to ensure they wouldn't be stuck with the moniker if they won. Bassist Adam Clayton previously described the competition as the exact point the band became U2, while drummer Larry Mullen Jr noted that winning the Limerick contest fundamentally changed their lives.

Author Brian O'Connell spent more than 15 years working on the book, a project that began after a plaque was unveiled at the city centre venue in 2011. He noted that despite the band identifying the Limerick gig as their first public appearance under the U2 name, accurate records regarding the date and location were scarce, with the only detailed contemporary report appearing in the Evening Press in March 1978.

The publication has also revived local hopes that the band might return to Limerick for a homecoming concert in 2028 to mark the 50th anniversary of their historic debut.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363075.localAngle: The book explores Limerick's pivotal role in music history as the location where U2 played their first official gig and won a band competition in 1978.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363075.originalTitle: New book revives hopes of U2 homecoming in Limerick in 2028

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53743.headline: Former UL Graduate William Keohane Launches Debut Memoir ‘Out There’
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53743.summary: Former University of Limerick graduate William Keohane has released his debut memoir, ‘Out There’, exploring grief, gender transition, and identity from an Irish perspective. He will conclude his UK and Irish book tour at O’Mahony’s in Limerick this Thursday.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53743.story:
Former University of Limerick graduate William Keohane released his debut memoir, ‘Out There’, on November 10. Keohane, who completed an MA in Creative Writing at UL, said he initially expected to focus on poetry during his studies, but found himself compelled to write prose that eventually formed the basis of his new book.

Published by And Other Stories, the memoir offers a trans and Irish perspective on grief, gender transition, and grappling with identity. Keohane cited the fearlessness of Irish women authors such as Sinéad Gleeson, Sara Baume, and Doireann Ní Ghríofa as major inspirations during his writing process, alongside the support of his UL classmates and teachers, including Joseph O’Connor, Donal Ryan, and Kit de Waal.

Keohane is currently touring eight bookshops across the UK and Ireland. The tour concludes this Thursday, November 12, at 7pm with an event at O’Mahony’s in Limerick, where he will be in conversation with acclaimed author and former teacher Joseph O’Connor. For Keohane, finishing the tour at O’Mahony's holds personal significance, noting that the book itself is partly about coming home to Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53743.localAngle: The author is a UL graduate concluding his book tour with a homecoming event at O'Mahony's in Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53743.originalTitle: Limerick author William Keohane releases debut memoir ‘Out There’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363049.headline: Minister Niall Collins Opens Free Teagasc Forestry Events for Limerick Landowners
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363049.summary: Limerick landowners are invited to attend four free evening forestry information events organised in conjunction with Teagasc. Minister of State Niall Collins will open the series in Templeglantine.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363049.story:
Limerick landowners looking to learn more about forestry have been invited to attend a series of four free evening information events organised in conjunction with Teagasc.

Minister of State at the Department of Agriculture, Limerick TD Niall Collins, will officially open the information campaign at the Devon Inn in Templeglantine Village.

Each event kicks off with two informative presentations followed by a panel discussion, giving attendees the chance to hear directly from a local farmer about their personal forestry journey.

Participants will also have the opportunity to speak face-to-face with professional Forestry Inspectors from the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine, alongside Teagasc Forestry Advisors. The events are entirely free and open to all interested members of the public, with further schedule details available on the department’s website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363049.localAngle: The event series specifically caters to Limerick landowners and is being opened by local TD and Minister of State Niall Collins.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363049.originalTitle: Limerick Minister opens free forestry information events

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363034.headline: Milford NS claim Celtic Image Shield with final victory over Scoil an Spioraid Naoimh
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363034.summary: Milford National School secured the girls Gaelic football Celtic Image Shield at Na Piarsaigh GAA Grounds, defeating Scoil an Spioraid Naoimh 2-3 to 0-3 in the final.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363034.story:
Milford National School were crowned champions of the Celtic Image Shield following a strong display in the girls Gaelic football final at Na Piarsaigh GAA Grounds.

Having advanced past Herbertstown in the semi-final stages, Milford went on to claim the silverware with a 2-3 to 0-3 victory over Scoil an Spioraid Naoimh of Roxborough. Early goals from Ava Barry and Ruth Larkin set the tone for the winners, while teammates Éillidh McMillan, Ella Burns, and Laurie Earls also delivered key performances on the pitch.

Despite the loss, the Roxborough outfit battled hard throughout the encounter, with Dalia Almuktar, Hazel Keogh, Sadie McNamara, Millie English, and Lily Conway putting in tireless shifts for Scoil an Spioraid Naoimh.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363034.localAngle: The primary schools' Gaelic football decider brought together young sports stars from across the local Limerick community at Na Piarsaigh GAA Grounds.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363034.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Fine win by Milford NS

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363060.headline: Hit-and-Run Sentence Appeal Adjourned Due to Solicitors' Dispute
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363060.summary: An appeal against a three-month jail sentence for a Clare man involved in a serious hit-and-run near Ardnacrusha has been delayed due to the ongoing solicitors' industrial dispute over legal aid fees.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363060.story:
The appeal hearing for 40-year-old Paul Dady at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court could not proceed as scheduled due to the ongoing solicitors' industrial dispute regarding legal aid fees. Dady, of Sixmilebridge, County Clare, was handed a three-month prison sentence last December after pleading guilty at Limerick District Court to dangerous driving, hit-and-run, failing to remain at the scene, and failing to report a collision.

The charges stem from a November 10, 2024, incident in Ardnacrusha, County Clare, where a 16-year-old boy was struck by a car. Prosecuting Garda Sergeant Aisling O'Neill previously told the court that Dady's vehicle crossed carriageways and mounted a footpath, knocking down the teenager who was walking with his younger brother. The driver left the scene without offering assistance or details, though the victim's brother photographed the car as it departed.

The injured teenager was taken to University Hospital Limerick (UHL) and later readmitted with worsening leg injuries that left him without use from the knee down, requiring a 13-night stay. Dady's legal representation previously argued the appeal on grounds of "severity," maintaining that Dady claimed he only heard a bang and did not realise he had struck a person. Judge Patricia Harney previously dismissed that explanation during sentencing, stating it "defies any kind of belief at all."

Dady, a native of Milton Keynes, UK, who was working as a maintenance man in County Clare at the time, turned himself in to a Garda station three days after the incident and expressed remorse. The matter has been put on hold pending the resolution of the legal aid dispute.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363060.localAngle: The court case was heard at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court following an incident investigated by Limerick-based Gardaí and initial proceedings at Limerick District Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363060.originalTitle: Hit and run sentence appeal adjourned over solicitors dispute

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363046.headline: Limerick Apprentices Win Four National Titles at Dublin Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363046.summary: Limerick talent secured four awards at the National Apprentice of the Year Awards in Dublin, with Johnson & Johnson's Sapna Sian taking the overall top title from over 500 nominees.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363046.story:
Limerick apprentices claimed a total of four awards at the recent Apprentice of the Year Awards Showcase held at the RDS in Dublin. Sapna Sian, a manufacturing technician apprentice with Johnson & Johnson Vision Care Limerick, beat over 500 nominees to be named Ireland’s National Apprentice of the Year 2026. She also collected the Engineering Industry Apprentice of the Year award, marking a notable milestone as a woman working in STEM.

Two other Shannonside apprentices joined Ms Sian in success at the 17-category competition. Auryn Souness of Johnson and Johnson MedTech in Plassey was named Logistics Apprentice of the Year for supply chain management, while Darragh Sweeney of H&MV Engineering in Castletroy took home the Electric Apprentice of the Year title.

Overseen by SOLAS, the Further Education and Training Authority of Ireland, the national awards recognise the leadership, teamwork, creativity, and problem-solving contributions made by apprentices across various industries. Nominees are put forward by employers, training providers, or peers.
