Following her win, Ms Sian said she was proud of her achievement as the first manufacturing technician apprentice to receive the top award. Mr Souness added that the supply chain manager apprenticeship had opened doors for him by connecting practical workplace experience with his learning.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363046.localAngle: Three local apprentices from Limerick employers secured four national titles at the RDS showcase in Dublin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363046.originalTitle: Top awards for Limerick talent at Apprentice of the Year awards

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363147.headline: All We Have Are Days festival returns to 25 Limerick venues
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363147.summary: The multi-venue arts festival will host 60 shows across pubs, churches, and theatres over the St Brigid's Bank Holiday weekend in January 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363147.story:
Limerick's pubs, churches, and theatres are gearing up for the return of the All We Have Are Days festival, which has announced its third edition will take place over the St Brigid's Bank Holiday weekend from Friday, January 29, to Monday, February 1, 2027. The four-day event will feature 140 artists performing 60 shows across 25 venues throughout the city.

The first wave of acts confirmed for the festival includes Dublin post-punk band Gurriers, traditional musician Cormac Begley, and Grammy Award-winning producer Thomas Bartlett. They will be joined by Denise Chaila, Feli Speaks, Bronagh Gallagher, Caoi de Barra, Anna B Savage, Dowry, ROE, Zkellies, Cruel Sister, Negro Impacto, and Pellador.

Venues participating in the 2027 programme include Dolan's, The Commercial, Mother Mac's, The White House, Flannery's, JJ Bowles, The Old Quarter, South's, Glen Tavern, 101, Costelloes, Theatre Royal, John's Church/Dance Limerick, Pharmacia, Myles Breen's, The Coach House at 2 Pery Square, and No 1 Pery Square, with further locations to be announced.

Festival director David O'Donovan said planning for the event has been ongoing since the conclusion of the last festival. Audiences can expect intimate pub sessions, pop-up performances, and a range of free events, with tickets for selected shows currently on sale through Eventbrite ranging from €10 to €28. Further programme additions will be announced in early December.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363147.localAngle: The festival utilizes 25 local venues, pubs, and historic spaces across Limerick city, bringing 140 artists to local audiences.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363147.originalTitle: All We Have Are Days festival returns to Limerick with 140 artists across 25 venues

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363050.headline: Limerick community groups urged to apply for €100k circular economy fund
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363050.summary: Time is running out for Limerick circular economy initiatives to apply for a share of a €100,000 national grant fund, with applications closing for the 2026 Circular.ie Communication Grants programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363050.story:
Community-led circular initiatives across Limerick have been issued a final call to apply for a €100,000 grant fund aimed at boosting their local impact. 

Backed by the Irish Government through the Circular Economy Fund, the national platform Circular.ie has launched its 2026 Communication Grants programme. The funding is specifically designed to help grassroots organisations amplify their operations through both physical and digital communications.

Successful applicants can secure up to €10,000 to help scale their reach, which includes practical projects such as developing and building out websites. The grants are targeted directly at groups and organisations that are already actively engaged in circular activities within their local communities.

Interested groups and organisations in Limerick can access further details and submit their applications by visiting the official website at Circular.ie/articles/apply-for-a-grant.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363050.localAngle: Limerick community-led circular initiatives are eligible to apply for a share of the national €100k funding pot to expand their local reach.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363050.originalTitle: Final call for €100k circular grand funding

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363031.headline: Kilmallock's Eddie Wiley and Effin's Mary Donovan Myers honoured in New York
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363031.summary: The Limerick Foundation will honour two expatriates at its annual banquet in Eastchester, New York, celebrating a stellar year for Limerick GAA.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363031.story:
The Limerick Foundation's annual celebration banquet takes place this Friday at Mulino’s at Lake Isle Country Club in Eastchester, New York, where two prominent figures with deep roots in the county will be honoured.

Foundation Chairman Finbar Flood of South Liberties pointed to a successful year for the county, noting that the seniors secured the All-Ireland Championship, National League, and Munster Senior Leagues, while the minors claimed their first All-Ireland title in 42 years. 

Eddie Wiley of Kilmallock has been named Guest of Honour. A founding member of Club Limerick New York, Wiley played hurling and football from his youth in Fitzgerald Park, winning a County Senior Hurling title in 1985 before moving to New York in 1989. He recently stepped down after serving as Club Chairman.

Mary Donovan Myers, originally from Effin, will receive the Club Person of the Year award. Donovan Myers, whose nephew Patrick O’Donovan currently plays on the senior panel, has served as Club Secretary with tremendous dedication since her election in 2019.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363031.localAngle: The event celebrates the deep-rooted ties between local Limerick GAA clubs and their diaspora community in New York.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363031.originalTitle: Honours for Limerick GAA persons in New York

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363051.headline: Limerick Minister Niall Collins Launches Report on Farm Safety Training Programme
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363051.summary: County Limerick TD and Minister of State Niall Collins has launched a new evaluation report on a Department-funded farm safety training programme aimed at connecting farmers with vital health services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363051.story:
County Limerick TD and Minister of State Niall Collins has launched an evaluation report on "On Feirm Ground 2" (OFG2), a farm safety training programme funded by the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine.

Delivered by the Men’s Development Network, the initiative is designed to equip farm advisors, private veterinary practitioners, farming organisations, and other agri-professionals with the skills needed to engage farmers and signpost them to health services.

Speaking at the launch, Minister Collins emphasised that mental wellbeing and physical safety on farms are closely linked. "Stress and exhaustion are farm safety issues. A farmer who is worn out is more at risk on the farm," he stated.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363051.localAngle: County Limerick TD Niall Collins launched the national farm safety report in his ministerial capacity.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363051.originalTitle: Farmer wellbeing and farm safety go hand in hand says Limerick Minister launching new report

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53752.headline: Limerick students face rising ticket and travel costs as cultural calendar fills
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53752.summary: With November events in Limerick ranging from theatre productions to Garth Brooks tickets costing over €130, students are finding live entertainment increasingly difficult to afford on a tight budget.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53752.story:
Limerick's packed cultural calendar for November has put the spotlight on whether the city's arts scene remains accessible for students. While venues across the city offer a wide selection of theatre, music, and comedy, students are weighing up the mounting costs of attendance against strict budgets.

The debate has intensified ahead of ticket sales for Garth Brooks' upcoming 2027 Irish tour, which includes two June concerts at the TUS Gaelic Grounds on the Ennis Road. Promoter Peter Aiken confirmed that tickets will cost €136.25 for standing and €156.25 for seated. For students, however, the ticket price is only the beginning of the expense. Transport to the venue via taxi can add between €21 and €31 each way, alongside costs for food and clothing, pushing total expenses up by at least €40 to €50.

Local student Leah noted that while expected ticket prices for major bands might sit around €50 or €60, smaller local acts should ideally cost between €15 and €20. Beyond major stadium gigs, theatrical and musical events across the city also present financial hurdles. Productions at the Lime Tree Theatre this November range from concession tickets at €23 for 'The Ferryman' and €28 for 'The Hunchback of Notre Dame', up to €32 for standard tickets to Ballet Ireland's 'Romeo and Juliet'.

Meanwhile, niche events such as the 'Faulty Towers Dining Experience' at Dolan's are priced at €60 a ticket, and Hans Zimmer’s music performed by the Glas String Quartet at Saint Mary’s Cathedral ranges from €26.50 to €54.50. For students living on limited incomes, these cumulative costs mean many cultural events are drifting out of reach.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53752.localAngle: The story examines the affordability of Limerick city's local venues, transport routes, and cultural events for student residents.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53752.originalTitle: Is Limerick’s art scene affordable for students?

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363163.headline: O’Connell Street youth organisation Narrative 4 marks 10th anniversary at Belltable
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363163.summary: Award-winning youth organisation Narrative 4 is celebrating a decade of creative projects in Limerick with a special anniversary event at the Belltable this Friday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363163.story:
Limerick youth organisation Narrative 4 is marking its 10th anniversary this Friday, November 13, with a celebratory evening of music, literature, and storytelling at the Belltable.

Located on O’Connell Street, the award-winning group has established itself over the past decade as a leader in creative projects, collaborating closely with local schools, youth groups, and international partners.

Friday's anniversary event, titled 'The Power of Stories', will showcase a decade of the organisation's youth programmes. Directed by musician and theatre practitioner Ann Blake, the line-up features a host of artists, authors, and youth leaders.

Dr Jennifer McMahon, Head of the Department of Psychology at the University of Limerick, will serve as Master of Ceremonies for the special evening commemorating the milestone.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363163.localAngle: The milestone event celebrates a decade of youth and creative work based out of Narrative 4's O'Connell Street hub in Limerick city.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363154.headline: Moyross Partners Group warns Limerick CCTV service faces closure over €660k funding
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363154.summary: The Moyross Partners Group has warned that public safety is at risk due to ongoing uncertainty surrounding the future of Limerick’s CCTV monitoring service. The group is demanding permanent government funding of approximately €660,000 for 2027 to prevent hundreds of cameras from going unmonitored.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363154.story:
The Moyross Partners Group has issued a stark warning that public safety across Limerick is being put at risk due to a lack of a commitment to fund the local CCTV monitoring service. In a statement released to the media, the group expressed deep concern and frustration over the continued uncertainty facing the essential public safety resource.

The group highlighted that the city has endured years of serious violence, criminality, intimidation, and public disorder, with the CCTV system having originally been established as a key response following the Fitzgerald Report and the subsequent regeneration initiatives. The monitoring service actively supports An Garda Síochána by assisting investigations, deterring criminal activity, and reassuring local communities.

With a funding requirement of approximately €660,000 needed for 2027, the group warned that failure to secure this money would leave hundreds of cameras without active monitoring and deprive Gardaí of a vital investigative tool. The community representatives also questioned the message being sent as Limerick prepares to welcome thousands of additional visitors for the Ryder Cup in 2027 while simultaneously leaving public safety infrastructure at risk.

The Moyross Partners Group is now calling on every TD, Senator, and elected representative in Limerick to bring the matter directly to Government and demand an immediate, permanent funding decision. The group emphasised that public safety must be non-negotiable and that established services protecting communities across the city must be protected rather than subjected to repeated threats of collapse.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363154.localAngle: The story directly concerns the funding and operation of the public CCTV monitoring service across Limerick city communities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363154.originalTitle: Community says public safety being put at risk

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363104.headline: MARY Immaculate Dramatic Arts Society brings Clue to Belltable stage
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363104.summary: MIDAS will stage its production of the fan-favourite play Clue at the Belltable for the first time on November 18 and 19. Tickets are priced at €17.50 for general admission and €12.50 for students.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363104.story:
The Mary Immaculate Dramatic Arts Society (MIDAS) is preparing for a landmark production, bringing its showstopping play Clue to the Belltable stage for the very first time. Performances will take place at 8pm on Wednesday, November 18, and Thursday, November 19.

Traditionally staging their plays in the campus Halla or smaller performance spaces, the society secured the professional city-centre theatre following the election of chairperson Ciara Reidy. Reidy noted that the move aims to reach a wider audience and provide students with valuable professional theatre experience both on and off the stage.

The production blends comedy and suspense in a classic murder mystery set on a dark and stormy night, where guests arrive for an unusual dinner party and the host is found already dead. MIDAS boasts a strong track record of sold-out shows and society awards.

Tickets cost €17.50, with student tickets available at €12.50, and can be purchased now through limetreebelltable.ie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363104.localAngle: The Mary Immaculate College student society is expanding its reach by moving its annual production from campus to the city-centre Belltable theatre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363104.originalTitle: MIDAS to bring Clue to Belltable stage for first time

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363156.headline: Limerick Councillors Condemn 'Vile' Online Abuse Aimed at Unwell Minister Patrick O'Donovan
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363156.summary: Fianna Fáil councillor Michael Collins has slammed online trolls for targeting Limerick TD Patrick O'Donovan while he receives hospital treatment for deep frontal lobe epilepsy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363156.story:
Limerick councillors have rallied around Minister Patrick O'Donovan after the Fine Gael politician faced a wave of abusive online comments following his recent hospitalisation. The 49-year-old TD was re-admitted to University Hospital Limerick last weekend after suffering further complications from deep frontal lobe epilepsy, a condition that has caused him to collapse during political duties.

Speaking at last Wednesday's Newcastle West Municipal District meeting, Fianna Fáil councillor Michael Collins called for a letter of support to be sent to the Minister for Culture. He also strongly condemned the reaction from social media users following the Minister's initial medical emergency on October 13, when he fell ill while hosting EU Telecommunications Ministers at the University of Limerick.

"I also want to comment on some of the vile messages and comments I’ve seen online towards Patrick. It’s not fair. It’s not warranted, and I think people should be ashamed of themselves to make comments like that to a person that’s sick," Cllr Collins told the meeting. He added that the Fine Gael politician has done "trojan work" for the country and is currently recovering in the hospital's high dependency unit after being rushed there for the second time in less than a month.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363156.localAngle: The story centers on Limerick TD and Minister Patrick O'Donovan receiving treatment at University Hospital Limerick and local reaction from the Newcastle West Municipal District.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363156.originalTitle: Councillors rally round to support unwell Limerick Minister after ‘vile’ social media onslaught

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363089.headline: Hit Comedy Drama 'Happiness Then' Comes to Belltable Theatre
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363089.summary: Bewley’s Cafe Theatre will stage Elizabeth Moynihan's acclaimed production at the Belltable on Saturday, November 21. The 8pm show stars Rachael Dowling and Sorcha Furlong as two estranged sisters.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363089.story:
Theatregoers in Limerick will have the chance to see the hit comedy drama 'Happiness Then' when it arrives at the Belltable on Saturday, November 21. Written by Elizabeth Moynihan, the production explores the fallout of a mother's death and the complex relationship between two estranged sisters.

Starring Rachael Dowling and Sorcha Furlong under the direction of Liam Halligan, the play follows Bridget and Frances as they meet for the first time following their mother's passing. The siblings bicker over everything from the wine to the will, examining past loves and losses with acerbic wit and put-downs while questioning if they can mend their broken relationships.

The production has received strong critical praise, with Emer O’Kelly of the Sunday Independent describing it as "sharp and very sophisticated" and full of acuity. The Arts Review also lauded the two "riveting performances" in the genuinely heartfelt show.

The performance begins at 8pm. Tickets are priced at €22, with concessions available at €18.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363089.localAngle: The acclaimed Bewley’s Cafe Theatre production is coming to the Belltable venue in Limerick for one night only.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363089.originalTitle: Happiness Then: Sisters clash over wine and will in comic drama

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363158.headline: Limerick Council Critics Question Efficiency Under Executive Mayor
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363158.summary: Concerns have been raised over local governance in Limerick, with critics pointing to ongoing disputes, bureaucracy, and frequent public communications from the executive mayor's office.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363158.story:
Local democracy in Limerick has come under scrutiny over concerns that increased bureaucracy and advisors are hindering local progress. Critics argue that despite the introduction of Ireland's first executive mayor and various consulting teams, local governance remains bogged down by familiar rows and administrative hurdles.

Observers point to ongoing debates surrounding key local issues, including road closures, modular housing projects, and administrative proposals. Concerns have been raised that the volume of press releases and public communications from the mayor's office has created tension among councillors, business owners, and residents alike, potentially drawing focus away from day-to-day local administration.

Additionally, the emergence of various faction groups ahead of council votes has been cited as a contributing factor to local political friction. Commentators suggest that despite changes in the structure of local government, the system continues to face challenges similar to those seen under previous administrations.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363158.localAngle: The report examines the state of local government administration and political dynamics within Limerick City and County Council.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363158.originalTitle: Council Affairs – Back to the future

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363086.headline: The Frank & Walters play Dolans to mark 30 years of Grand Parade
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363086.summary: Indie favourites The Frank & Walters perform at Dolans this Saturday, November 14, celebrating three decades of their landmark album Grand Parade.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363086.story:
Indie favourites The Frank & Walters will take to the stage at Dolans this Saturday, November 14, as part of a national tour celebrating 30 years of their landmark album Grand Parade. 

The 1990s record features enduring fan favourites such as 'Colours', 'Indian Ocean', 'How Can I Exist?', and 'Tony Cochrane'. It followed the band's breakthrough debut, Trains, Boats and Planes, which famously entered the UK charts with tracks like 'After All' and led to an appearance on Top of the Pops in January 1993.

The band remains an active fixture on UK and European stages, enjoying a renewed surge of popularity following the 2012 release of 'Indie Love Song' and the album Greenwich Mean Time. Their seventh studio release, Songs for the Walking Wounded, also featured a notable collaboration with Oscar-winning actor Cillian Murphy on the single 'Stages'.

To coincide with the anniversary tour, Grand Parade has been reissued in three limited-edition vinyl colours—Tangerine, Bluebell, and Apple Green—in partnership with record label Last Night From Glasgow. Saturday's gig at Dolans will be followed by an after-show party on the venue's terrace, featuring indie classics and a free cover charge.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363086.localAngle: The Cork indie veterans are bringing their 30th-anniversary album tour to Limerick live music venue Dolans this weekend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363086.originalTitle: The Frank & Walters celebrate 30 years of Grand Parade in Dolans

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363033.headline: Limerick Celtics and Eagles Secure Impressive National Cup Victories
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363033.summary: Limerick Celtics defeated Tralee Warriors 87-75 in the Men's National Cup, while reigning champions Limerick Eagles claimed an away win against Killester.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363033.story:
The Tony Hehir-coached Limerick Celtics kicked off their Men's National Cup campaign in style over the weekend with an 87-75 home victory against last year’s finalists, Tralee Warriors. Sebastian Cole starred in the final period with 13 points, maintaining a 100 per cent record across two-pointers, three-pointers, and free-throws. Meanwhile, debutant Tiras Morton contributed heavily with 18 points, 17 rebounds, and seven assists. 

Last season’s National Cup holders, Limerick Eagles, also started their title defence strongly by defeating six-time winners Killester in Clontarf. The Eagles established control early with a 26-point opening quarter, driven by Aaron Rhooms and Tobias Christensen, eventually securing a 12-point victory.

In the upcoming quarter-finals, Celtics are set to face Griffith College Éanna, while Eagles will take on the Sligo All-Stars. However, it was not entirely a clean sweep for the Celtics over the weekend, as the club's women's team suffered a narrow defeat to Super League pacesetters Cavan Eagles in the Women's National Cup.

Meanwhile, the local sporting calendar saw standout results in rugby as Shannon defeated previous leaders Cashel 41-35 at Thomond Park in the All-Ireland League, and UL Bohemian climbed out of the relegation zone with a 35-12 win away to Galwegians.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363033.localAngle: The report highlights weekend sporting achievements and fixtures involving Limerick-based basketball, rugby, and soccer clubs.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363033.originalTitle: SPORT ROUND-UP: Basketball Cup wins for Limerick, Shannon stand out in AIL, Junior Cup takes centre stage, and much more

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363152.headline: Tipperary Man Pleads Not Guilty to Attempted Murder in Petrol Attack Trial
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363152.summary: Chad Allan has pleaded not guilty at the Central Criminal Court in Limerick to the attempted murder of Patrick Williams, who was allegedly doused in petrol and set alight in County Tipperary last year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363152.story:
A mid-West man went on trial in Limerick this Wednesday afternoon accused of the attempted murder of another man who was allegedly doused in petrol and set alight. Chad Allan, 28, of Cahir, County Tipperary, pleaded not guilty before the Central Criminal Court, sitting at the Limerick courthouse, to the attempted murder of Patrick Williams in his 40s at Knockane, Ballylooby, Cahir, on October 11, 2025.

Appearing before a jury of six men and six women sworn in on Wednesday, Mr Allan also denied charges of assaulting Mr Williams causing him serious harm, and committing arson on a car belonging to John Coffey at the same location and date. He further denied the alleged theft of fuel and items from a filling station in Cahir on the same date.

Senior prosecution counsel Eoghan Cole told the jury in his opening address that the State's case is that Mr Allan acted jointly with a man named Luke Caplice in an attempt to murder Mr Williams. The prosecution alleges that an altercation occurred after a grey jeep driven by Mr Caplice collided with a red Audi, and that Mr Williams was subsequently doused in petrol and set on fire.

Presided over by Ms Justice Melanie Greally, the trial is expected to hear evidence from the injured party, Patrick Williams, along with CCTV footage of the alleged attack. Evidence in the trial is due to begin on Thursday morning.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363152.localAngle: The Central Criminal Court trial is sitting in Limerick, bringing a high-profile criminal case from the wider Mid-West region before a Limerick-sworn jury.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363152.originalTitle: Man pleads not guilty to attempted murder of man doused in petrol and set alight

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363136.headline: Limerick students don Christmas jumpers early for annual festive celebrations
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363136.summary: Students across Limerick City hit the streets early Wednesday morning in festive attire for the annual Student Christmas Day celebrations, taking a break ahead of upcoming exams.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363136.story:
Students in Limerick City embraced the festive season early this week, turning out in full holiday attire for the annual Student Christmas Day celebrations on Wednesday.

Participants dusted off their festive knitwear for the traditional yuletide event, which provides students with a chance to celebrate together from early morning before the heavy focus shifts to upcoming exams.

Photographer Brendan Gleeson captured local students enjoying the atmosphere across the city, with large groups gathering in Christmas jumpers to mark the occasion.

Among those spotted out and about enjoying the festivities were Anna Gohery, Abbie Daunt, Emma Higgins, Roisin O'Donoghue, Abba Marclaw, Isabelle Philips, Iosa Smith, Nevaeh Griffin, Keelin Burke, Sean McContoguec, Diarmuid Savage, John Culhane, Ella Murphy, Emily O'Brien, Leah Maher, Maria Murphy, Mya Hickey, Doireann Ryan, Nicole O'Rahilly, Mary Gregory, and Laura Brennan.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363136.localAngle: The annual student tradition brings festive celebrations and heavy footfall to the streets of Limerick City ahead of the academic exam season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363136.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Christmas craic for Limerick students

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363254.headline: Accused Murderer Denies Attacking Scarlett Faulkner in Central Criminal Court Trial
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363254.summary: A 41-year-old woman on trial for the murder of young mother Scarlett Faulkner denied laying a hand on her during a recorded phone call played in court. The accused has pleaded not guilty to murder and several other charges.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363254.story:
A 41-year-old woman accused of murdering young mother Scarlett Faulkner denied any physical involvement in the attack, telling a friend in a recorded phone call played at the Central Criminal Court: “I didn’t put a finger on her… I’d kill no woman over a man.”

The trial heard recordings of the phone call from March 22, in which the accused swore on her children's lives that she never attacked Ms Faulkner. Ms Faulkner subsequently passed away at Cork University Hospital on April 13 after being removed from life support. The accused has pleaded not guilty to murder, alongside separate charges of burglary, entering a building as a trespasser, and causing criminal damage in Tipperary on March 20, as well as robbery and assault causing harm in Limerick on March 21. A 17-year-old girl has also pleaded not guilty to murder but has entered a guilty plea to manslaughter.

During Thursday's proceedings, Garda Sergeant Jennifer Skelly continued presenting preliminary device reports from mobile phones belonging to the accused and others. The court heard text message exchanges and Facebook messages detailing domestic friction, alleged infidelity, and disputes regarding a vehicle between the older accused and her former partner in the days leading up to the fatal incident. Defence questioning noted that the relationship involved allegations of stolen money and drug use.

The court was also told that 267 calls were recorded on the older accused’s phone on the day of the fatal attack in Birdhill.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363254.localAngle: The case involves charges stemming from an alleged incident in Limerick on March 21, with mobile phone evidence and proceedings drawing attention across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363254.originalTitle: Murder accused in Scarlett Faulkner trial tells friend: ‘I’d kill no woman over a man’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363160.headline: Limerick Council Security Claims Surge 418 Per Cent Amid Abuse Concerns
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363160.summary: Figures show Limerick City and County Council security allowance claims jumped to €36,422 this year. Meanwhile, local representatives report facing sustained harassment and stalking.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363160.story:
Security allowance claims by Limerick local representatives have surged by 418 per cent so far this year, according to figures released by Limerick City and County Council. Local elected officials have claimed a total of €36,422 in 2026, compared to €7,026 for the entirety of 2025, €3,902 in 2024, and €1,476 in 2023. 

Citing safety concerns for elected representatives, the Council declined to provide specific details on who claimed the allowance, how many representatives availed of it, or what the funds were spent on. While nine out of Limerick's 41 local representatives confirmed they had not claimed the allowance when asked, this does not reflect security measures already in place.

Social Democrats Councillor Elisa O'Donovan revealed she is entirely self-funding her personal security after experiencing sustained harassment and stalking since her election in 2019. Cllr O'Donovan stated she does not feel comfortable using public funding for her security measures out of concern that it could be used against her publicly or online.

The Department of Local Government described the rise in abuse and threats against politicians as disturbing, warning that it extends beyond online harassment to physical threats and violence. The security allowance scheme permits councillors to improve home physical security after a review by a Garda Crime Prevention Officer, with a maximum lifetime allowance of €10,000 available under a revised scheme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363160.localAngle: The figures highlight a sharp increase in security spending and personal abuse concerns among local representatives serving on Limerick City and County Council.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363160.originalTitle: 418 per cent hike in security costs for Limerick councillors amid ‘disturbing’ increase in abuse against politicians

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363250.headline: UCH aims to give free panto tickets to 1,500 Limerick children
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363250.summary: University Concert Hall is calling on local businesses and the public to help its award-winning campaign provide free panto tickets to 1,500 children and families this Christmas. The initiative will see every donation matched by UCH and Specsavers Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363250.story:
University Concert Hall (UCH) has launched an appeal to bring its Christmas panto to 1,500 children and families across Limerick by the end of the festive season. The venue's 'Panto For All' campaign is inviting local charities and community groups to apply for free tickets to this year's production of 'Jack & the Beanstalk', which runs from 14th December 2026 to 10th January 2027.

Since the initiative started in 2024, more than 930 children and families have attended the UCH panto free of charge. Organisers hope to push that total to 1,500 this year, backed by recent national recognition after winning the Creative Access Award at the Business to Arts Awards 2026.

“Panto is such a special Christmas tradition and we want as many children and families as possible to have the chance to experience it,” said Sinéad Hope, Director of University Concert Hall. To help reach the target, UCH and panto sponsor Specsavers Limerick have pledged to match every public and business donation received, doubling the impact of each contribution.

Charities and community organisations supporting families who might otherwise miss out can now apply for tickets at uch.ie/donate. Members of the public can also donate through the website, while local businesses can get involved by contacting UCH directly.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363250.localAngle: The campaign provides free University Concert Hall panto tickets to children and families across Limerick who might otherwise be unable to attend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363250.originalTitle: UCH aims to spread its panto magic to 1,500 children and families by this Christmas

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363178.headline: Munster Rugby Utilises 39 Players Across Opening Six Matches of Season
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363178.summary: Munster Rugby has deployed 39 players, handed out six debuts, and seen 12 academy appearances during the opening five rounds of the URC and their sole Champions Cup tie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363178.story:
Munster Rugby has released statistics detailing squad usage across the opening block of the season, showing 39 players featuring for the club in the first five rounds of the United Rugby Championship (URC) along with their sole Champions Cup fixture.

Six players have made their debuts for the province so far: Jack Aungier, Kieran Brookes, Marnus van der Merwe, Michael Foy, Charlie O’Shea, and Rob Russell. In total, academy players have racked up 12 appearances, with Charlie O’Shea remaining ever-present alongside Gavin Coombes, Brian Gleeson, and JJ Hanrahan across all six games. Other academy and senior players to feature include Foy, Jake O’Riordan, Gordon Wood, and all five summer-promoted academy members Ben O’Donovan, Seán Edogbo, Ronan Foxe, Ben O’Conner, and Max Clein.

On-field leadership has been shared by captain Tadhg Beirne, Diarmuid Barron, Craig Casey, and Jack O’Donoghue. Player of the Match accolades have gone to Ben O’Donovan, O’Shea, van der Merwe, and Casey. Meanwhile, in the All-Ireland League (AIL), senior and academy players have recorded over 60 club appearances, with local representatives Oisín Minogue of Young Munster and Joe Finn of Garryowen featuring in every game for their respective clubs. Munster will return to URC action away to Zebre on December 5.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363178.localAngle: Local Limerick club players from Young Munster and Garryowen have featured prominently in the AIL alongside their Munster commitments.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363178.originalTitle: Plenty of players involved with Munster

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363196.headline: County Limerick Serial Sex Offender Faces More Jail Time After Third Victim Comes Forward
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363196.summary: Christopher O'Mahony, already serving a nine-year sentence for abusing his daughter and sister-in-law, has pleaded guilty to indecently assaulting a third victim in the 1970s after she read about his previous crimes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363196.story:
A 68-year-old County Limerick man already serving a nine-year prison sentence for sex crimes against family members is facing additional jail time after pleading guilty to abusing a third victim decades ago. Christopher O’Mahony, of Kerrykyle, Ardagh, admitted to two counts of indecently assaulting the victim during the 1970s when she was a young girl.

Limerick Circuit Criminal Court heard that the victim came forward after reading media reports last year regarding O’Mahony's previous convictions for abusing his daughter, Emma O’Shaughnessy, and sister-in-law, Helen Costelloe. The victim, who was between five and 12 years old at the time of the offenses, asked the court for her identity to be unmasked.

Prosecuting barrister Lily Buckley detailed how O’Mahony first targeted the victim while she was sleeping as a young child, forcing her to touch him and attempting to remove her pyjamas before she managed to escape. In a later incident when the victim was 11 or 12, O’Mahony made inappropriate remarks and grabbed her breast. Detective Garda James Muldowney brought the fresh allegations to O'Mahony at Midlands Prison, where he eventually entered guilty pleas.

The court heard that the victim suffered serious mental health difficulties as a direct result of the abuse. The sentencing hearing is ongoing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363196.localAngle: The case was heard at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court, involving a defendant from Ardagh, County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363196.originalTitle: ‘Monster’ paedophile facing more jail time after third victim comes forward

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363083.headline: Punk-folk duo Wasps vs Humans to launch new album at The Record Room
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363083.summary: Punk-folk duo Wasps vs Humans will celebrate the release of their new album with a Limerick gig at The Record Room on Friday, November 20. They will be joined by special guests Japanese Jesus, with tickets priced at €15.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363083.story:
Punk-folk duo Wasps vs Humans are bringing their new album launch tour to Limerick this month, performing live at The Record Room in The Commercial on Friday, November 20. The band will celebrate the release of their latest record, 'The Day Homo Sapiens Destroyed the Earth', with support from special guests Japanese Jesus. Tickets for the show are priced at €15 and are available through Eventbrite.

The new album has already garnered strong critical acclaim, earning a four-star review from The Irish Times critic Tony Clayton-Lea, who likened their abrasive sound to a spiky hybrid of The Ruts, The Clash, Patti Smith, and Siouxsie Sioux. Recorded across Dublin and Cork, the release is the culmination of two years of intensive gigging. It captures the raw energy of the band's live shows through a harder, grittier yet melodic sound that blends heavy guitar riffs, electronic beats, harmonies, folk instruments, and punk poetry.

Formed by punk poet and drummer Carl Antony Plover—who began the project as a solo endeavor before teaming up with musician and wife Linda Plover in 2024—the band tackles themes including inner-city crime, disappointment, social decay, and a fame-obsessed culture. The Limerick gig also marks the celebration of the group's first-ever vinyl pressing, produced in partnership with Anthem Vinyl. Special guests Japanese Jesus, featuring Bertie and Denny, will open the night with their alternative punk sound.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363083.localAngle: The album launch tour stops at The Record Room in The Commercial on Friday, November 20.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363083.originalTitle: Wasps vs Humans to launch new album with Limerick gig

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363188.headline: Dr Joachim Fischer to deliver talk on Shannon Scheme in Rathkeale
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363188.summary: The Rathkeale Historical Society is hosting a free public lecture tonight at the Rathkeale House Hotel exploring the Shannon Scheme from a German perspective.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363188.story:
History enthusiasts in West Limerick have the opportunity to delve into the county's industrial past this evening (Friday, November 13) as the Rathkeale Historical Society hosts its latest meeting.

Dr Joachim Fischer, a member of the German Department at the University of Limerick, will deliver a keynote presentation titled 'The Shannon Scheme from a German perspective'. The talk examines the monumental hydroelectric engineering project through a distinct international lens.

Proceedings get underway at 7.30pm at the Rathkeale House Hotel. While attendance at tonight's lecture is completely free of charge, annual society membership is available for €15.

Organisers are also looking ahead to their next gathering on January 29 and are seeking local speakers. Anyone interested in delivering a 15-minute talk on an aspect of local history is asked to contact 083 024 6203 to secure one of the two remaining slots.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363188.localAngle: The event explores the local history of the Shannon Scheme, a major engineering project deeply tied to the heritage of County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363188.originalTitle: Free historical talk in Rathkeale this evening

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363264.headline: HSE scraps 100 step-down beds for UHL due to funding shortages
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363264.summary: A HSE tender for 100 step-down beds to ease overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick has been cancelled due to a lack of funding, leaving dozens of local beds sitting idle.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363264.story:
Plans to secure 100 step-down and rehabilitation beds to ease chronic overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick (UHL) have been abandoned because of funding constraints. A HSE tender for the beds, advertised last March, was withdrawn without explanation.

Meanwhile, a state-of-the-art €20 million facility operated by Bartra Healthcare in Raheen Lodge, Mungret, sits just 1.8km from UHL with 60 beds continuing to lay idle. Bartra said it attempted to secure a contract to provide up to 80 step-down beds and would have supplied its own ambulance patient transfers to keep pressure off the National Ambulance Service.

In response to a parliamentary question from Limerick Sinn Féin TD Maurice Quinlivan, HSE Mid West Acute and Older People Services CEO Ian Carter confirmed the procurement process was withdrawn due to "the absence of an available funding allocation." He noted that the clinical need for the beds remains high as emergency department overcrowding persists.

Deputy Quinlivan slammed the decision as an illustration of "decades of underfunding in the Mid West health service." Figures show that in the first eight months of this year, an average of 38 acute beds across the region—including 28 at UHL—were occupied daily by patients medically cleared for discharge but unable to leave due to a lack of step-down capacity.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363264.localAngle: The cancelled bed provision directly impacts patients and emergency department overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363264.originalTitle: Plan for step-down beds to ease capacity crisis at UHL abandoned due to funding constraints

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363260.headline: Moyross Family Launches GoFundMe to Bring Murder Victim Carrie Mullane-Noonan Home to Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363260.summary: A fundraising campaign has raised over €8,600 to help bring Carrie Mullane-Noonan home to Moyross for burial after her body was recovered in County Fermanagh.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363260.story:
A fundraising campaign has been launched to cover the funeral expenses of Carrie Mullane-Noonan, a mother of four from Moyross whose body was recovered from a lake in County Fermanagh this week. Ms Mullane-Noonan had been missing since travelling to Enniskillen on October 10.

Family friend Sarah Power established the 'Remembering Carrie' GoFundMe page on behalf of the Mullane and Noonan family. As of Friday morning, the campaign has raised €8,650 toward its €16,000 target. Ms Power paid tribute to Ms Mullane-Noonan as a "cherished mother, daughter, sister, and friend" who was "completely harmless, with not a bad bone in her body." She added that any leftover funds will be donated to Woman’s Aid Ireland in memory of Carrie.

Three people have been arrested and brought before the courts in Fermanagh in connection with the Limerick woman’s death. Michael Lynch, 35, of Trasna Park, Enniskillen, has been charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a corpse. His mother, Mary Lynch, 69, of Windmill Heights, Enniskillen, appeared in court in relation to withholding information. A third individual, a 31-year-old man, has been charged with withholding information concerning an arrestable offence and encouraging or assisting in the commission of murder.

Donations to support the family in bringing Ms Mullane-Noonan home to Pineview Gardens for burial can be made via the GoFundMe platform.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363260.localAngle: The victim is a native of Pineview Gardens in Moyross, and her family are working to bring her home to Limerick for her final burial.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363260.originalTitle: Fundraiser to bring tragic mother of four home for burial

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363101.headline: Cork power ballad band Fist of Pure Emotion to play Limerick debut
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363101.summary: Cork 10-piece band Fist of Pure Emotion will bring their decade-long anniversary tour to Dolan’s Warehouse on Saturday, November 28, marking their first-ever Limerick performance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363101.story:
Cork power ballad band Fist of Pure Emotion (FOPE) is bringing its self-proclaimed “Teeny Tiny Tour” to Dolan’s Warehouse on Saturday, November 28, marking the 10-piece band's debut performance in Limerick.

The group, co-founded by lead singer Muireann Holly and guitarist John Boyle, promises a set filled with 1980s and 1990s rock anthems, power ballads, and guilty pleasures. The performance will feature tracks from artists like Meat Loaf, Bon Jovi, Starship, and Bonnie Tyler, alongside what the band describes as “more Celine Dion than should be legal,” as well as forgotten gems and one-hit wonders.

Founded as a passion project for professional musicians wanting to play their favorite tracks, FOPE has grown from its first show at the Cork Arts Theatre in 2016 to sell-out runs at Cyprus Avenue. Billed by fans as “cheaper than therapy and twice as effective,” the band encourages audiences to sing along.

“What began as a celebration of beloved rock anthems has now become a must-see, sell-out event,” said co-founder Muireann Holly, adding that the band looks forward to bringing the show to the Treaty City. The group urged concertgoers to leave their troubles and cynicism at the door for the Limerick debut.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363101.localAngle: The Cork-based band is performing its first-ever concert in Limerick at Dolan's Warehouse on November 28.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363101.originalTitle: Fist of Pure Emotion to make Limerick debut at Dolan’s Warehouse

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53785.headline: Limerick's Des Galligan Reflects on Five Decades as Ireland's First Grandmaster
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53785.summary: Ninth-degree black belt Des Galligan has spent nearly 50 years in martial arts, using the discipline to drive youth work across Limerick and connect with martial arts icons internationally.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53785.story:
For nearly five decades, Limerick native Des Galligan has used martial arts not just for physical training, but as a tool to help others find confidence and direction. Now 63, the ninth-degree black belt and Ireland's first grandmaster began his journey around 1977 after being inspired by Bruce Lee films. After navigating age restrictions to find training as a teenager, he trained in judo, karate, kickboxing, and taekwondo before dedicating much of his life to community work.

Galligan’s passion for youth development led him to collaborate in the mid-1990s with two nuns to establish a youth club in Southill, which combined martial arts with homework support and meals. He also spent six years volunteering on school completion programmes with former Limerick City Councillor Orla McLoughlin. These community experiences inspired him to return to education in his mid-40s, culminating in a social care degree at age 50 and subsequent work in youth justice, probation services, and currently as a student support worker at Crescent College Comprehensive.

His international profile in the sport eventually led him to the United States to visit Chuck Norris’s Kickstart Kids organisation, where he met Norris himself—an encounter that left him deeply emotional. Reflecting on his lifetime in the sport, Galligan emphasised that the true value of martial arts lies in personal growth rather than competition. “The best legacy you can leave is just leave people with a better impression of themselves and a stronger characteristic of themselves,” he said.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53785.localAngle: Limerick native Des Galligan reflects on a 50-year martial arts career rooted in local youth work across Southill and Crescent College Comprehensive.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53785.originalTitle: ‘I still feel so privileged,’ shares Ireland’s first grandmaster on a lifetime in martial arts

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363258.headline: Microsoft Global IT Outage Disrupts Limerick City and County Council Services
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363258.summary: Limerick City and County Council's digital operations have been hit by the widespread Microsoft outage affecting millions globally. Customers are being warned of potential delays in email responses and enquiry processing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363258.story:
Limerick City and County Council has confirmed that some of its key IT systems are experiencing disruptions due to the ongoing global Microsoft service outage. The local authority is among millions of individual users and organisations worldwide impacted by the technical failure, which has disrupted major Microsoft programmes including Teams, Outlook, and Copilot AI software. Microsoft has stated that it is not aware of any malicious activity behind the incident.

A statement issued by the Council advised customers, service users, and stakeholders that day-to-day operations and communications are currently affected. Because the local authority relies on Microsoft services for daily functions, the disruption may lead to delays in receiving, processing, and responding to emails and other enquiries from the public.

The local authority stated that it is actively monitoring updates from Microsoft and working to minimise the impact while systems remain affected. The Council apologised for any inconvenience caused and thanked the public for their patience, adding that further updates will be provided as it aims to return to normal service as soon as possible.

Despite the IT issues affecting digital communications, the local authority's customer services department remains operational and can still be reached directly by phone at 061 556 000.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363258.localAngle: Limerick City and County Council's day-to-day operations and public communications have been impacted by the global tech failure.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363258.originalTitle: Microsoft outage causing disruptions for Limerick Council

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363078.headline: Japanese Rock Trio Electric Eel Shock to Play Dolans This Wednesday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363078.summary: Tokyo power trio Electric Eel Shock will bring their global tour to Dolans Kasbah Social Club on Wednesday, November 18. The band is known for a high-energy sound that blends stoner rock, punk, and metal.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363078.story:
Japanese rock band Electric Eel Shock are bringing their ongoing world tour to Limerick this week, performing at Dolans Kasbah Social Club on Wednesday, November 18.

The Tokyo trio left Japan in 1999 to try their hand in America and have remained on a near-constant world tour ever since, funding their travels by selling merchandise and self-recorded albums.

Known for a sound that mixes dark, fuzzy stoner rock riffs with classic rock and punk, the band harks back to an era before rock music fractured into multiple sub-genres. EES has built a reputation for high-energy live performances that bridge the gap between punk and metal.

Having worked hard to sustain their journey, the band members are inviting both old and new fans in Limerick to join the party for this Wednesday's gig.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363078.localAngle: The international rock trio are performing a live gig at Dolans Kasbah Social Club on the Dock Road.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363078.originalTitle: Japanese rock trio Electric Eel Shock bring world tour to Dolans

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363185.headline: Abbeyfeale middle-income housing plan approved despite councillor opposition
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363185.summary: Limerick City and County Council has approved Mayor John Moran's plan to provide six rental homes for middle-income earners in Abbeyfeale, despite strong opposition from Fine Gael councillor Dan McSweeney.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363185.story:
Plans by Limerick Mayor John Moran to provide six rental homes for middle-income households in Abbeyfeale have been approved following a special meeting of the local authority in Dooradoyle. The scheme involves the disposal of properties at Convent Road, 6 and 7 Colbert Terrace, 8 Old Church Street, and units 1 and 2 at the Bridge Inn, which have been transferred to Limerick Twenty Thirty.

The initiative forms part of Mayor Moran's targeted approach to establish a cost-recovery rental model in West Limerick. Aimed at individuals who do not qualify for social housing but have a demonstrated need in the area, the project is designed to gradually build a revolving housing fund to support future acquisitions, refurbishments, and regeneration schemes.

The proposal faced opposition from Fine Gael councillor Dan McSweeney, who argued the project was not viable and questioned the council's overall housing output. Citing figures for the first two quarters of 2026, Cllr McSweeney stated the local authority had delivered just five units against a target of 562, suggesting the properties should instead be used for social housing or cost rental.

Defending the initiative, Mayor Moran acknowledged differing viewpoints on solving the housing crisis but emphasized the need to explore new solutions. While Cllr McSweeney maintained his preference for policies promoting home ownership over the private rental market, the council ultimately pushed the housing plan over the line.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363185.localAngle: The decision directly impacts local housing provision and municipal strategy in Abbeyfeale and the wider West Limerick area.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363185.originalTitle: Reservations over Limerick Mayor’s innovative plans for housing in Abbeyfeale

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363030.headline: Kilmallock face daunting Munster semi-final test against holders Ballygunner
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363030.summary: Limerick champions Kilmallock travel to Walsh Park on Sunday to face reigning All-Ireland champions Ballygunner in the Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship semi-final. James Hickey's side enter the clash as clear underdogs against a formidable Waterford outfit.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363030.story:
Limerick kingpins Kilmallock face a daunting task this Sunday as they travel to Walsh Park to take on reigning All-Ireland and provincial champions Ballygunner in the semi-final of the Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship. The 1.15pm fixture, refereed by Clare's Niall Malone, pits the John Daly Cup holders against a formidable Waterford side that has claimed four of the last six provincial titles.

Ballygunner boast a formidable lineup featuring Stephen O’Keeffe, Philip Mahony, Dessie Hutchinson, and Pauric Mahony, and carry a 13-game unbeaten home championship run into the weekend. Bookmakers have installed the Waterford club as 3/10 favourites, mindful of their dominant 3-20 to 1-12 victory over Kilmallock in the 2021 Munster Final and a seven-year streak of eliminating Limerick challengers.

Despite the odds, James Hickey's Kilmallock side arrive as proven competitors following their stunning victory over Na Piarsaigh to claim a 13th Limerick title. The Balbec will look to key figures such as captain Graeme Mulcahy, Robbie Egan, Micheál Houlihan, and newly-minted All-Star Shane O’Brien to produce a historic performance, though Aaron Costello remains an injury concern ahead of the throw-in.

In other provincial action, Inagh-Kilnamona meet Thurles Sarsfields in the day's other semi-final, with the final scheduled for November 29. Meanwhile, local championship action sees Dromin/Athlacca host Clarecastle in the Intermediate grade at Fitzgerald Park, and Caherline welcome Kerry's Dr Croke’s in the Junior Championship on Saturday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363030.localAngle: Limerick champions Kilmallock carry the county's hopes into the Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship semi-final against Ballygunner.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363030.originalTitle: Kilmallock face daunting test in Munster SHC

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363096.headline: Internationally Acclaimed Violinist Anton Jablokov to Perform at Belltable
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363096.summary: Internationally acclaimed violinist Anton Jablokov will bring his 'Heart & Fire' tour to the Belltable on Friday, November 20, accompanied by pianist and composer Adam I. Kuruc.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363096.story:
Music fans across Limerick can look forward to a unique cross-cultural performance when violinist Anton Jablokov takes to the stage at the Belltable on Friday, November 20. Known for blending classical virtuosity with traditional music and Romani-inspired improvisation, Jablokov will present his 'Heart & Fire' show alongside acclaimed pianist, composer, and arranger Adam I. Kuruc.

Kuruc brings extensive international experience to the collaboration, having previously worked with the Los Angeles Philharmonic under Gustavo Dudamel, the BBC Concert Orchestra, and contributed to Rodrigo y Gabriela’s Grammy Award-winning album. Jablokov’s own career has seen him perform on major international stages, including the BBC Proms, the London Palladium, Dublin’s 3Arena, and the Tipos Arena in Bratislava.

The upcoming Limerick programme promises a diverse musical journey spanning borders and traditions. Highlights will range from the haunting melodies of traditional Irish ballads like 'Danny Boy' to the warmth of the Mediterranean with 'Bella Ciao', Monti’s 'Csardas', and the Romani classic 'Dark Eyes'. Tickets for the Belltable performance are available now.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363096.localAngle: The internationally acclaimed concert brings high-profile global musicians to Limerick's Belltable venue for a one-night-only performance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363096.originalTitle: Violinist Anton Jablokov brings Heart & Fire to Belltable

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363187.headline: Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention Urgently Seeks New Base Ahead of Cleeve's Eviction
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363187.summary: Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention needs a new home by January as redevelopment at the former Cleeve's site forces the volunteers to vacate their current base. The group, which patrols city bridges four nights a week, is appealing for a private space to conduct interventions, store equipment, and debrief.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363187.story:
Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention (LTSP) is urgently appealing for a new base of operations after being told they must vacate their current room at the former Cleeve's site by January due to upcoming site redevelopment. 

For the past 11 years, the 50-strong volunteer group has averaged around 200 interventions a year patrolling the bridges of Limerick City. While they have used a room at the Cleeve's site rent-free courtesy of Limerick Twenty Thirty, the upcoming works mean the patrol is now facing a pressing search for a new facility within roughly 15 minutes of the river.

Matt Collins, president and founding member of the patrol, explained that a private space is critically needed to protect the dignity of individuals in distress. He noted that volunteers currently face challenges during interventions when members of the public stop to film and take pictures.

"The dream is to have somewhere that we can take a person in distress away from the river and from public view," Mr Collins said. The group also requires space to store equipment, allow volunteers to change out of the rain rather than using the boot of a car, and hold debriefings after patrols. LTSP has launched the 'Give Hope A Home' campaign and is asking anyone with a suitable room or plot of land for a container to contact Matt Collins directly or reach out via their Facebook page.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363187.localAngle: The LTSP provides crucial life-saving bridge patrols across Limerick City four nights a week.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363187.originalTitle: Limerick suicide prevention group urgently need new home

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363194.headline: MEP Michael McNamara Demands Clear Signage for Killaloe Farmers’ Market
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363194.summary: Ireland South MEP Michael McNamara is calling on Clare County Council to install clear signage for the Killaloe Farmers’ Market from the new Brian Boru Bridge, disputing claims that trader footfall has improved.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363194.story:
Ireland South MEP Michael McNamara has intervened in a local dispute over trader footfall at the Killaloe Farmers’ Market, demanding that Clare County Council erect clear directional signage from the newly opened Brian Boru Bridge.

The Independent MEP stated that his discussions with Sunday morning market traders contradicted the council's position that pedestrianisation of the former Killaloe–Ballina bridge had boosted visitor numbers.

"While on summer days, pedestrians on the old bridge might drop in to the market, on the other days, I am told business is down due to the lack of passing traffic," Mr McNamara said. 

The politician confirmed he will maintain pressure on Clare County Council to provide the necessary signage to direct visitors toward the market stalls from the new bridge infrastructure.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363194.localAngle: The story concerns a popular cross-border market destination frequently visited by people living in the Limerick and Clare region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363194.originalTitle: MEP calls for clear signage for Killaloe Farmers’ Market

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53792.headline: TUS students launch Rhythm Runway fashion and music show for Limerick Suicide Watch
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53792.summary: TUS music, fashion, and film students are collaborating on the Rhythm Runway event at the Millennium Theatre on November 18, with proceeds supporting Limerick Suicide Watch.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53792.story:
Students across multiple Technological University of the Shannon (TUS) campuses are joining forces next week for Rhythm Runway, a multidisciplinary showcase of fashion, music, and film. The event takes place on November 18 at the TUS Millennium Theatre, kicking off at 7pm.

The production brings together TUS Music Production students, LSAD final-year fashion students, and Creative Broadcast and Film Production crews. Organizers describe the showcase as the culmination of years of study, featuring modern pieces curated by a new generation of stylists alongside student-produced music and film.

Proceeds from ticket sales on Eventbrite will be donated directly to Limerick Suicide Watch, a volunteer group that patrols the riverside in Limerick City to assist individuals in distress. Following the main theatre event, an after-party featuring DJ sets from Wheel-up Wednesday will be held at Pharmacia at 9pm.

"It is the culmination of not only months of preparation but also years of study and practised skill," the organizing team stated. "We are all artists, and so it only makes sense that we should all work together, to support each other’s work, and create opportunities for said work to be displayed and enjoyed by the community."
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53792.localAngle: The student-led event raises funds for Limerick Suicide Watch, which actively patrols the city's riverside.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53792.originalTitle: TUS Campuses collide for a night of fashion and music in aid of Limerick Suicide Watch

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53795.headline: Treaty United’s Honor Mulvihill Earns First Republic of Ireland U16 Call-Up
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53795.summary: Fifteen-year-old Treaty United forward Honor Mulvihill has made her international debut for the Republic of Ireland Women's U16 squad, featuring in a 2-2 draw against Portugal.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53795.story:
Treaty United forward Honor Mulvihill has earned her first international call-up, featuring for the Republic of Ireland Women's U16 squad during their current international break in Portugal.

The 15-year-old came off the bench in the 78th minute during Ireland's opening fixture against Portugal on Wednesday, November 11, at the Estádio Municipal in Rio Maior, which ended in a 2-2 draw. Mulvihill is one of five first-time call-ups in the 20-player squad and forms part of a strong domestic contingent, with 19 players selected from the League of Ireland.

The international recognition caps a rapid rise for the former GB Rovers player, who recently made history by becoming Treaty United’s youngest-ever goalscorer after finding the net against Waterford in the Women’s Premier Division last month. Mulvihill has enjoyed a standout breakthrough season, featuring prominently at U17 level and with the senior side under manager Laurie Ryan.

The squad concludes its fixtures for 2026 with a second international friendly against Portugal.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53795.localAngle: Limerick soccer talent Honor Mulvihill has been recognised on the international stage following a record-breaking season with Treaty United.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53795.originalTitle: Treaty United’s youngest-ever goalscorer earns Ireland call-up

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363191.headline: 25th Limerick Scout Group marks 50th anniversary with Shannonbanks parade
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363191.summary: The 25th Limerick Scout Group is celebrating its 50th anniversary this weekend with a community parade, campcraft displays, and a historical talk. Former members, leaders, and families are invited to join the milestone celebrations in Shannonbanks on Saturday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363191.story:
The 25th Limerick Scout Group reaches a major milestone this weekend as it marks 50 years of scouting in the local area. Celebrations kick off on Saturday, November 14, with a public parade starting at 2pm from St Nicholas Church and making its way to the Scout Hall in Shannonbanks.

The anniversary procession will be led by the Limerick Pipe Band. Following the parade, the Shannonbanks hall will host a range of activities, including displays of campcraft, a magic show, a talk on the group's five-decade history, and games for attendees.

Organizers have opened the event to the wider community, inviting all former Beavers, Cubs, Scouts, Venturers, leaders, parents, and committee members to take part in the festivities. Refreshments, including a celebratory birthday cake, will be provided to mark the occasion.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363191.localAngle: The milestone event celebrates half a century of youth community engagement by the Shannonbanks-based 25th Limerick Scout Group.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363162.headline: Limerick schools invited to join free AI and climate change TY programme
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363162.summary: Secondary schools across Limerick can now apply for GreenFutures, a free Transition Year programme exploring the links between artificial intelligence, climate change, and sustainability.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363162.story:
Secondary schools across Limerick are being encouraged to apply for a new free artificial intelligence and climate change initiative aimed at Transition Year students.

The GreenFutures programme was developed by the Research Ireland ADAPT Centre in partnership with UNESCO and is supported by Huawei Ireland. It is designed to help students understand how AI and climate change are reshaping their world, while exploring the role technology could play in building a more sustainable future.

The initiative contributes to a wider European conversation about how science education can prepare young people for a future increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, climate change, and rapid technological transformation.

Limerick schools interested in participating in the programme can find more information and apply online through the ADAPT Centre website at adaptcentre.ie/projects/greenfutures/.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363162.localAngle: Secondary schools across Limerick are eligible to apply for the free educational programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363162.originalTitle: Schools encouraged to take part in free AI and climate change initiative

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53806.headline: Rathkeale's Barry Coleman named Limerick senior football captain for 2027
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53806.summary: Rathkeale clubman Barry Coleman has been appointed captain of the Limerick senior football team for the 2027 season, succeeding Cillian Fahy. He takes over leadership of the squad under incoming manager Micheál Cahill.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53806.story:
Rathkeale clubman Barry Coleman has been named captain of the Limerick senior football team for the 2027 season, taking over the leadership role from Cillian Fahy. Coleman previously served as vice-captain and steps into the primary role as the county squad prepares for a new campaign under incoming manager Micheál Cahill.

The forward brings significant inter-county experience to the position, having featured in the squad that earned promotion from Division Two of the Allianz National Football League in 2022 and reached the Tailteann Cup final in 2025. At club level, Coleman was among Rathkeale's leading scorers during their 2026 county championship campaign.

Coleman's appointment comes as Limerick looks to regroup following a difficult 2026 season that ended in relegation from Division Three. The team will compete in Division Four when the National Football League gets underway in January 2027, with promotion back to Division Three set as an immediate objective under Cahill's management.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53806.localAngle: The appointment places Rathkeale's Barry Coleman at the helm of the Limerick senior football team as they prepare for the 2027 season.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53806.originalTitle: Barry Coleman appointed Limerick senior football captain for 2027

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53803.headline: Treaty United Duo Shortlisted for PFAI Awards and Team of the Year
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53803.summary: Katie Lawlee and Madison McGuane have been named in the Women’s Premier Division Team of the Year and nominated for Young Player of the Year ahead of the November 21 ceremony.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53803.story:
Treaty United players Katie Lawlee and Madison McGuane have been named in the Women’s Premier Division Team of the Year and shortlisted for the Women’s Young Player of the Year award.

The nominations are part of the 2026 Professional Footballers’ Association of Ireland (PFAI) Awards, which will take place on Saturday, November 21. More than 750 votes were cast by professional players across the leagues for this year's accolades.

Both teenagers have made significant impacts at the Markets Field. McGuane earned her senior debut in March 2025 at age 15 and collected the division's Player of the Month award in April 2026, alongside her international duty captaining Ireland at underage levels. Forward Lawlee has similarly starred for the Limerick side, captaining national underage teams and securing the March 2026 Goal of the Month award.

Former Treaty United women’s manager Seán Russell has also been recognised with a nomination for Manager of the Year following his spell at the club before taking over at Shelbourne. Meanwhile, former men's player Lee Devitt featured in last season's First Division Team of the Year, though no current men's players were nominated following a difficult campaign.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53803.localAngle: Two of Treaty United's star players have been recognised nationally for their standout performances representing the Limerick side.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53803.originalTitle: Treaty United duo shortlisted ahead of PFA Awards ceremony

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363198.headline: Limerick Diocesan forum hears poverty is not inevitable ahead of World Day of the Poor
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363198.summary: Organisations and social outreach groups gathered at the Diocesan Centre in Corbally to address local inequalities and mark the tenth World Day of the Poor.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363198.story:
Poverty is not inevitable and local communities play a vital role in challenging the structures that sustain it, a Limerick Diocesan forum was told ahead of the tenth World Day of the Poor.

The gathering at the Diocesan Centre in Corbally brought together individuals and organisations involved in social outreach, research, and action across the region. Organised by Bishop of Limerick Brendan Leahy, the event also recognised the ongoing work of local organisations providing essential supports to disadvantaged groups.

Keynote speaker Jim Clarken, an Askeaton native and CEO of Oxfam Ireland, addressed the forum by stating that global inequality has a direct local relevance. He emphasised that the world's resources are sufficient, but the distribution remains the core issue, encouraging local organisations to share expertise and amplify the voices of those excluded from decision-making.

Opening the event, Bishop Leahy highlighted that despite Limerick's community spirit, significant unaddressed social inequalities persist alongside growing affluence. He noted that poverty takes multiple forms in the city and county, including material, social, cultural, digital, fuel, and housing poverty, and thanked volunteers for their daily impact on society.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363198.localAngle: The event brought together local Limerick social outreach organisations and community workers at the Diocesan Centre in Corbally to address regional disadvantage.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363093.headline: Inclusive rugby documentary Try! screens at Belltable on Monday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363093.summary: Director Oisín Mistéil’s 88-film feature follows four players on their journey to the World Cup of 15-a-side full-contact rugby for people with and without disabilities. The screening takes place on November 16 as part of the IFI@Belltable programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363093.story:
Film fans and rugby supporters in Limerick will have the chance to see the 88-minute Irish documentary *Try!* when it screens at the Belltable this Monday, November 16.

Part of the venue's IFI@Belltable programme, the film is directed by Oisín Mistéil and explores the world's most inclusive rugby tournament. It follows four players—Richie, Maeve, Tommy, and Paul—on their path to the World Cup in a unique 15-a-side, full-contact sport played by individuals with and without disabilities.

The documentary captures the team's journey from wet and windy training sessions to the climax of their World Cup campaign. Among the featured players is Richie, who shares how joining The Rebels made it possible for him to play the sport after years of being told his autism would prevent him from doing so.

Rated 12A, the film highlights the role sport plays in building community for those who previously felt they did not belong. Tickets for Monday's screening are available through the Belltable.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363093.localAngle: The screening brings a critically acclaimed Irish sports documentary directly to Limerick audiences at the Belltable on O'Connell Street.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363093.originalTitle: Inclusive rugby documentary Try! screens in Belltable

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362987.headline: Photographer Brendan Gleeson captures weekend social scenes in Limerick City pubs
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362987.summary: Local photographer Brendan Gleeson was out capturing weekend social scenes across Limerick City spots like the Locke Bar and Mother Mac's. Residents and visitors were snapped enjoying the lively atmosphere around town.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362987.story:
Limerick City's weekend social scene was out in full force as local photographer Brendan Gleeson captured lively gatherings at some of the city's most popular pubs. Patrons were snapped enjoying the atmosphere at both the Locke Bar and Mother Mac's.

Among those spotted out and about at the Locke Bar were Sophia Bayliss, Eva Barnett, Colin Murphy, Michael Regan, and Shirley Constan. Meanwhile, crowds gathered at Mother Mac's where Adam Flynn, Paula Skaite, Mairead Ryan, Brigid Shanahan, Jake Nagle, Anna Carey, and Ciara Regan were among those caught on camera.

The weekly photo feature highlights the vibrant social life across Limerick's city centre watering holes, giving locals a chance to spot familiar faces enjoying the weekend.
