https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362987.localAngle: The photo series captures familiar faces enjoying the weekend social scene across popular venues in Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362987.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Out and about in Limerick City

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363201.headline: Labour Cllr Pádraigh Reale Presses Council Over City Centre Festoon Lighting
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363201.summary: Labour Party councillor Pádraigh Reale has called on the local authority to fix ongoing connection issues with the festoon lighting at Arthur's Quay Park. While repairs along the Three Bridges Walk are complete, the Arthur's Quay section is awaiting a new ESB connection.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363201.story:
Labour Party councillor Pádraigh Reale has asked Limerick City and County Council for an update on city centre festoon lighting and the progress being made by the ESB to restore power at Arthur’s Quay.

At a recent Metropolitan District meeting, local representatives were informed that the Council's appointed maintenance contractor, LBK, has finished repairs on all identified faults along the festoon lighting network on the Three Bridges Walk. The local authority stated that weekly inspections and patrols are now in place to catch and fix future faults quickly.

However, the section of festoon lighting located at Arthur’s Quay Park remains non-operational and is currently awaiting a new ESB connection before it can be brought back into service.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363201.localAngle: The story directly impacts Limerick city centre residents and visitors who use the Three Bridges Walk and Arthur's Quay Park.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363201.originalTitle: Councillor asks Council to shed light on festoon lighting

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363200.headline: Learning Hub Limerick secures nearly €30,000 in national community funding
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363200.summary: Learning Hub Limerick in Kileely has been awarded €26,000 through the annual AIB Community €1m Fund following public and customer votes. The facility is one of 300 charities across Ireland to receive backing from the initiative.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363200.story:
Learning Hub Limerick has been chosen by the community to receive a major funding boost of nearly €30,000 through the annual AIB Community €1m Fund.

The Kileely-based educational hub has specifically secured a €26,000 allocation from the nationwide fund, which this year supports 300 different charities across Ireland.

The successful funding announcement follows a public selection process that relied on backing from AIB customers, the wider public, and bank employees. The initiative aims to spotlight and support charities making a tangible difference in the local areas where people live, work, and volunteer.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363200.localAngle: The funding directly benefits Learning Hub Limerick in Kileely, supporting its ongoing work within the local community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363200.originalTitle: Funding boost for Learning Hub Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363202.headline: Eir Retires 3G Network Across Limerick for 4G and 5G Upgrade
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363202.summary: Mobile provider eir has officially switched off its 3G data network in Limerick as part of a nationwide rollout to enhance 4G and 5G services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363202.story:
Eir customers in Limerick are officially offline when it comes to the provider's legacy 3G data network. The mobile and internet provider retired the network on October 28 as part of a broader, nationwide programme designed to support the continued development and enhancement of its 4G and 5G services.

The switch-off is being rolled out on a phased basis across the country. While the initial phase has already begun, the transition will continue across Limerick and remaining counties over the coming weeks.

According to the provider, the change is expected to cause no disruption for the vast majority of local users, who already rely on 4G and 5G services for their daily mobile and internet usage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363202.localAngle: The 3G network switch-off directly affects eir mobile and internet customers living and working in Limerick as part of the phased nationwide rollout.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363202.originalTitle: No more 3G data for Limerick eir customers

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363213.headline: Limerick's First Private Cemetery Opens in Castletroy Offering Pre-Purchased Plots
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363213.summary: Meadowstone Park Cemetery on the Monaleen Road has opened its first phase, providing 1,100 new burial plots with the option for people to pre-purchase graves. The eco-friendly park caters to all faiths and is the first facility of its kind outside Dublin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363213.story:
Limerick's first private cemetery park has officially opened on the Monaleen Road in Castletroy, offering locals the ability to pre-purchase graves for themselves and their families. Developed by a group of local residents responding to a 2022 council call for a new cemetery in the area, Meadowstone Park Cemetery is the only facility of its kind in Limerick and the first outside Dublin to allow pre-purchased plots.

Speaking to the Limerick Post, Dorothea Fahy said the first phase provides approximately 1,100 plots, with a total capacity of 3,300 expected across three phases. Designed by Limerick architect Deirdre Kelly, the grounds feature wildflower meadows, native trees, reflection pools, and flame torches. The facility is open to all faiths and offers traditional burial plots, Columbarium Walls, and Ash Burial Plots.

Services at the park are designed to accommodate elderly and less mobile mourners, with minimal walking distances from parking and gathering spaces. On burial days, families are provided with grave-side seating, a covered marquee for immediate family, and nearby heated fires for the service. 

The cemetery has been open for just over two weeks, with organisers noting strong local demand. "We find it gives people a lot of peace of mind, they don’t want to trouble their family when the time comes," Ms Fahy said. The park's design also places a strong emphasis on sustainability and biodiversity, featuring indigenous hedgerows, grasslands, and pollinator-friendly shrubs throughout the landscape.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363213.localAngle: The opening of Meadowstone Park Cemetery introduces Limerick's first private burial ground and the only cemetery in the county where residents can pre-purchase graves.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363213.originalTitle: New private park cemetery opens in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363210.headline: UL Mathematics and Physics Student Wins Prestigious Royal Irish Academy Prize
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363210.summary: University of Limerick student Frederick Costello has been honoured with the undergraduate Hamilton Prize in Mathematics by the Royal Irish Academy, recognising him as a top final-year student in his field.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363210.story:
A University of Limerick student has been recognised nationally after being named one of nine winners of the Royal Irish Academy's undergraduate Hamilton Prize in Mathematics. Frederick Costello, who is studying Mathematics and Physics at UL, was honoured during the 2026 Hamilton Lecture held last month.

The prize is awarded annually to the top-performing undergraduate student in their final year of study, as nominated by their respective universities. In recognition of his academic achievement, Costello received a cash prize and a certificate.

As part of the award, Costello also took part in an exclusive masterclass with Professor James Maybard, which was hosted by Ibec.

Photograph by Johnny Bambury.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363210.localAngle: University of Limerick student Frederick Costello was honoured as one of Ireland's top mathematics undergraduates by the Royal Irish Academy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363210.originalTitle: Limerick student wins prestigious Royal Irish Academy prize

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363268.headline: Limerick's Chloe Keogh wins gold at Kickboxing World Championships in Madrid
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363268.summary: Twenty-year-old Limerick kickboxer Chloe Keogh has won gold in the full contact low kick category at the International Sport Kickboxing Associations Championships in Madrid, improving on her two silver medals from 2024.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363268.story:
Limerick has a new World Champion following Chloe Keogh's success at the International Sport Kickboxing Associations Championships in Madrid. The 20-year-old secured gold in the full contact low kick category, stepping up after claiming a double silver at the 2024 tournament.

"Having competed at the World Championships in 2024 and come home with two silver medals, I knew I wanted to come back and push myself even further. To return this year and finally become a World Champion makes it all that bit more special," Keogh said.

Keogh, who trains with Hub Martial Arts and Learning Hub Limerick, credited her coach Paul O’Brien for his support throughout her training. She also thanked her teammates, family, friends, and sponsors for backing her journey to the world stage.

Her success contributed to a strong showing for the club, which had 12 representatives competing in Spain. The Limerick contingent returned with a total of nine medals, consisting of one gold, two silvers, and six bronzes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363268.localAngle: Limerick martial artist Chloe Keogh secured a world title representing Hub Martial Arts/Learning Hub Limerick at the international championships in Spain.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363214.headline: Limerick Beneficiaries Warned Over Estate Debts and Refusing Inheritances
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363214.summary: Local beneficiaries dealing with wills containing significant debts are advised to request a full estate breakdown before signing documents or considering a disclaimer. Under the Succession Act 1965, executors must handle all estate liabilities before any remaining assets are distributed.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363214.story:
Residents across Limerick navigating the probate process following the death of a relative are being advised on their rights regarding inherited debt and estate disclaimers. Legal experts have clarified that beneficiaries do not automatically become personally responsible for a deceased person's mortgages or personal loans simply by accepting an inheritance.

However, complications can arise if a will includes conditional gifts, such as property tied to specific mortgage repayments. While non-financial conditions like marriage or education requirements can sometimes be set aside by the courts if impossible to fulfil, beneficiaries retain the legal right to disclaim a gift entirely. Under Irish law, a disclaimer must apply to the whole amount rather than a portion, with the refused assets then falling into the estate's residue.

Before making any binding decisions or providing personal details like PPS numbers and dates of birth to executors, individuals are urged to request a clear outline of the estate's assets and liabilities. If a full disclaimer is being considered, beneficiaries should seek independent legal advice to ensure the documentation is handled correctly.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363214.localAngle: This legal guidance affects Limerick residents dealing with family estates and wills administered locally.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363262.headline: Hurling legend Ciarán Carey to host Adare charity night for Children’s Grief Centre
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363262.summary: Limerick hurling great Ciarán Carey is hosting 'An Evening of Restoring Hope' at Fitzgerald’s Woodlands House Hotel in Adare this Thursday, November 19. The ticket-only event will raise funds for the Children’s Grief Centre and features a lineup of sports stars, comedy, and music.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363262.story:
Limerick hurling icon Ciarán Carey will host 'An Evening of Restoring Hope' at The Treehouse in Fitzgerald’s Woodlands House Hotel, Adare, this coming Thursday, November 19, at 7.30pm. The event is being facilitated by Carey’s counselling service, which provides addiction and mental health support, with all proceeds going directly to the Children’s Grief Centre.

The Children’s Grief Centre offers its services completely free of charge to children who are grieving the loss of a loved one or experiencing family separation and emotional challenges. Thursday's fundraiser will feature an array of special guests, including All-Ireland Senior Hurling winners Cian Lynch and Kyle Hayes, alongside rugby figures Keith Earls and Olive Foley.

Entertainment on the night will be provided by comedian Aidan Tierney and musical act Madra Rua. Tickets for the event are strictly ticket-only and can be purchased through Eventmaster. Those seeking support from Carey’s addiction and mental health counselling service can contact 086 160 2874.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363262.localAngle: The event brings together prominent Limerick hurling, rugby, and entertainment figures in Adare to raise funds for a local support service for children.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363262.originalTitle: It’s good to talk, with Ciarán Carey

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363215.headline: Casper Kelly's directorial debut 'Buddy' delivers 1990s children's TV slasher horror
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363215.summary: Casper Kelly's debut film 'Buddy' combines 1990s children's television aesthetics with slasher horror, starring Topher Grace as part of its unhinged cast.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363215.story:
Film fans looking for a surreal crossover between children's educational programming and the slasher genre can now look to Casper Kelly's directorial debut, 'Buddy'. The feature-length project takes viewers on a nightmarish trip into a hyperbolic 1990s children's TV show, acting as a dark, violent answer to programmes like Barney and Friends.

The film centres on Buddy, a furry orange unicorn who outwardly leads a cheerful world of educational content and singalongs about friendship and personal hygiene. Beneath the surface, however, the character unleashes murderous tendencies reminiscent of Michael Myers, paired with Friday the 13th-style stabbings.

While the opening 20 minutes lean heavily into the mundane tropes of preschool television—triggering flashbacks to shows like Fireman Sam and Bob the Builder—the film quickly descends into an unhinged frolic. The production also features actor Topher Grace, known for *That '70s Show*, rounding out a cast that blends schmaltzy humour with horror.

Ultimately awarded a three-out-of-five star rating, the Sesame Street-meets-Texas Chainsaw Massacre crossbreed offers a puerile and bizarre ride that proves entirely unsuitable for squeamish viewers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363215.localAngle: Local film enthusiasts in Limerick can catch the latest cinematic reviews and cultural releases through the Limerick Post.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363403.headline: Scarlett Faulkner Murder Trial Adjourned at Central Criminal Court Due to Juror Illness
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363403.summary: The 11th day of the murder trial for Limerick mother Scarlett Faulkner was halted on Monday after a juror fell ill, adjourning proceedings at the Central Criminal Court until Tuesday afternoon.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363403.story:
Proceedings in the trial of two people accused of murdering Limerick mother Scarlett Faulkner were adjourned on Monday at the Central Criminal Court in Dublin after a juror became unwell.

The 28-year-old Limerick woman, who had an address at Longpavement, died on April 13 following an incident in Birdhill, County Tipperary, on March 21. Last week, Assistant State Pathologist Dr Margaret Bolster told the jury that Ms Faulkner died of a severe traumatic brain injury caused by multiple force blows with an iron bar.

Forensic and witness evidence presented earlier in the trial included testimony from individuals who came across the scene, alongside DNA evidence matching Ms Faulkner's blood on a 64.5-centimetre iron bar and a silver transit van door. The court also heard a series of voice notes and Garda interviews involving the two accused individuals.

A 41-year-old woman has pleaded not guilty to murder, burglary, and assault charges. A 17-year-old girl has pleaded not guilty to murder but guilty to manslaughter. The trial is scheduled to resume before Mr Justice Kerida Naidoo and the jury on Tuesday afternoon.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363403.localAngle: The trial concerns the tragic death of 28-year-old Limerick mother Scarlett Faulkner, who had an address at Longpavement in the city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363403.originalTitle: Proceedings in Scarlett Faulkner murder trial adjourned for day due to juror illness

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53825.headline: Kilmallock exit Munster championship as Dromin-Athlacca and Caherline reach finals
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53825.summary: Limerick clubs recorded two wins from three outings in the Munster hurling championships over the weekend, with Kilmallock bowing out against Ballygunner while Dromin-Athlacca and Caherline both advanced to provincial finals.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53825.story:
It was a mixed weekend for Limerick hurling clubs in the Munster Junior, Intermediate and Senior Hurling Championships, highlighted by Kilmallock's exit at the hands of All-Ireland holders Ballygunner on Sunday. The Limerick Senior champions battled courageously and found a lifeline through Oisin O’Reilly’s 43rd-minute goal. However, Ballygunner finished strongly with the final eight points—driven by top-scorer Dessie Hutchinson’s 1-4 and Pauric Mahony's impressive display—to seal a 1-20 to 1-11 victory and book a Munster final spot against Thurles Sarsfields.

There was better news for Limerick Intermediate champions Dromin-Athlacca, who edged past Clarecastle 1-20 to 0-22 in a fierce encounter on Sunday. Corner-forward Jack Fitzgibbon struck the game's only goal in the 14th minute, while county man David Reidy led the scoring with 10 points, including seven frees and a 65. The south Limerick men advance to face Tipperary side Saint Mary’s in the final on November 29.

Meanwhile, Limerick Junior champions Caherline secured a comfortable 2-20 to 0-13 win against Dr Croke’s on Saturday. Full-forward Hugh Murnane laid the foundations with two first-half goals, finishing with a personal tally of 2-5. Caherline now progress to the Munster Junior Hurling Final, where they will meet Cork’s Killshannig in two weeks' time.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53825.localAngle: Three Limerick club hurling sides represented the county across the Munster junior, intermediate, and senior championship fixtures over the weekend.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53825.originalTitle: Mixed results for Limerick hurling clubs in Munster Championships

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363238.headline: Limerick Post-Primary Schools Urged to Join Gender-Based Violence Campaign
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363238.summary: Secondary schools across Limerick are being called upon to participate in White Ribbon Ireland's Post-Primary Schools programme. The initiative aims to help staff challenge harmful gender norms and guide conversations with students on healthy relationships.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363238.story:
Secondary schools across Limerick are being urged to join White Ribbon Ireland’s Post-Primary Schools programme, which positions educational facilities as a key part of addressing Ireland’s gender-based violence crisis.

Led by the Men’s Development Network, the programme is designed to support school staff in fostering safer and more respectful environments. It aims to build educators' confidence in challenging harmful gender norms and attitudes, while providing guidance on how to facilitate conversations with young people about equality and healthy relationships.

The initiative comes ahead of the White Ribbon Ireland Conference 2026, hosted by the Men’s Development Network at the Aviva Stadium on November 19 under the theme “Change the Story”. Local school staff and administrators seeking further information on how to participate can visit mensnetwork.ie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363238.localAngle: Secondary schools throughout Limerick are being directly targeted by the national campaign to help address gender-based violence locally.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363238.originalTitle: Limerick schools urged to join campaign against gender-based violence

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363107.headline: Jimmy MacCarthy brings songbook tour to University Concert Hall
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363107.summary: Renowned songwriter Jimmy MacCarthy will perform his greatest hits at the University Concert Hall on November 25, accompanied by his band The Acoustic Horseman and a string quartet.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363107.story:
Limerick audiences will soon have a rare opportunity to experience some of Ireland's most enduring modern songs performed by their creator. Celebrated songwriter Jimmy MacCarthy is set to bring his special concert tour, *The Song of the Singing Horseman – The Best of Jimmy MacCarthy*, to the University Concert Hall on Wednesday, November 25.

The show follows recent performances at Cork Opera House and Dublin's National Concert Hall. During the Limerick date, MacCarthy will take to the stage alongside his backing band, The Acoustic Horseman. The performance features special string arrangements by Nollaig Casey and Bill Whelan, delivered by Casey and a live string quartet. They will be joined by guest musicians Steve Cooney, James Blennerhassett, and Paul McAteer to recreate the sound of the original recordings while sharing the stories behind the music.

MacCarthy's extensive catalogue includes modern classics such as "Ride On", "No Frontiers", "The Contender", and "Ancient Rain", which have been recorded by prominent artists including Christy Moore, Mary Black, The Corrs, and Westlife. Born in Macroom, County Cork, MacCarthy established himself on the Cork music circuit before his debut solo album launched a decades-long career that led to his induction into the IMRO Academy in 2013.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363107.localAngle: The acclaimed songwriter performs at the University Concert Hall on November 25 as part of his national tour.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363107.originalTitle: Jimmy MacCarthy brings The Song of the Singing Horseman to UCH

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53815.headline: Film in Limerick launches free training workshops for emerging directors and writers
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53815.summary: Film in Limerick has announced three free weekend workshops covering producing, screenwriting, and directing at the Engine building across November and December.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53815.story:
Emerging filmmakers across the Mid-West are being offered the chance to hone their craft through a series of free training workshops running at the Engine building in Limerick throughout November and December.

Organised by Film in Limerick in partnership with local authorities and the Limerick and Clare Education and Training Board, the initiative is part of the Engine Shorts Film Training and Production Scheme. The programme features three distinct weekend events led by industry professionals, covering producing with Aoibhín Murphy on November 21–22, screenwriting with Kate Leys on November 28, and directing with Hannah Quinn on December 5.

Regional Film Manager Paul C. Ryan said the sessions are designed to help participants take a creative concept and bring it to the screen. "From developing an initial concept and writing a script, to understanding the practicalities of planning, budgeting and producing a film, participants will gain an insight into the different stages involved," he said.

The workshops are open to anyone aged 18 and over in Ireland, though preference will be given to applicants from the Mid-West region. While the events are free, places are limited and successful applicants will be notified by email, with applications now open via limerick.ie.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53815.localAngle: The training workshops take place at the Engine building in Limerick and are backed by local authorities and the Limerick and Clare Education and Training Board.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53815.originalTitle: Film in Limerick announce free filmmaking training workshops

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363223.headline: Limerick Council acquires Wickham Street site to build Pigtown-themed pocket park
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363223.summary: Limerick Council has completed the acquisition of a derelict site at 20-24 Wickham Street to transform it into a public pocket park celebrating the city's pork industry heritage. The €80,000 project, supported by the 2026 Mayoral Fund, is scheduled for completion by the end of 2026.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363223.story:
Work is already underway to transform a fenced-off, overgrown site at 20-24 Wickham Street, at its junction with Lower Gerald Griffin Street, into a new public amenity for the city centre. Limerick Council completed the acquisition of the location to create the Wickham Street Pocket Park, which aims to provide a vibrant and multifunctional space for the neighbourhood.

The park's design is themed around Limerick's historic pork industry. Proposed timber sculptures and murals created by Draw Out will reflect on the area's Pigtown heritage. The facility will also feature age-friendly seating, herbaceous and tree planting, and a dog-friendly layout to encourage greater public use of the previously underutilised space.

Tallybrooke Civil Engineering Ltd has already completed site clearance and wall stabilisation works at the location. The project is backed by €80,000 in funding from the 2026 Mayoral Fund and is on track to open by the end of 2026.

Limerick Mayor John Moran welcomed the completion of the acquisition. "This project demonstrates how relatively small interventions can make a significant difference to the quality and attractiveness of our city centre," he said. "By transforming a neglected and inaccessible site into a welcoming public space, we are creating another reason for people to spend time in the city while also celebrating an important piece of Limerick’s heritage."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363223.localAngle: The project transforms a neglected city centre site in Limerick while celebrating the local area's historic Pigtown heritage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363223.originalTitle: Pig Park on the pig’s back says Limerick Council

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363216.headline: Limerick manager advised on rights as boss demands holiday availability
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363216.summary: A local manager preparing for their first Christmas break in over a year has been told to remain on call. Legal guidance clarifies that annual leave is a statutory right and working time legislation applies.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363216.story:
A Limerick employee facing pressure to stay on call during a hard-earned Christmas break has been advised to check their contract and clarify how any working time will be compensated. The worker, who holds a management position in a company that recently underwent restructuring and redundancies, has not taken leave in over a year.

Despite agreeing a three-week holiday period to catch up on much-needed time off, the employer insisted the worker remain reachable by phone and email for urgent issues. Legal guidance highlights that under the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997, employees are entitled to paid annual leave, and both parties share a duty to ensure it is taken.

While the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) has issued a Code of Practice on the Right to Disconnect, it notes that senior employees may occasionally be contacted in genuinely urgent circumstances. However, experts advise that remaining available should not be treated as a default expectation and any required work during leave should result in time being rescheduled or restored rather than simply deducted.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363216.localAngle: Local workers and employers across Limerick are navigating holiday entitlements and remote availability rules as the busy Christmas period approaches.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363216.originalTitle: Lawlink – Boss is asking me to me ‘on call’ during my first holiday in years, what should I do?

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363282.headline: Templeglantine Clinch Munster Junior Camogie Title with Three-Point Win Over Cillard
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363282.summary: Templeglantine captured the Munster Junior Camogie Championship title after defeating Kerry side Cillard 3-12 to 4-6 in an exciting final in Charleville.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363282.story:
Templeglantine are celebrating a historic Munster Junior Camogie Championship title after holding off a resilient Cillard side to claim a 3-12 to 4-6 victory in an action-packed final held in Charleville.

The Limerick side laid the groundwork for their victory in the opening half, building a commanding 1-10 to 1-2 lead by the interval. Although Cillard mounted a strong challenge in the second half, the West Limerick outfit maintained their composure to cross the finish line with three points to spare.

A crucial part of the victory came from the lethal goal-scoring form of Sarah O'Brien, who netted twice, alongside a vital goal from Michelle Curtin. Curtin's standout performance was further recognized when she was named Player of the Match, receiving her award from Munster Camogie Secretary Mairi McMahon.

Additional points were contributed across the attack by O'Brien, Curtin, Stephanie Woulfe, Noelle Curtin, and Ciara Curtin. The winning side proudly lifted the cup under the captaincy of Connie Sheehan.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363282.localAngle: Templeglantine brought home a Munster camogie title to Limerick following a hard-fought provincial final against Kerry opposition.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363434.headline: Limerick Chamber Urges Faster Rail Investment and Shannon Estuary Development
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363434.summary: At the annual Regional Business Awards, Limerick Chamber President Maria Gleeson called on Tánaiste Simon Harris to accelerate regional rail connectivity and develop the Shannon Estuary. The gala event also celebrated local business achievements, with Croom Medical taking home Overall Business of the Year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363434.story:
Limerick business leaders have pressed the Government to accelerate regional rail connectivity and unlock the potential of the Shannon Estuary, warning that infrastructure bottlenecks and rising operational costs threaten future investment in the Mid West. Speaking at the Limerick Chamber President’s Dinner and Regional Business Awards, Chamber President Maria Gleeson told Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris that local companies are ready to drive job creation and innovation given the right conditions.

Ms Gleeson urged the Government to fund All-Island Strategic Rail Review projects for the Limerick-Shannon area, building upon the recent reinstatement of the Limerick-Foynes freight railway and planned temporary passenger services for the 2027 Ryder Cup. She also called for a dedicated delivery programme to align offshore renewable energy development in the Shannon Estuary with port infrastructure, industrial policy, and grid investment.

Tánaiste Simon Harris acknowledged the region's strong enterprise sector, skilled workforce, and solid track record in drawing investment from both indigenous and multinational firms. 

The evening also celebrated regional business success, with Catherine Duffy receiving the President’s Award for her leadership at Northern Trust and her contributions to the Mid West community. Croom Medical claimed the Overall Business of the Year award, alongside the Best SME prize. Other winners included Fíor Jewellery for Best Emerging Business, BD RCI for Best Employer, Narrative 4 for Best Not-for-Profit Impact, CD Environmental for Sustainability, WrxFlo for Innovation, University Concert Hall Limerick for Customer Experience, and Conack Construction for community impact.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363434.localAngle: The story centers on infrastructure demands and business achievements directly impacting the Limerick and Mid West regional economy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363434.originalTitle: Limerick businesses want accelerator pedal pressed on rail transport, Chamber awards hear

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363449.headline: Kurt Ryan Pleads Guilty to 2010 Murder of Limerick Man Lee Slattery
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363449.summary: Kurt Ryan has pleaded guilty to the 2010 murder of 25-year-old Lee Slattery, who was forced to dig his own grave before being shot twice in Limerick. The case was brought back to court after being reopened by a cold case unit in 2021.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363449.story:
The sister of Lee Slattery told the Central Criminal Court in Cork that her brother was the "heartbeat of our home" during a harrowing victim impact statement. Twenty-five-year-old Mr Slattery's remains were discovered in a shallow grave at Delmege Estate, Knockalisheen Road, on May 31, 2010, after being reported missing days earlier.

Thirty-two-year-old Kurt Ryan, of Moylish Crescent, Limerick—who was 17 at the time of the incident—pleaded guilty to murder in association with a criminal organisation and to possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life. Prosecution counsel stated that Mr Slattery was coerced and lured to an abandoned property during the early hours of May 28, 2010, after refusing to participate in a local gang feud.

Witness Charlene Costello told Gardaí that Mr Ryan returned home on the night of the killing and admitted to the shooting. Defence counsel challenged the credibility of the witness due to past addiction and health conditions, though the guilty plea brought a new development to the cold case, which was reopened in 2021.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363449.localAngle: The case involves a tragic crime that occurred within Limerick communities, affecting a local family and involving city-based criminal organisations.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363449.originalTitle: Sister of Limerick man made to dig his own grave before being shot says he was ‘heartbeat of our home’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363240.headline: O'Donoghue Presses Justice Minister Over Rural Garda Shortages in Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363240.summary: Independent Ireland TD Richard O'Donoghue has raised concerns with Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan over the lack of Garda presence in rural County Limerick. In response, Minister O'Callaghan stated that recruitment is ongoing and national Garda numbers are expected to reach 15,000.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363240.story:
The absence of a visible Garda presence across rural County Limerick has been brought directly to the Dáil. Independent Ireland TD Richard O'Donoghue challenged Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan on the issue, seeking guarantees regarding security for local residents.

During the exchanges, Deputy O'Donoghue pressed the Minister for a firm commitment on the level of policing that urban and rural communities across the county can expect going forward to ensure public safety.

In response, Minister O'Callaghan pointed to ongoing recruitment efforts as a driver for increased deployments. He noted that additional Gardaí will be allocated to both frontline duties and specialist units, which include dedicated Community Policing teams.

"I expect that Garda numbers will reach 15,000 in the near future, and numbers will continue to grow beyond 15,000 over the coming years," Minister O'Callaghan stated, adding that An Garda Síochána remains fully committed to tackling all forms of crime.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363240.localAngle: The security and policing levels across urban and rural areas of County Limerick were the central focus of the Dáil exchange.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363240.originalTitle: Limerick TD speaks out on Garda presence in County Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363239.headline: National Gallery masterpiece La Jeune Bretonne arrives at The Hunt Museum
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363239.summary: Roderic O'Connor's iconic painting La Jeune Bretonne is now on special display at The Hunt Museum in Limerick. The artwork will remain on exhibition until January 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363239.story:
An iconic painting from the National Gallery of Ireland has officially arrived at The Hunt Museum in Limerick. Roderic O’Connor’s *La Jeune Bretonne* is on special loan to the city as part of the cultural programme celebrating Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

The high-profile loan highlights longstanding cultural connections between Ireland and Brittany, as well as Limerick’s historic friendship with its twin city of Quimper. Alongside the headline piece, visitors to the museum will also be able to view other works by the artist, including *Breton Woman* and *Red Firs*.

The special exhibition will remain on display for local art enthusiasts and visitors at The Hunt Museum until January 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363239.localAngle: The exhibition reinforces Limerick's historic friendship with its twin city of Quimper through a major cultural loan from the National Gallery of Ireland.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363421.headline: Over 400 attend Limerick Chamber President's Dinner and Regional Business Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363421.summary: More than 400 business leaders and guests gathered in Limerick last week for the annual Chamber event celebrating Mid West enterprise. Northern Trust General Manager Catherine Duffy was among the award recipients on the night.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363421.story:
More than 400 business leaders, guests, and public figures turned out last week for the annual Limerick Chamber President's Dinner and Regional Business Awards, celebrating the best of commerce and enterprise across the Mid West region.

Attendees at the high-profile gathering included Tánaiste Simon Harris, Limerick Chamber President Maria Gleeson, Minister Kieran O'Donnell, and Cllr Peter Doyle. A central feature of the evening was the recognition of regional business achievements, with Northern Trust General Manager Catherine Duffy receiving the Chamber President's Award.

The annual event serves as a major fixture on the local business calendar, highlighting top-performing companies and key figures driving economic activity and employment throughout Limerick and the wider Mid West.

Photographer Kieran Ryan-Benson captured the proceedings as business owners, developers, and political representatives mingled at the major regional celebration.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363421.localAngle: The event brought together over 400 business leaders from across Limerick and the Mid West to celebrate local enterprise and achievement.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363421.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Out and about at the Limerick Chamber President’s Dinner and Regional Business Awards

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363286.headline: Limerick Celtics secure top spot with 100-83 victory over UCC Demons
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363286.summary: Limerick Celtics moved to a 6-1 record in the Domino’s Men’s Super League after a 100-83 home win against UCC Demons. Tiras Morton starred with 15 points, 16 rebounds, and seven assists.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363286.story:
Limerick Celtics strengthened their position at the summit of the Domino’s Men’s Super League following a conclusive 100-83 home victory over UCC Demons.

Sebastian Cole led the scoring for the Celtics with 21 points, but it was Tiras Morton who delivered a standout all-round performance on the night. Morton contributed 15 points, hauled in 16 rebounds, and provided seven assists to help seal the win.

Elsewhere in the league action, Limerick Eagles suffered a heavy 118-89 defeat away to Killester at St Munchin’s College. Alex Carlisle continued his strong scoring form for the Munster side with 24 points, while Irish underage international Fryderyk Klimas added 12 points in the losing effort.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363286.localAngle: The Limerick Celtics maintained their lead at the top of the Super League table with a strong home win, while Limerick Eagles faced a tough defeat against Killester at St Munchin’s College.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363286.originalTitle: Celtics keep top spot in Super League

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363515.headline: Castleconnell Teen Jailed for Nearly Six Years Over Death of Limerick Nurse Áine O'Reilly
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363515.summary: Keelan O’Connell has been sentenced to five years and 11 months with the final year suspended after driving high on drugs and at speeds up to 180kph, causing the death of 33-year-old nurse Áine O’Reilly in County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363515.story:
A 19-year-old man who was driving high on drugs and at excessive speeds when he caused the death of a Limerick nurse has been jailed for five years and 11 months, with the final year suspended.

Keelan O’Connell, of Scanlon Park, Castleconnell, was sentenced at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court on Tuesday. The court heard that O’Connell was driving without a licence or insurance and was already disqualified from driving at the time of the fatal collision. Travelling at speeds between 160kph and 180kph in a 100kph zone, he slammed into the rear of a car, which then collided with the vehicle driven by 33-year-old Áine O’Reilly.

Ms O’Reilly, from Pallasgreen, was on her way to work at Shannondoc, an out-of-hours GP service in Limerick, when she died at the scene. The driver of the other car struck by O'Connell was seriously injured in the crash. Sentencing judge Mary Morrissey also imposed a 10-year driving ban on O’Connell, with his prison sentence backdated to March 20, when he first went into custody following his arrest.

O’Connell pleaded guilty to a string of charges, including dangerous driving causing death, dangerous driving causing serious bodily harm, driving without insurance or a licence, and failing to report and offer assistance knowing a person was seriously injured or dead.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363515.localAngle: The fatal collision claimed the life of a County Limerick nurse travelling to work at a local out-of-hours GP service, impacting communities across Pallasgreen and Castleconnell.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363515.originalTitle: Jail sentence for teen who caused nurse’s death

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363477.headline: Gardaí investigate shooting at Castleconnell house in latest local attack
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363477.summary: Shots were fired at a home in the St Patrick’s Villas estate in Castleconnell on Saturday evening. No injuries were reported as Gardaí appeal for information on the latest violent incident in the village.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363477.story:
Gardaí have launched an investigation after a firearm was discharged at a house in the riverside village of Castleconnell over the weekend.

Emergency services and Gardaí responded to the incident in the St Patrick’s Villas estate at approximately 7pm on Saturday, November 14. A Garda spokeswoman confirmed that no injuries were reported during the shooting, and enquiries into the circumstances of the incident are currently ongoing.

The gun attack marks the latest in a string of violent incidents targeting properties in the local area. Recent weeks have seen a number of vehicles attacked in the village, alongside an incident where masked men armed with slash-hooks visited a residential property. Similar violence occurred in August of last year, when shots were fired at homes and masked individuals attacked a house and firebombed a car.

The Garda Press Office did not respond when asked whether the house was occupied at the time shots were fired into the property.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363477.localAngle: The shooting marks the latest in a string of violent property attacks in the County Limerick village of Castleconnell.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363477.originalTitle: Gardaí investigating shots fired at house in Castleconnell

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363431.headline: 3for3 Breast Cancer Walk raises over €48,000 to surpass €250,000 total
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363431.summary: The annual Limerick charity walk has hit a major ten-year milestone, bringing in a total of over a quarter of a million euro for the Symptomatic Breast Unit at University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363431.story:
The 3for3 Breast Cancer Awareness Walk has officially crossed the €250,000 fundraising threshold for the Symptomatic Breast Unit at University Hospital Limerick. The milestone was achieved following this year's event on Sunday, October 18, which alone brought in over €48,000.

Favouring clear weather, a crowd of families, friends, supporters, and breast cancer survivors gathered at Arthur’s Quay Park before taking on Limerick’s Three Bridges route for the tenth-anniversary walk.

Professor Anne Merrigan addressed attendees at the event, underscoring the critical role of breast cancer awareness and the tangible impact that ten years of funds raised by the 3for3 initiative have had on the hospital's Symptomatic Breast Unit and its patients.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363431.localAngle: The funds raised directly benefit the Symptomatic Breast Unit at University Hospital Limerick, aiding local patients and healthcare services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363431.originalTitle: 3FOR3 reaches incredible €250,000 milestone for UHL Symptomatic Breast Unit

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363492.headline: Moyross Mother Carrie Mullane-Noonan Laid to Rest in Limerick This Wednesday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363492.summary: The funeral takes place this Wednesday for 39-year-old Carrie Mullane-Noonan from Moyross, whose body was recovered from Lough Erne last month. Three people have since faced court charges following her disappearance and death.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363492.story:
The funeral arrangements have been finalized for Carrie Mullane-Noonan, a 39-year-old mother-of-four from Moyross, who will be laid to rest this Wednesday (November 18). Ms Mullane-Noonan had been missing since arriving in Enniskillen on October 10, and her body was subsequently recovered from Lough Erne on November 9.

Her remains will repose at Cross’s Funeral Home in Limerick City on Wednesday morning before moving to Corpus Christi Church in Moyross for a midday Requiem Mass. Burial will follow at Ballycannon Cemetery in Meelick. In a heartfelt funeral notice, her family remembered her as being "forever loved, deeply mourned, and sadly missed" by her four children—Jayden, Madison, Lily, and Luke—alongside her parents, siblings, extended family, and wide circle of friends.

In a statement, the Noonan family expressed profound gratitude to the PSNI, Mayorstone Garda Station, and the Moyross community for their extraordinary support throughout the search and aftermath. Meanwhile, legal proceedings are underway. Michael Lynch, 35, of Trasna Park, Enniskillen, has been remanded in custody charged with murder. Two other individuals from the same address—Kenneth Lynch, 31, and Mary Lynch, 69—have also appeared before the courts on related charges of withholding information and assisting an alleged offender.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363492.localAngle: The tragic loss of Limerick mother Carrie Mullane-Noonan has deeply impacted the community of Moyross, where her family and children reside.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363492.originalTitle: Limerick mother ‘forever loved and deely mourned’ to be laid to rest on Wednesday

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53843.headline: Rachael Blackmore and Jean Butler receive honorary doctorates from UL
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53843.summary: Grand National-winning jockey Rachael Blackmore and acclaimed choreographer Jean Butler have been awarded honorary doctorates at Plassey House. University Chancellor Brigid Laffan presented the highest honours to the two athletes in front of family, friends, and invited guests.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53843.story:
Grand National-winning jockey Rachael Blackmore and internationally acclaimed dancer Jean Butler received the University of Limerick's highest honour today at Plassey House. University Chancellor Brigid Laffan presented the awards with friends, family, and invited guests in attendance.

Blackmore, a 2015 Equine Science graduate from UL, was conferred with an Honorary Doctor of Science. Speaking to RTÉ, the Tipperary native expressed her excitement: "To be honoured in this way is just phenomenal, it really, really is, and a big thanks to everyone involved who made this happen." Blackmore is celebrated as the first female jockey to win the Champion Hurdle, the Aintree Grand National, and the Cheltenham Gold Cup, alongside being crowned leading jockey at the Cheltenham Festival with 18 career wins.

Jean Butler was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Letters following an impressive career that included sparking international interest with her 1994 Eurovision appearance in Riverdance. Butler previously completed an MA in World Contemporary Dance at UL and served as an artist in residence at the University's Irish World Academy of Music and Dance from 2003 to 2005.

UL President Shane Killcommins praised both recipients, stating they "represent fearlessness and a drive to pursue the very best in sporting and creative endeavor."
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53843.localAngle: The University of Limerick hosted the conferring ceremony at Plassey House, celebrating two figures with strong ties to the institution.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53843.originalTitle: UL awards Rachael Blackmore and Jean Butler honorary doctorates

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363231.headline: Councillors Clash with Limerick Council Management Over Property Disposal Legal Clarity
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363231.summary: Limerick councillors slammed council management at a special meeting over a lack of legal preparation regarding the disposal of six local authority houses to Limerick Twenty Thirty. Following an hour-long adjournment for legal advice, it was ultimately agreed that board members had no conflict of interest.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363231.story:
Limerick City and County Council management faced fierce criticism from elected members at Merchants Quay for failing to have proper legal guidance in place ahead of a special meeting regarding property disposals. The session was thrown into confusion at the start when several councillors who sit on the board of Limerick Twenty Thirty questioned whether they needed to leave over a potential conflict of interest regarding the transfer of six council-owned houses to the development company.

Fine Gael councillors John Sheahan, Daniel Butler, Sarah Kiely, and Dan McSweeney, alongside Fianna Fáil's Michael Collins and Independent Eddie Ryan, expressed frustration over the executive's lack of readiness. Council Director General Dr Pat Daly initially suggested that members should step out if they felt any discomfort "in the interest of absolute fairness and belt and races." However, Cllrs Sheahan, Butler, Collins, and Ryan ultimately opted to leave the chamber.

Cllr McSweeney blasted the executive's response during the session, telling Dr Daly that the top table had "serious questions to answer" and noting that the lack of readily available advice was "deeply, deeply concerning." Cllr Adam Teskey echoed these concerns, stating that relying on phrases like "I suppose" and "I think" on important legal matters is dangerous. Following an hour-long adjournment to seek formal legal advice, the councillors returned to the chamber after it was agreed that no conflict of interest existed.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363231.localAngle: The dispute centers on decisions made by Limerick City and County Council regarding local authority housing and the local development company Limerick Twenty Thirty.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363231.originalTitle: Council management comes under fire over legal quandary

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53821.headline: Gurriers and Thomas Bartlett to headline All We Have Are Days festival in Limerick
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53821.summary: Limerick's winter-closing festival returns for its third edition from January 29 to February 1, 2027, featuring 140 artists across 25 city venues.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53821.story:
Post-punk band Gurriers and Grammy-winning musician Thomas Bartlett will headline the third edition of the All We Have Are Days festival, which takes over Limerick from Friday, January 29 to Monday, February 1, 2027. Billed as Ireland’s first gathering after winter, the four-day cultural event features an ambitious programme of 140 artists, 60 shows, and 25 venues across the city.

The lineup also includes traditional musician Cormac Begley, Limerick's own Denise Chaila, poet Feli Speaks, THEATRE, Bronagh Gallagher, Brad Pitt Light Orchestra, Esme O’Riordan, Zkellies & Catherine Ireton, Dowry, and Leah Hayden Cassidy. Performances and events will take place in well-known Limerick spaces including Theatre Royal, John’s Church/Dance Limerick, Dolan’s, The Commercial, Pharmacia, and Mother Mac’s, with a comprehensive programme of free events alongside ticketed shows.

Presented by thefiveandeight in partnership with Guinness and Limerick City & County Council, the festival is supported by the Mayoral Fund. Mayor of Limerick John Moran said the event has become an important fixture on the local cultural calendar.

Tickets for selected shows are now on sale via Eventbrite, priced from €10 to €28, while many events remain free with required booking. Further programme additions and special collaborations will be announced ahead of the festival.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53821.localAngle: The four-day festival takes place across 25 venues in Limerick City, featuring local artists and supported by the Limerick City & County Council and the Mayoral Fund.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53821.originalTitle: All We Have Are Days festival to bring 140 artists to 25 venues across Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363472.headline: Victim tells Central Criminal Court sitting in Limerick he was set on fire
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363472.summary: Patrick Williams told a court he still suffers nightmares a year after he was allegedly doused in petrol, set alight, beaten, and stabbed during an attack in Tipperary. Chad Allan has pleaded not guilty to attempted murder and related charges.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363472.story:
A man who was allegedly doused in petrol, set on fire, beaten, and stabbed told the Central Criminal Court on Monday that he continues to suffer nightmares a year on from the attack. Patrick Williams (42) gave harrowing evidence during the trial of Chad Allan, who is accused of attempted murder at Knockane, Ballylooby, near Cahir, County Tipperary, on October 11, 2025.

“I went up in flames, I was in agony, my skin was peeling off,” Mr Williams told the court, which is sitting in Limerick. CCTV footage was played showing what appeared to be the petrol attack, capturing a bright ball of fire and a male screaming. Mr Williams claimed he drove a borrowed red Audi to the home of Luke Caplice, where Mr Caplice and Mr Allan later arrived in a jeep. According to the prosecution, Mr Allan acted in a "joint enterprise" with Mr Caplice, allegedly directing him to set Mr Williams on fire after Mr Caplice rammed the Audi and doused the victim in petrol.

Mr Williams told the court that he managed to remove his burning clothes, stating he would have "burned to death" otherwise. He claimed that as he ran naked from the yard, Mr Allan tried to pull him back, struck him across the head with a bottle, and stabbed him in the back before he managed to escape to neighbouring properties.

Mr Allan (27), with an address in Cahir, has pleaded not guilty to attempted murder, assault causing serious harm, arson, and the theft of petrol, diesel, and kerosene. Under cross-examination by senior counsel Bernard Condon, Mr Williams rejected suggestions that he was not telling the truth or that his account of the events was inaccurate. The trial before the Central Criminal Court continues.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363472.localAngle: The Central Criminal Court is currently sitting in Limerick to hear the high-profile attempted murder trial.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363472.originalTitle: ‘I went up in flames, I was in agony’: Man allegedly doused in petrol and set alight gives testimony in attempted murder trial

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363436.headline: Martinstown's Team McManus Secures Impressive Cheltenham and Navan Double
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363436.summary: JP McManus's racing stable celebrated a notable weekend double, highlighted by Meetmebythesea winning the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham and The Wallpark claiming the Troystown Handicap Chase at Navan.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363436.story:
Team McManus of Martinstown enjoyed a stellar weekend across the water and at home, securing a notable double on the racing front in the famed green and gold colours. 

The highlight came at Cheltenham where the fancied Meetmebythesea (2/1f) triumphed in the valuable Paddy Power Gold Cup. Ridden by UK retained jockey Harry Cobden and trained by Ben Pauling, it marked the first time owner JP McManus has captured the prestigious prize.

Speaking to the Racing Post about future ambitions, McManus said: “It’s nice to win the Paddy Power. I’ve tried many times and have always come up short in the past. I’ve never won the King George, the Champion Chase or the Arkle – and there’s the two mares’ hurdles at the festival. I’ve got to try and get those off the bucket list now.”

The weekend's success was rounded off at Navan by The Wallpark (6/1), which secured victory in the €100,000 BAR 1 Betting Troystown Handicap Chase. Trained by Gordon Elliott, the horse was guided to victory by jockey Jack Kennedy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363436.localAngle: The successful racing syndicate is based in Martinstown, carrying the famous green and gold colours associated with prominent local owner JP McManus.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363246.headline: Kilmallock's West Wall Walkway identified as prime location for wildlife lighting
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363246.summary: Sinn Féin Councillor PJ Carey has pressed Limerick City and County Council on funding options for low-level, wildlife-friendly lighting along the West Wall Walkway in Kilmallock.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363246.story:
Sinn Féin Councillor PJ Carey has asked Limerick City and County Council whether funding will be sought to install low-level, wildlife-friendly lighting at the West Wall Walkway in Kilmallock.

During a recent monthly district meeting, Cllr Carey was informed that four local walkways were recently assessed for their suitability for this specific type of lighting. The West Wall Walkway emerged as the most appropriate location, largely due to a limited amount of recorded bat activity and the existing level of surrounding illumination.

However, implementing the lighting will require a specific funding allocation. According to council officials, this would need to be secured through either the General Municipal Allocation (GMA) or the Development Fund, as other funding streams included in the schedule of municipal district works do not cover projects of this nature.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363246.localAngle: The proposed lighting project directly impacts local infrastructure and residents using the West Wall Walkway in Kilmallock.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363246.originalTitle: Limerick councillor has questions on funding for West Wall Walkway in Kilmallock

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363232.headline: Limerick Council libraries record 900,000 book loans and 4,000 events in three years
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363232.summary: New figures show Limerick's three city libraries recorded 900,000 book loans, 4,000 public events, and 910 school class visits between 2022 and 2025. The data was released ahead of the council's statutory budget meeting following a request by Cllr Shane Hickey-O'Mara.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363232.story:
New figures released to Limerick City and County Council reveal that city libraries recorded over 900,000 book borrows, facilitated 910 school classes, and hosted upwards of 4,000 free public events between 2022 and 2025. 

Social Democrats councillor Shane Hickey-O'Mara requested the statistics ahead of the upcoming statutory budget meeting. The data covers council-run library facilities across the Metropolitan District, highlighting community engagement through art exhibitions, local history lectures, book clubs, and adult education classes.

Cllr Hickey-O'Mara also pointed to recent service expansions, including the installation of communication boards across all 16 county branches to assist library users with different abilities. The roll-out builds on previous accessibility measures, such as the sensory room opened at Watch House Cross Library in Moyross in 2019.

Additionally, the library service launched the inaugural 'One Limerick, One Book' initiative this year, selecting local author Karen Fitzgibbon's psychological thriller *Tell the Truth*. Cllr Hickey-O'Mara stated that the council's libraries remain essential free public amenities for residents of all ages and abilities across the city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363232.localAngle: The figures highlight the usage and ongoing community impact of local library services across Limerick city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363232.originalTitle: Council figures tell story of incredible Limerick librarians

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363248.headline: Labour Councillor Urges Mayor Moran to Secure Funding for Limerick CCTV Network
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363248.summary: Cllr Pádraigh Reale has called on Mayor John Moran to intervene and secure a further year of funding for Limerick's CCTV network to protect the system and 20 local jobs. He argues a 12-month extension will give the newly established Community Safety Partnership time to become operational.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363248.story:
The future of Limerick's CCTV network and 20 local jobs are currently at risk, according to Labour Party councillor Pádraigh Reale. Cllr Reale has formally urged Mayor John Moran to intervene and secure an additional year of funding for the system.

While acknowledging that neither the Mayor nor Limerick City and County Council should be expected to finance the CCTV network over the long term, Cllr Reale insisted that local authorities maintain a duty of care to the people of Limerick. He emphasized the need for a proactive approach to safeguard both the infrastructure and the staff affected by the funding uncertainty.

“I believe we need to take a proactive approach to protecting the system and the people affected. Securing funding for one further year would provide a vital opportunity for the newly established Community Safety Partnership to get to work,” Cllr Reale said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363248.localAngle: The funding shortfall threatens Limerick's city-wide CCTV network and puts 20 local jobs at risk.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363248.originalTitle: Security of Limerick CCTV funding urged once again

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363520.headline: Light Up Limerick procession kicks off city Christmas festival this Saturday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363520.summary: Limerick City and County Council has unveiled its 2026 Christmas festival line-up, starting this Saturday with the Light Up Limerick procession. The festive trail spans from King John's Castle to The Crescent, featuring a new Georgian Christmas Fayre and ice skating.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363520.story:
The festive season officially gets underway in Limerick this Saturday (November 21) with the return of the Light Up Limerick procession and Christmas lights switch-on ceremony. Produced by LUXE, the procession will depart from Brown Thomas at 7pm, travelling along O’Connell Street before a grand finale and pyrotechnic display at Lower Glentworth Street.

This year's festival centres on a trail of experiences stretching from King John's Castle through the city centre to The Crescent on O’Connell Avenue. Major new additions include a Georgian Christmas Fayre running at The Crescent until December 23, featuring market stalls, artisan gifts, food, and a traditional carousel. Arthur's Quay Park will also host ice skating, entertainment, and a panoramic wheel.

Mayor of Limerick John Moran said the programme reflects the warmth and goodwill of people across the county. “From King John’s Castle to The Crescent, there’s magic around every corner,” he said. “I’m confident that children right across the country will discover that, this year, Limerick even beats Lapland.”

Príomh Chomhairleoir Cllr Tom Ruddle encouraged locals to engage with the more than 150 listings now live on Limerick.ie/Christmas, which include theatre, live music, comedy, and community celebrations spanning both the city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363520.localAngle: The festival spans key Limerick landmarks from King John's Castle to The Crescent, bringing festive events and community celebrations directly to local residents.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363520.originalTitle: CHRISTMAS LINE-UP REVEALED: Christmas starts here as lights blaze across Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363422.headline: Gardens International hosts annual Garryowen Business and Leadership Lunch
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363422.summary: Rugby legend Keith Wood hosted the 2026 Garryowen Leadership and Business lunch at Gardens International last week, featuring special guest Sam Torrance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363422.story:
Gardens International provided the venue last week for the 2026 Garryowen Leadership and Business lunch, drawing local business figures and sports fans alike.

Irish rugby legend Keith Wood served as host for the event, which featured eight-time Ryder Cup player and winning captain Sam Torrance as the special guest. Torrance took part in an on-stage conversation led by Shane O’Donoghue.

Attendees at the city centre lunch included John Mark Griffin, Dave Sherry, Michael Sherry, Liam Glynn, and Audrey Fehily, with photography on the day captured by Kieran Ryan-Benson.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363422.localAngle: The high-profile business and leadership lunch was held locally at Gardens International in Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363422.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Garryowen leadership lunch

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363437.headline: Athlacca handler Evan McAuliffe chases back-to-back titles in St Leger final
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363437.summary: Local trainer Evan McAuliffe is bidding to retain the Irish St. Leger crown this Saturday night as Drombeg King lines up for the 94th final at Limerick Greyhound Stadium.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363437.story:
Local hopes rest firmly on the shoulders of Athlacca trainer Evan McAuliffe this weekend as he prepares Drombeg King for the 94th 1XBet Irish St. Leger final at Limerick Greyhound Stadium this Saturday night.

McAuliffe is bidding to retain the prestigious title he won last year with Drombeg Banner. Securing back-to-back victories will be no small task, however, as Drombeg King faces a stellar line-up on the night.

The final brings together some of the sport's biggest names, including Kingdom Derby winner Solo and Go, Irish Derby champion Bockos Gold, and English Derby winner Lennies Eddie. Also joining the field are Irish Puppy Derby champion Getup The Boy and Ballymac Deniro, the English Derby runner-up and holder of the 550 track record at Limerick.

Racing gets underway with an attractive support card from 7.30pm ahead of the headline final.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363437.localAngle: Athlacca trainer Evan McAuliffe is aiming to keep the Irish St. Leger title in Limerick by defending his crown at the local greyhound stadium.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363437.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: What a Leger final in store at Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363623.headline: Ryanair announces new twice-weekly Shannon Airport service to Toulouse for Summer 2027
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363623.summary: Shannon Airport has welcomed a new Ryanair route to Toulouse, France, starting March 25, 2027. The twice-weekly service will operate on Mondays and Thursdays.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363623.story:
Passengers across the Mid-West will have direct access to the south-west of France following Ryanair's announcement of a new Summer 2027 service between Shannon Airport and Toulouse. The route will launch on March 25, 2027, operating twice weekly on Mondays and Thursdays.

The new connection to Toulouse—widely known as 'La Ville Rose' due to its distinct terracotta architecture—marks the second new Ryanair route announced for Shannon in recent weeks, following a previously announced service to Milan Bergamo. Both routes will take off in March 2027, collectively generating an estimated 50,000 additional seats for the airport's Summer programme.

Ray O’Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, said the announcement reflects strong regional demand and ongoing confidence from the airline. "Following our strongest route programme in 17 years, we are pleased to maintain this momentum as we continue to grow connectivity for the communities and businesses we serve," he said.

Ryanair’s Director of Communications, Jade Kirwan, added that the route offers customers across the region new options for both weekend city breaks and extended holidays. Declan Power, Head of Aviation Development at Shannon Airport, noted that Toulouse offers strong appeal for leisure and business travellers alike, serving as both a vibrant cultural centre and a major European aerospace hub.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363623.localAngle: The new route boosts international travel connectivity directly from Shannon Airport for passengers across Limerick and the wider Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363623.originalTitle: Up and away to Toulouse as new route announced for Shannon

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363532.headline: Limerick Council Agrees to Speed Survey on Old Dublin Road After Safety Complaints
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363532.summary: Limerick City and County Council has agreed to conduct a speed survey on the Old Dublin Road in Rhebogue following concerns from local residents and councillors over "ferocious" speeding and traffic rat-runs.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363532.story:
Limerick City and County Council has agreed to carry out a speed survey on the Old Dublin Road between the Parkway Roundabout and the service station near Colourworks Paint. The decision follows calls from Aontú Councillor Sarah Beasley at November’s Metropolitan District meeting for urgent traffic calming measures along the stretch.

Cllr Beasley told the meeting that she had been contacted by elderly residents who feel increasingly cut off near Limerick's busiest roundabout. She highlighted that two dogs and three family cats have been knocked down on the road, alongside two near-misses involving elderly residents, and pointed out that drivers speed down the hill as a cut-through from the roundabout.

The motion was seconded by Social Democrats Councillor Shane Hickey-O’Mara, while Independent Councillor Ursula described some of the motorists' speed as "ferocious". Councillors noted that the lack of parking around a local GP service forces drivers to park in the service station and attempt to cross the busy road on foot.

In response, Patricia Liddy, the Council’s Director of Transportation, Mobility, and Public Realm, confirmed that the Metropolitan Area Office will arrange the survey. She stated that the findings will be reviewed to assess vehicle speeds and determine whether traffic calming measures, such as speed ramps, are warranted under national guidance and Council policy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363532.localAngle: The story directly impacts motorists and residents navigating the Old Dublin Road and Parkway Roundabout in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363532.originalTitle: Rhebogue residents call for action on ‘ferocious’ speeding

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363600.headline: Indie Bands MJ ICE and Parliament Square Headline Dolans Kasbah
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363600.summary: Two rising Limerick indie bands will share the stage for a co-headline show at Dolans Kasbah this Saturday, November 21. Both acts aim to grow their fan base and support younger artists entering the local music industry.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363600.story:
Two of Limerick’s rising indie acts are joining forces this weekend for a high-profile local gig. MJ ICE and Parliament Square will take to the stage at Dolans Kasbah this Saturday, November 21, for a co-headline performance known for its energy and passion.

Led by Justice Mjr, MJ ICE will share the bill with Parliament Square, fronted by Brendon Markham. Both bands have built reputations for delivering passionate live performances and are eager to team up to expand their respective audiences.

Beyond their own performance, the bands hope the joint show will help open doors for upcoming young artists starting out in the music industry. The event highlights the collaborative spirit within the local independent music scene.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363600.localAngle: The gig showcases home-grown musical talent at one of Limerick's most popular live music venues.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363600.originalTitle: MJ ICE and Parliament Square to share the stage at Dolans Kasbah this Saturday

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363587.headline: Limerick rock band Puppets announce debut EP and single 'Pearl'
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363587.summary: University of Limerick students comprising the alternative rock band Puppets will release their debut single 'Pearl' this week ahead of a four-track EP early next year. The four-piece will also play a live show at Pharmacia on Thursday, November 19.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363587.story:
Limerick alternative rock band Puppets are preparing to release their debut single, 'Pearl', marking the official announcement of a four-track debut EP due for release early next year. 

The band consists of University of Limerick students Joshua Cottingham on vocals, Diarmuid Farrell on drums, JC Cusipag on guitar, and Taylor Ford on bass. Ahead of the single's release, the group is set to play a live show at Pharmacia on Thursday, November 19.

Earlier this year, Puppets sold out their first headline show at the Record Room before releasing any official music, following it up with support slots around Limerick. Their upcoming EP was entirely self-recorded and self-produced at the University of Limerick, with the members balancing the project alongside their degree studies under tight time constraints.

'Pearl' serves as the opening release from the project, designed to introduce the band's distinctive sound while leaving much of their wider musical range under wraps. The track builds from a restrained opening into a powerful climax, showcasing a blend of classic rock foundations, J-rock guitar work, blues, and jazz elements.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363587.localAngle: The band is made up of University of Limerick students who built their local following with sold-out shows in Limerick venues like the Record Room and Pharmacia.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363587.originalTitle: Limerick band Puppets announce debut EP with first single ‘Pearl’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363531.headline: Limerick LSAD to Host Remembrance Event for Magdalene Women on November 27
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363531.summary: Women’s Collective Ireland is reviving Limerick's annual Magdalene Women remembrance event at the former Good Shepherd convent and laundry on Clare Street. The free public event on November 27 will feature local historians, activists, and guest speakers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363531.story:
The former Good Shepherd convent and laundry on Clare Street will host a special event this month to honour the Magdalene Women of Limerick. Organised by Women’s Collective Ireland, the remembrance gathering takes place on Friday, November 27, in the building that now houses the Limerick School of Art and Design (LSAD).

The event marks the return of an annual local remembrance that was previously interrupted by the Covid-19 pandemic. Attendees will hear from a panel of guest speakers, including local author and historian Sharon Slater, who will discuss the history of the site, and activist and artist Evelyn Glynn, who has extensively researched Limerick's Good Shepherd laundry.

Maeve O’Rourke, a prominent figure in the Justice for Magdalenes Campaign who was involved in bringing cases before the European Court of Human Rights, the UN Committee against Torture, and the UN Human Rights Council, will also address attendees.

Yvie Murphy, Women’s Collective Ireland Limerick Coordinator, said the event is an opportunity to ensure this history is not forgotten. "We were approached by organisers of the annual remembrance... we are delighted to have the opportunity to acknowledge and honour Limerick’s Magdalene Women and to make sure our dark history and horrific treatment of women is not forgotten," she said.

The event begins at 12.30pm in the Church Gallery at LSAD. Admission is free, but places must be booked in advance via Eventbrite.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363531.localAngle: The event takes place at the former Good Shepherd convent and laundry in Limerick, directly addressing a painful chapter in the city's local history.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363531.originalTitle: Remembering the Magdalene Women of Limerick event to be held

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363571.headline: Dolans Opens Spiegeltent Pavilion on North Circular Road with Star-Studded Lineup
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363571.summary: Dolans has launched its winter live music season at the new Spiegeltent Pavilion opposite Cleeves, running a packed schedule of gigs from this Friday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363571.story:
A new winter live entertainment season kicks off this Friday as Dolans opens the Spiegeltent Pavilion on the North Circular Road, constructed just across the road from Cleeves.

Featuring an interior of mirrors, wood finishes, and rich textures, the pop-up venue opens its doors on Friday, November 20, with a performance by The Proclaimers.
