Local acts will also take centre stage, with Dylan Flynn And The Dead Poets headlining their biggest show yet on Saturday, November 21. The band recently signed with Nettwerk Music Group, reaching 190,000 monthly Spotify listeners following summer support slots with Maroon 5 and Bastille.

The jam-packed November programme continues with OTT Wrestling Live on Sunday, November 22, followed by songwriter Paul Brady on Wednesday, November 25, and impressionist Mario Rosenstock on Thursday, November 26. The Stunning will play on Friday, November 27, Ash bring their 1977 tour on Saturday, November 28, and mentalist Keith Barry performs on Sunday, November 29. After-show parties with DJs running late will also take place on Dolans Terrace every Friday and Saturday night.

Mick Dolan of Dolans stated that the ambition behind the project was to deliver "something genuinely special for Limerick during the winter months." He added: "Looking at the final line-up, I think we’ve achieved that."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363571.localAngle: The Spiegeltent Pavilion brings a major new winter entertainment venue and high-profile acts directly to Limerick's North Circular Road.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363571.originalTitle: A season of live music and events begins at Spiegeltent Pavilion this weekend

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363247.headline: Minister Kieran O'Donnell receives flu jab at University Hospital Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363247.summary: Limerick TD and Minister Kieran O'Donnell has received his annual flu vaccine at UHL as the HSE urges at-risk groups and older people to get vaccinated amid the current flu season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363247.story:
Limerick TD and Minister of State for Older People and Housing, Kieran O’Donnell, has received his annual flu vaccination at University Hospital Limerick. Minister O'Donnell was pictured getting his jab from UHL vaccinators Ann Noonan and Noelle Hurley as health authorities step up calls for the public to protect themselves.

With flu season now in full swing, the HSE is urging all older people and at-risk groups to make vaccination a top priority. Officials note that it takes up to two weeks for the vaccine to become effective, meaning early vaccination is strongly recommended for those eligible.

The flu vaccine is available free of charge to anyone aged 60 and older, as well as individuals with weakened immune systems or certain underlying medical conditions. Residents looking to receive the vaccine are advised to consult a participating GP or pharmacist, or visit the HSE website for further details.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363247.localAngle: Local TD and Minister Kieran O'Donnell received his vaccination at University Hospital Limerick to highlight the HSE's seasonal rollout for Limerick residents.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363247.originalTitle: Limerick Minister encourages people to take flu vaccine

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363610.headline: Mozart, Comedy, and The Proclaimers Headline Packed Limerick Arts Week
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363610.summary: Limerick's arts scene is bustling this week with performances from the Irish Chamber Orchestra at the University Concert Hall, The Proclaimers at the Spiegeltent Pavilion, and various theatre and comedy shows running across the city until November 26.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363610.story:
A busy week of live music, theatre, and cultural events is underway across Limerick, running from November 19 to November 26. Classical music enthusiasts can catch the Irish Chamber Orchestra alongside pianist Yeol Eum Son performing Mozart at the University Concert Hall this Friday, November 20. Violinist Anton Jablokov is also set to perform at the Belltable with pianist Adam I. Kuruc.

For music fans looking for other genres, The Proclaimers take to the stage at the Live at the Spiegeltent Pavilion on the North Circular Road, while venues across the city host events ranging from acoustic country at Charlie Malone’s to heavy guitar riffs at the Record Room. Theatre productions include the UL Drama Society's staging of 'The Minotaur' at the Luna Theatre and 'The Hunchback of Notre Dame' at the Lime Tree Theatre.

Comedy and literary events also feature prominently in the schedule. Comedian Aideen McQueen performs at Dolans, while O’Mahony’s Booksellers hosts an in-store conversation with authors Sharon Guard and June O’Sullivan. The packed programme offers a diverse mix of entertainment across city and county venues throughout the week.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363610.localAngle: The week-long programme of events spans multiple venues across Limerick city and county, including the University Concert Hall, Belltable, and Dolans.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363610.originalTitle: What’s On in Limerick: Live Music, Theatre, Comedy & Events | 19–26

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363583.headline: UL Drama Society stages original World War I Greek myth play
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363583.summary: The University of Limerick Drama Society is staging 'The Minotaur' at the Luna Theatre on November 18 and 19, blending ancient Greek legend with trench warfare.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363583.story:
The University of Limerick (UL) Drama Society is bringing its latest major production, 'The Minotaur', to the campus Student Centre this week. The original play runs in the Luna Theatre on Wednesday, November 18, and Thursday, November 19, with doors opening at 6.30pm on both evenings.

Written and staged entirely by the student society, the production recasts the classic Greek legend against the backdrop of First World War trench warfare. Organisers said the piece explores themes of sacrifice, obligation, and humanity during wartime hardship. The project is co-directed by H Soucie and Gwenna Spitzer, with Nour Hamdy producing a student cast and crew.

Soucie, who also penned the script, explained that the concept came from combining distinct creative interests. Behind the scenes, the student-led crew has built custom sets, sourced period-accurate costumes and props, and participated in stage combat and performance workshops to authentically portray battlefield realities.

Tickets for the two-night run are currently available through the UL Drama Society Linktree.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363583.localAngle: The production is entirely student-led and staged at the University of Limerick's campus theatre in Castletroy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363583.originalTitle: UL Drama Society brings Greek myth to First World War trenches with original play ‘The Minotaur’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363517.headline: Clonlara COPD patient regains independence after HSE Limerick care programme
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363517.summary: Teresa Madden credits the HSE Mid West Chronic Disease Management service for helping her ditch her wheelchair. She is now urging other long-term sufferers to use the local care hub ahead of winter.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363517.story:
A former Limerick resident who previously relied on a wheelchair has credited a local HSE health initiative with giving her life back. Teresa Madden, now based in Clonlara, was diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in 2015 and later referred by her GP to the HSE Mid West Chronic Disease Management service on Mulgrave Street in Limerick City.

The hub provides patients with respiratory nursing and physiotherapy clinical assessments, medication titration, airway clearance, and pulmonary rehabilitation under one roof. The initiative aims to bring specialist community care to patients in Limerick, Clare, and North Tipperary while reducing hospital admissions.

Marking World COPD Day, Ms Madden shared how the pulmonary rehabilitation classes transformed her mobility and confidence. "I had needed a wheelchair for so long and when I came out of the hub I managed to get out of the wheelchair," she said, praising the nursing staff for helping her regain her independence.

Dr Eithne Mulloy, Respiratory Consultant at University Hospital Limerick and the Community Chronic Disease Hub, noted that COPD affects up to one in 10 people over 40 in Ireland, with up to half of sufferers unaware of their diagnosis. She encouraged patients to use the community service, which sees GP referrals within a week or two. Nursing and physiotherapy staff, alongside the Limerick COPD Support Group, are hosting an informational stand at the Crescent Shopping Centre to offer advice to those managing the condition.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363517.localAngle: The HSE Chronic Disease Management hub operates out of Mulgrave Street in Limerick City, providing community-based respiratory care to patients across Limerick, Clare, and North Tipperary.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363517.originalTitle: HSE service helped Limerick COPD sufferer get out of her wheelchair

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53851.headline: Kilmallock’s Shane O’Brien and Ballybrown’s Aidan O’Connor lead Limerick’s next generation
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53851.summary: Following Limerick's 2026 All-Ireland hurling success, young talents Shane O'Brien and Aidan O'Connor are emerging to lead the county's next chapter under manager John Kiely.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53851.story:
As John Kiely’s side continues its dominance on the inter-county hurling scene after claiming another All-Ireland title in 2026, attention has turned to the players ready to carry on the legacy. With household names like Aaron Gillane, Cian Lynch, and Declan Hannon moving towards the latter stages of their careers, a new crop of young hurlers is stepping up.

Among them is 22-year-old Shane O'Brien of Kilmallock, who joined the Limerick senior panel in 2023. Operating in the full-forward line, O'Brien has earned praise from his club for his grounded attitude, pace, physicality, and eye for goal. Kilmallock GAA noted that the young forward brings "hunger, energy, fearlessness and a genuine desire to make a difference" to a squad of established winners.

Meanwhile, 24-year-old Aidan O’Connor from Ballybrown has established himself as an important half-forward during the 2026 season. Former coach Tiernan O’Neill described O'Connor as a player who marries incredible skill with a massive work ethic, cementing his place in the senior squad alongside O'Brien as Limerick plans for the future.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53851.localAngle: Local club hurlers Shane O'Brien of Kilmallock and Aidan O'Connor of Ballybrown are emerging as key players for the Limerick senior hurling team.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53851.originalTitle: Limerick’s next generation: The young hurlers carrying on the legacy

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363537.headline: Gardaí issue security warning following recent tool thefts in Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363537.summary: Limerick Gardaí are investigating a series of tool thefts from a van in Adare and a construction site on the Dock Road. Officers have urged local tradespeople to secure their vehicles and avoid leaving valuables in plain sight.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363537.story:
Gardaí in Limerick are investigating a number of tool thefts across the county following separate incidents reported in recent weeks. 

Tools were stolen from a van parked at a hotel in Adare on October 30 between 3.15pm and 3.30pm. In a separate incident between October 24 and 27, power tools were taken from a construction site on the Dock Road in Limerick City, according to Sergeant Michelle O’Halloran.

Following the incidents, Sergeant O’Halloran has urged tradespeople across the county to always lock their vehicles and avoid leaving spare keys or valuables in obvious locations. She also advised workers to choose well-lit areas covered by CCTV where possible when parking near jobs or work sites.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363537.localAngle: The thefts and subsequent Garda warnings directly impact tradespeople and construction workers operating across Limerick city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363537.originalTitle: Gardaí investigating tool thefts in Limerick

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53861.headline: Granagh Community Centre to Host Floral Painting Workshop with Carol Ahern and Aly Harte
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53861.summary: Limerick artist Carol Ahern and Belfast painter Aly Harte are hosting their 'Loosen Up Your Floral Painting' day-long workshop at Granagh Community Centre on November 29.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53861.story: Paintbrushes, colour palettes and creative conversations will fill the rural community centre for the upcoming event led by the two artists. Readers can view the full story on Limerick Voice.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53861.localAngle: The workshop takes place at Granagh Community Centre and is co-hosted by Limerick artist Carol Ahern.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53861.originalTitle: Artists Carol Ahern and Aly Harte bring floral painting workshop to Granagh Community Centre

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363535.headline: Mid West homeless children figures surge to 435 in emergency accommodation
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363535.summary: The number of homeless children across Limerick and Clare rose to 435 in September, while overall regional homelessness climbed to 809. Limerick alone accounted for 702 people in emergency accommodation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363535.story:
The number of children experiencing homelessness in Limerick and Clare has increased significantly over the past year, with 435 children recorded in emergency accommodation in September 2026. This compares to 269 children recorded in emergency accommodation during the same month in 2025.

Across the Mid West region, the total number of homeless people reached 809 in September, up from 619 in September 2025. In Limerick specifically, the number of people in emergency accommodation rose to 702 from 543 the previous year, while the number of homeless families in the region climbed from 163 to 233.

Nationally, Department of Housing figures showed the total number of homeless people topped 18,000 for the first time, reaching 18,065 in September. These figures include nearly 6,000 children across the country, though they exclude rough sleepers and individuals accessing domestic violence refuges.

Focus Ireland Director of Advocacy Mike Allen attributed the ongoing rise to difficulties people face in exiting homelessness. Speaking on RTÉ’s Morning Ireland, Mr Allen said the capacity for people to leave homelessness has declined because individuals are less able to transition to the private rented sector without increased government subsidies.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363535.localAngle: The figures highlight a sharp rise in family and child homelessness specifically impacting Limerick and Clare.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363535.originalTitle: 435 children homeless in the Mid West

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363538.headline: Limerick TD Conor Sheehan demands immediate publication of HAP rent limit review
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363538.summary: Labour TD Conor Sheehan is calling on the Housing Minister to publish a delayed review of Housing Assistance Payment limits and set a date for increases. The demand follows new figures showing that nearly three-quarters of HAP tenancies nationwide rely on discretionary top-ups.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363538.story:
Labour TD for Limerick City Conor Sheehan has called on the Housing Minister to immediately publish the Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) rent limits review and establish a firm date for increases. 

The demand follows newly revealed figures showing that 72.4 per cent of HAP tenancies across the country currently receive a discretionary top-up. 

"When almost three in four HAP tenancies need a discretionary top-up, the HAP limits must be urgently reviewed. What was meant to give councils some flexibility has become the way they keep most HAP tenancies within reach," Deputy Sheehan said.

The Limerick TD added that the Government has failed to deliver an adequate supply of social and affordable homes. He noted that while HAP was originally introduced as a temporary measure, a persistent lack of State housing investment has turned it into the default system rather than an exception.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363538.localAngle: Limerick Labour TD Conor Sheehan is demanding national housing policy changes to address how the HAP system impacts renters locally and nationwide.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363538.originalTitle: Limerick TD calls for Government to publish HAP rent limit review

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363542.headline: Film in Limerick launches free winter workshops in producing, screenwriting and directing
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363542.summary: Emerging filmmakers in Limerick can now apply for three free training workshops taking place across November and December as part of the Engine Shorts scheme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363542.story:
Aspiring filmmakers across Limerick have been given a boost with the launch of three free workshops focusing on producing, screenwriting, and directing. Running through November and December, the sessions are designed to support local talent looking to break into the industry.

The training initiative is being delivered by Film in Limerick in partnership with local authorities in Limerick, Clare, and Tipperary, alongside the Limerick and Clare Education and Training Board. The workshops form part of the wider Engine Shorts Film Training and Production Scheme.

Organisers have noted that the sessions are particularly recommended for creatives considering applying for funding to produce a short film through the Engine Shorts scheme or other similar funding programmes. 

All workshops are completely free to attend and are open to emerging filmmakers aged 18 and over. Applications are currently open, with further information and application forms available directly through the Engine scheme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363542.localAngle: The workshops are part of a regional initiative delivered in partnership with Limerick City and County Council and the Limerick and Clare Education and Training Board to support local filmmakers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363542.originalTitle: Free filmmaking workshops in Limerick this winter

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363552.headline: Zero Affordable Homes Delivered in Limerick City West and North in Five Years
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363552.summary: Figures revealed at a Limerick Council meeting show that all 41 affordable purchase homes delivered across the city's three electoral areas in the past five years went to Limerick City East, with neither City West nor City North receiving any.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363552.story:
Just 41 affordable purchase homes have been delivered across the three Limerick City electoral areas over the past five years, figures provided by Limerick City and County Council have confirmed.

Revealed at November’s Metropolitan District Meeting, the data shows that every single one of those 41 homes was located in Limerick City East. Neither Limerick City West nor Limerick City North saw a single affordable purchase home delivered during the five-year period. Furthermore, Limerick City West is not currently projected to receive its first affordable homes until 2028, with no units scheduled for 2027.

Fine Gael councillor Dan McSweeney described the figures as extremely disappointing and frustrating, pointing out that despite significant residential developments in areas like Mungret, Raheen, and Patrickswell, no families have been able to buy an affordable home through the scheme in City West.

Cllr McSweeney contrasted Limerick's output with Waterford City and County Council, which delivered 204 affordable purchase homes from an original target of 76 during the same timeframe. He called on the local authority to work closely with the Department of Housing, private developers, and the Land Development Agency to accelerate delivery across the Metropolitan District.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363552.localAngle: The figures highlight a stark disparity in affordable housing delivery across Limerick City's electoral areas, directly impacting families trying to get on the property ladder locally.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363552.originalTitle: Not a single Affordable Purchase Home delivered in Limerick City West or North since scheme introduced

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53875.headline: Former Boxer Jonathan O’Brien Pays Emotional Tribute to Late Friend Lee Reeves
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53875.summary: Former boxer and trainer Jonathan O’Brien has paid an emotional tribute to his close friend Lee Reeves, who died at University Hospital Limerick on November 16 following a critical brain injury.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53875.story:
For almost three months, Jonathan O’Brien served as a vital source of information for a Limerick community following the condition of boxer Lee Reeves. Following Reeves' death at University Hospital Limerick on November 16, O'Brien spoke of his heartbreak, admitting he broke down several times while recording a tribute to the 31-year-old.

Reeves suffered a critical brain injury during his August 1 bout against Gary Cully at Dublin’s 3Arena. Throughout his hospitalisation, O’Brien kept the public informed. Reflecting on that period, he said: “We screamed out for Lee, we were fighting for him, we were his voice. It wasn’t the outcome we were all looking for.”

O’Brien thanked the medical staff at the hospitals who cared for Reeves, as well as the public for their messages and contributions to a GoFundMe campaign established to support the family. He described Reeves as a young man who left a lasting positive impact on those around him.

Reeves will be laid to rest on Friday, November 20, following funeral arrangements at Our Lady Queen of Peace Church in Limerick, where he will be honoured with full military honours.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53875.localAngle: Lee Reeves was a 31-year-old from Limerick who passed away at University Hospital Limerick and will be laid to rest in the city.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53875.originalTitle: ‘We were his voice’ as Jonathan O’Brien pays emotional tribute to Lee Reeves

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363541.headline: Castletroy Park Hotel hosts Construction Industry Federation Mid West conference
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363541.summary: Government figures, industry leaders, and State agencies gather at the Castletroy Park Hotel on November 20 for the Construction Industry Federation’s Mid West Construct event, opened by Minister Kieran O’Donnell.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363541.story:
Government figures, industry leaders, and State agency decision makers from across the Mid West region gathered at the Castletroy Park Hotel on November 20 for the Construction Industry Federation’s Mid West Construct event. Minister Kieran O’Donnell officially opened the conference, which focused on exploring the construction sector’s most urgent challenges and opportunities.

A key address at the event was delivered by Iarnród Éireann (Irish Rail) CEO Mary Considine. The former Shannon Airport Group leader provided a strategic overview of Irish Rail’s ongoing developments and emphasized the critical role of transport connectivity in driving regional economic growth.

Discussions throughout the day centered heavily on regional development and housing. Delegates examined housing prospects for 2027, strategies for financing the future of housing, and insights shared by local authorities, the Housing Agency, and Uisce Éireann.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363541.localAngle: The conference brings key national and regional decision-makers to Limerick's Castletroy Park Hotel to address local housing and construction challenges.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363541.originalTitle: Limerick to host Mid West Construct conference

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53872.headline: Fairview Rangers Lead Premier League as FAI Junior Cup Action Heats Up
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53872.summary: Fairview Rangers top the Limerick District Premier League standings while local clubs battle through a busy weekend of FAI Junior Cup fixtures.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53872.story:
Fairview Rangers currently set the pace at the summit of the Premier League, holding a lead over Geraldines and Aisling Annacotty who remain in hot pursuit. Meanwhile, Corbally United lead the charge in the Premier A division, closely tracked by Hyde Rangers, Caherdavin Celtic, and Charleville. In division 1A, Pike Rovers B hold a healthy advantage at the top of the table ahead of chasing sides Cappamore, Holycross, and Ballynanty Rovers B. Aisling Annacotty’s D side face strong pressure from Caherconlish and Kilmallock United B in division 1B after nine games played.

Domestic league action took a backseat over the weekend as the FAI Junior Cup took centre stage. Pike Rovers delivered a commanding performance to hit ten goals past Shelbourne, while Regional United were forced into extra time before overcoming Ballynanty Rovers. Other sides to advance in Sunday's fixtures included Aisling Annacotty, Geraldines, Nenagh, Kilmallock, Summerville Rovers, Star Rovers, and Mungret Regional.

The cup fixtures brought an end to the run for several local teams. Hyde Rangers, Brazuca United, Herbertstown, Carew Park, Patrickswell, Murroe, and Corbally United all bowed out of the competition and will now turn their full attention back to their respective league campaigns. The cup action concludes its latest round on Thursday evening when Fairview Rangers face Newport Town.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53872.localAngle: The report covers the latest standings and cup results across Limerick's district soccer leagues and clubs.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53872.originalTitle: Limerick District Leagues taking shape with title races heating up

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363568.headline: Ballet Ireland Brings Romeo & Juliet to Limerick's Lime Tree Theatre
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363568.summary: Ballet Ireland will stage its production of Romeo & Juliet at the Lime Tree Theatre on Thursday, November 26, featuring Prokofiev's score and choreography exploring the Shakespearean tragedy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363568.story:
Theatregoers in Limerick will have the chance to see Ballet Ireland's production of Romeo & Juliet when it comes to the Lime Tree Theatre on Thursday, November 26.

Set to Sergei Prokofiev’s score, the production portrays the story of the star-crossed lovers against a backdrop of ancient feuds and gang warfare. The company describes the performance as a blend of choreography and emotion, following the pair as they defy their families.

The performance begins at 7.30pm. Tickets are priced at €32 or €27, with a family ticket available for €90 covering two adults and two children. 

Ballet Ireland’s tour of the production is sponsored by EY, with support from RTÉ Supporting the Arts.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363568.localAngle: The acclaimed dance production is coming to Limerick's Lime Tree Theatre for a single night performance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363568.originalTitle: Ballet Ireland to perform Romeo & Juliet at Lime Tree Theatre

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363562.headline: Limerick Milk Market unveils month-long Christmas programme with Santa and local crafts
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363562.summary: The Limerick Milk Market will run a festive programme featuring Santa visits, live music, and local craft stalls from November 28 to December 24. Events include charity fundraisers, pet-friendly photo sessions, and artisan markets.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363562.story:
The historic heart of Limerick is getting ready for the festive season as the Milk Market announces its comprehensive Christmas programme, running on select dates from Saturday, November 28, to Thursday, December 24.

Opening weekend kicks off at 8am on November 28 with a charity Santa raising funds for Limerick Suicide Watch, accompanied by Christmas elves from Fidget Feet and a market featuring local food and crafts. The schedule also includes a "Santa Paws" event on November 29 for pet owners, a Christmas Cupcake Day on December 4 supporting Rising Together Training Centre, and the return of the Festive Food and Craft Market on December 5 with over 80 traders.

Further highlights across the month include a Christmas Art Fair on December 6, a Transition Year student enterprise market on December 11, a free Boherbuoy Band concert on December 13, and a sensory Santa's grotto paired with an open-air car showroom by Lyons of Limerick on December 18. The seasonal series will wrap up with a final market on Christmas Eve from 8am to 2pm.

Milk Market manager David Fitzgerald expressed enthusiasm for the upcoming events. “We’re thrilled to welcome everyone back for another magical Christmas series. Our community spirit, local food and festive atmosphere make the market a truly special place to celebrate Christmas in Limerick,” he said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363562.localAngle: The Limerick Milk Market serves as a central festive hub for the city, bringing together local traders, charities, and families throughout December.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363562.originalTitle: Limerick Milk Market Christmas Programme brings Santa, live music and local crafts to the city

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363603.headline: Limerick author marks 176th anniversary of Kilkee emigrant ship disaster in new book
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363603.summary: Limerick writer Maureen Sparling has released a new book commemorating the 1850 wreck of the emigrant vessel Edmond, which claimed 98 lives after setting sail from Limerick for New York.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363603.story:
Limerick writer Maureen Sparling has drawn on one of the region's most tragic maritime histories for her new book, *Mystery at Sykes House – A Tribute to Kilkee*, which marks the 176th anniversary of the sinking of the emigrant vessel Edmond.

The ship, travelling from Limerick towards New York with 216 people on board, was driven into Kilkee Bay during a violent Atlantic storm on the night of November 19, 1850. The vessel struck the rocks near Sykes House and broke apart, resulting in the deaths of 98 passengers and crew.

In the aftermath of the disaster, local residents mounted an immediate rescue response. Richard Russell opened Sykes House to survivors, while others in Kilkee provided food, shelter, and assistance. The site of the wreck subsequently became known as Edmond Point.

Sparling's book, launched in Kilkee during the summer as part of the Kilkee Civic Trust programme, features a novella following characters Nell and Daniel against the backdrop of the tragedy. It also includes local stories, memories, poetry, and reflections, and is available online via Buythebook.ie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363603.localAngle: The book examines the legacy of the emigrant vessel Edmond, which departed from Limerick carrying local passengers before its tragic wreck in 1850.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363603.originalTitle: Remembering the Edmond: 176 years since the Kilkee tragedy

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363706.headline: Tributes paid following the passing of Limerick darts figure Tony Hickey
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363706.summary: Tony Hickey, affectionately known as 'Mr Darts' across Limerick and the wider Irish sporting community, has passed away at the age of 82. Tributes have poured in from world champions and local players alike following his death on Wednesday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363706.story:
Tributes have been paid across the sporting world following the death of Tony Hickey, a familiar face in the Limerick darts community from Ballinacurra Weston and Pennywell. Known widely as 'Mr Darts', he passed away peacefully on Wednesday, November 18, at Riverdale Nursing Home in Ardnacrusha, surrounded by his family.

The Irish National Darts Organisation led the tributes, describing him as a true gentleman and a tremendous ambassador who travelled the length and breadth of Ireland to support players at all levels, from grassroots events to the national calendar. International figures also shared their condolences, including 16-time World Champion Phil Taylor and local professional player William 'The Magpie' O'Connor, who remembered him for his friendship, humour, and dedication to the sport.

Mr Hickey is survived by his daughter Celine, son-in-law Gordon, grandchildren Emily, Naoise, Zachary, and Ethan, alongside his extended family, friends, and the wider darts community. 

His remains will repose at Cross’s Funeral Home on Lower Gerald Griffin Street on Friday from 5pm to 6.30pm. His Requiem Mass will take place at St John’s Cathedral at 11am the following morning, followed by burial at Mount St Oliver Cemetery.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363706.localAngle: Tony Hickey was a well-known local figure from Ballinacurra Weston and Pennywell who made a lasting impact on the Limerick and national darts communities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363706.originalTitle: The passing of ‘Mr Darts’ Tony Hickey

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53898.headline: Mary Immaculate student society MIDAS debuts at Belltable with 90-minute play 'Clue'
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53898.summary: The Mary Immaculate Dramatic Arts Society is staging its debut Belltable Theatre production with a two-night run of the murder mystery comedy 'Clue', concluding tonight.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53898.story:
The Mary Immaculate Dramatic Arts Society (MIDAS) is making its debut at the Belltable Theatre with a two-night run of the murder mystery play 'Clue'. Opening night took place on November 18, with the final performance scheduled for this evening, Thursday, November 19, with doors opening at 8pm.

Based on the 1985 film and the Cluedo board game, the 90-minute production marks a significant step up for the student society, which typically performs 45-minute pieces. Cast member Scott Callaghan, who plays Colonel Mustard, noted that moving to the Belltable is a major milestone for MIDAS. Rehearsals for the ambitious, fast-paced show have run up to four days a week since the start of November.

The production features a six-person dinner guest cast alongside physical comedy, quick exchanges, and atmospheric lighting and sound design. Following positive audience reactions on opening night, the student cast and crew return to the Belltable stage for the final performance of the run tonight.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53898.localAngle: The Mary Immaculate Dramatic Arts Society is staging its debut production at Limerick's Belltable Theatre.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53898.originalTitle: REVIEW: From the lounge to the library, relive the mystery of MIDAS’s new play ‘Clue’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363546.headline: Limerick Enable Ireland shop launches Christmas toy and decoration donation drive
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363546.summary: Enable Ireland's shop on Honan's Quay is asking Limerick families to donate pre-loved toys and Christmas decorations to fund local disability services. All profits from the holiday items will go directly toward supporting the charity's services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363546.story:
A Limerick charity shop is calling on local families to donate pre-loved toys and Christmas decorations in the run-up to the festive season. The Enable Ireland shop located on Honan's Quay launched the appeal to turn forgotten items into festive finds to help support the organization's disability services.

One hundred per cent of the profits generated from the sale of the donated toys and decorations will go directly toward funding vital disability services provided by Enable Ireland across the country.

As part of the 'Pass Christmas On' campaign, anyone who makes a donation to the Honan's Quay shop will also be automatically entered into a raffle for a chance to win a Christmas hamper.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363546.localAngle: The fundraising campaign takes place at the Enable Ireland shop on Honan's Quay in Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363546.originalTitle: Enable helping turn forgotten favourites into festive finds for Christmas

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363554.headline: O'Donovan Urges Limerick Council to Adopt Five-Step Active Travel Consultation
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363554.summary: Social Democrats councillor Elisa O'Donovan has called for the immediate implementation of a structured five-step consultation process for Active Travel schemes across Limerick city. Council officials have agreed to deliver a presentation to Metropolitan District members on the framework's ongoing rollout.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363554.story:
Social Democrats councillor Elisa O'Donovan has pressed Limerick City and County Council to immediately enforce a five-step non-statutory consultation process for Active Travel projects throughout the city. The framework was originally devised by the Council's Active Travel team alongside the Travel and Transportation Strategic Policy Committee (SPC) in December 2023.

Speaking at the November meeting of the Metropolitan District, Cllr O'Donovan stated she has repeatedly raised concerns regarding a lack of community consultation on local Active Travel schemes. She emphasized the need for a transparent process ensuring early engagement with residents and stakeholders, option examinations, public submissions, and further information sharing before statutory procedures begin. "If we genuinely want to bring people together and communities together and bring them along on better pedestrian and cycling infrastructure, we have to start with meaningful communication and engagement," she said.

Her party colleague, Cllr Shane Hickey-O'Mara, seconded the proposal, arguing that abandoning established frameworks leaves the Council isolated and residents uninformed. In response, Patricia Liddy, the Council's Director of Transportation, Mobility, and Public Realm, welcomed the notice of motion. She confirmed that the Active Travel team will schedule a presentation for Metropolitan District members to discuss the consultation process and its implementation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363554.localAngle: The proposed consultation process directly impacts residential communities across Limerick city where pedestrian and cycling infrastructure projects are planned.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363554.originalTitle: Call for Limerick Council to implement five-step Active Travel consultation process

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363424.headline: Limerick locals brave the Christmas chill as weekend social scenes captured on Treaty streets
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363424.summary: Photographer Brendan Gleeson captured locals enjoying the weekend atmosphere across Limerick City as festive temperatures began to set in. Residents were spotted out and about at local spots including the Locke Bar and Mother Mac's.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363424.story:
As the winter weather begins to settle over the Treaty City, locals have been spotted making the most of the weekend atmosphere. Photographer Brendan Gleeson was out capturing the celebratory scenes across Limerick as the seasonal chill arrived.

Among those snapped enjoying the weekend across the city were Aoife Rhatigan, Aine Moloney, and Diarmuid Layden. Also spotted taking in the early festive air were Isobel, Mike, Alisona, and Neil Heffernan.

The camera also caught Deirdre and Theresa Lynott, alongside Daniel Lynch and Serena Stewart, as they made their way around local establishments including the Locke Bar and Mother Mac's.

The series of snapshots offers a glimpse into everyday life on the city's streets as the community transitions into the winter months. Locals who recognise friends or family members in the published photographs are being encouraged to share the images.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363424.localAngle: The photos capture familiar faces enjoying popular social spots across Limerick City centre as winter sets in.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363424.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Out and about in Limerick City

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363513.headline: Dromin/Athlacca and Caherline Reach Munster Hurling Finals
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363513.summary: Limerick clubs Dromin/Athlacca and Caherline have advanced to their respective Munster hurling finals following semi-final victories over Clarecastle and Dr Crokes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363513.story:
Limerick hurling supporters have two Munster finals to look forward to the weekend after next after Dromin/Athlacca and Caherline secured provincial final berths.

At Fitzgerald Park in Kilmallock, James Kennedy-tutored Dromin/Athlacca edged past Clarecastle on a scoreline of 1-20 to 0-22 in a lively intermediate semi-final. The winners were propelled by the dependable David Reidy, who contributed 0-10, alongside a 1-3 haul from prolific goal scorer Jack Fitzgibbon and contributions from Cian Scully. On the eve of the club's 75th anniversary, Dromin/Athlacca will now face Tipperary's St Mary's of Clonmel in the decider on November 29.

In the junior semi-final at Fr Hayes Park in Caherconlish, Caherline comfortably defeated Killarney's Dr Crokes 2-20 to 0-13. Hugh Murnane led the scoring for the Limerick side with 2-5, while man-of-the-match Andrew Brennan added 0-6. Mike Hickey's team will meet Cork's Kilshannig in the silver anniversary final on November 28.

Meanwhile, in the senior semi-final, Kilmallock's provincial campaign came to an end following a 1-20 to 1-11 defeat to All-Ireland champions Ballygunner at Walsh Park in Waterford. A crucial double-save from Conor Hanley-Clarke kept Kilmallock in contention before a late scoring burst from the Waterford side. Elsewhere, Patrickswell has been confirmed as Limerick's representative in the provincial Junior B Championship Tournament, which Killeedy will host in the New Year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363513.localAngle: Limerick clubs Dromin/Athlacca, Caherline, Kilmallock, and Patrickswell are all featured in major Munster club hurling championship fixtures and provincial tournaments.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363513.originalTitle: Tasty finals ahead in Munster Club Hurling C’ship

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53902.headline: University Concert Hall Wins Limerick Chamber Regional Business Award for Third Time
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53902.summary: University Concert Hall has won the Customer Experience Excellence Award at the Limerick Chamber Regional Business Awards for the third consecutive year. The achievement follows the venue's recent Creative Access Award win in September.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53902.story:
University Concert Hall (UCH) has taken home the Customer Experience Excellence Award at the Limerick Chamber Regional Business Awards for the third year in a row. The win marks a significant milestone for the Midwest’s largest concert venue, recognizing the collective efforts of staff across box office, front-of-house, administration, marketing, and technical departments.

Interim Director Máire Logue congratulated staff on the achievement and paid tribute to outgoing Director Sinéad Hope, who departed last week after more than 13 years at the helm. Administration Manager Marie Healy, who has served at UCH for over 28 years, noted that the venue also picked up the Creative Access Award this past September.

Staff pointed to practical changes driven by audience feedback, such as earlier door openings and the provision of booster seats, as key factors in improving the customer experience. UCH has also focused on accessibility under Programming and Business Development Manager Jennifer Flewett, introducing dementia-friendly concerts through a partnership with Music & Health Ireland and adding captioning to cinema screenings.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53902.localAngle: The University Concert Hall is the Midwest’s largest concert venue, serving the local Limerick community through music, theatre, and cultural events.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53902.originalTitle: Three times the applause: UCH takes home business award for third consecutive year

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363629.headline: Troy Studios Managing Director Elaine Geraghty to Step Down in December
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363629.summary: Elaine Geraghty is stepping down as managing director of Limerick's Troy Studios and Ardmore Studios at the end of December 2026 after six years in the role. A global search is underway for her successor, while Geraghty will stay on temporarily as a strategic advisor.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363629.story:
Elaine Geraghty is stepping down from her role as managing director of both Troy Studios in Limerick and Ardmore Studios in Wicklow at the end of December 2026. Her departure marks the end of a successful tenure that formed part of a 30-year leadership career across Ireland's media, broadcasting, and screen production sectors.

Since taking the helm in autumn 2020, Geraghty has overseen significant infrastructure expansions at both campuses and helped solidify Ireland's position on the global production map. Among her key achievements was orchestrating a landmark €10 million, multi-year agreement with independent production company BiggerStage to establish a state-of-the-art global television production hub at the Limerick facility, backed by Ireland's unscripted tax credit.

"It has been an absolute privilege to lead Ardmore Studios and Troy Studios during a transformative period for the Irish creative screen sector," Ms Geraghty said. "I am incredibly proud of what we have built alongside Hackman Capital and our teams at The MBS Group, who operate and service these iconic studios."

Alastair Boucaut, Executive Vice President of Hackman Capital’s global studio team, thanked Geraghty for her vision and dedication in elevating the two studio hubs into internationally revered production ecosystems. A global executive search is currently underway to find her successor. To ensure an orderly transition, Geraghty will be retained as a strategic advisor to support the recruitment and onboarding of the new managing director while providing continued guidance to both studios.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363629.localAngle: The departure of managing director Elaine Geraghty directly impacts Limerick's Troy Studios, a major local employer and production hub for the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363629.originalTitle: Irish film business legend steps down at Troy

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363713.headline: Investigation Underway After 25-Year-Old Man Found Dead in Limerick Prison Cell
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363713.summary: Keith Craughwell was found unresponsive at the Mulgrave Street facility on Thursday evening. Paramedics pronounced him dead at the scene, with foul play currently not suspected.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363713.story:
An investigation has been launched by the Irish Prison Service following the death of a 25-year-old inmate at Limerick Prison.

Guards and paramedics rushed to the Mulgrave Street facility shortly before 5pm on Thursday (November 19) after the man was discovered unresponsive in his cell. Despite the arrival of emergency services, he was pronounced dead at the scene.

The man has been named locally as Keith Craughwell, originally from Athlone, County Westmeath. He had been serving a two-year and seven-month sentence after being convicted of robbery-related offences at Mullingar Circuit Criminal Court.

A spokesperson for the Irish Prison Service confirmed the death in custody at the Limerick male prison. Authorities stated that while foul play is not suspected, standard procedures will be followed. All deaths in custody are subject to independent investigations by the Irish Prison Service, An Garda Síochána, and the Office of the Inspector of Prisons, with the final cause of death to be determined by the Coroner's Office.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363713.localAngle: The incident occurred at Limerick Prison on Mulgrave Street in the city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363713.originalTitle: Investigation launched after prisoner found dead at Limerick Prison

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53918.headline: €3m Secured to Refurbish Limerick's Historic Theatre Royal on Cecil Street
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53918.summary: Approximately €3m has been allocated to restore the historic Theatre Royal on Cecil Street. Limerick Twenty Thirty will manage the project following an agreement with Mayor John Moran.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53918.story:
Plans to restore Limerick’s historic Theatre Royal have taken a major step forward with approximately €3m identified for the refurbishment of the Cecil Street venue. The funding details were revealed by Councillor Maria Donoghue following a question at a Metropolitan District meeting this week.

The project will be managed by Limerick Twenty Thirty under an agreement with Mayor John Moran, with a significant portion of the funding drawn from this year’s Mayoral Fund. Cllr Donoghue confirmed that the development is currently undergoing feasibility work, investigative surveys, and emergency repairs, alongside the procurement of an architect-led multidisciplinary design team and planning consultant.

Work has already begun on the site, though temporary cultural use of the building will continue where appropriate. Further funding applications are anticipated as the long-term redevelopment progresses over the coming years.

The 19th-century landmark, which originally opened as the Limerick Athenaeum and later operated as the Royal Cinema, has a storied past hosting major acts from The Cranberries to Billy Connolly, as well as serving as a filming location for ‘Father Ted’. After decades of closure, the venue recently welcomed audiences back in October 2025 for a production celebrating Limerick-born Hollywood actress Constance Smith.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53918.localAngle: The refurbishment breathes new life into a landmark Limerick cultural venue with over 170 years of local history.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53918.originalTitle: €3m identified for refurbishment of Limerick’s historic Theatre Royal

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363627.headline: Councillors urge NTA to include Castleconnell and Annacotty in Limerick BusConnects
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363627.summary: Independent councillor Ursula Gavan has called on the NTA to extend BusConnects to Castleconnell and Annacotty. Metropolitan District councillors backed the motion and expanded it to include Patrickswell, Clarina, and Mungret.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363627.story:
Limerick councillors have called on the National Transport Authority (NTA) to expand the upcoming BusConnects network to include Castleconnell and Annacotty. Raising the issue at November’s Metropolitan District meeting, Independent councillor Ursula Gavan argued that the fast-growing areas have been left behind in public transport planning despite significant population and business growth.

Cllr Gavan pointed out that the current lack of a proper service leaves thousands of residents, students, and workers—including over 3,000 employees in the Annacotty Business Park—entirely reliant on cars. She noted that Montpelier has been without a bus service since COVID-19, and called for an hourly service to help ease daily traffic congestion around the Mackey roundabout. "The present timetable has gaping holes with workers and students resorting to travel by car, adding to the logjam," she said.

Social Democrats councillor Elisa O’Donovan seconded the motion, acknowledging that while Limerick City West is better served, areas like Castleconnell and Annacotty urgently need prioritisation. Following the discussion, councillors agreed to amend the proposal to also incorporate Patrickswell, Clarina, and Mungret into the joint call for better suburban transport connections.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363627.localAngle: The motion addresses public transport gaps and traffic congestion affecting commuters travelling into Limerick city from surrounding suburbs and villages.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363627.originalTitle: Limerick councillor calls for Castleconnell/Annacotty inclusion in Bus Connects

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53905.headline: Treaty United Attendances Fall 28% as League of Ireland Crosses One Million
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53905.summary: Treaty United averaged 738 supporters per game in the Men’s First Division this season, marking a 28 percent drop from the previous year. Nationally, League of Ireland attendances surpassed one million for the third consecutive season.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53905.story:
Treaty United saw a notable decline in home support during the 2026 season, with average attendances in the Men’s First Division falling by almost 28 percent. The Limerick club recorded an average of 738 supporters per game, down from 1,022 in 2025—a decrease of 284 supporters per match.

Meanwhile, the club's Women’s Premier Division side averaged 226 supporters per game, placing them sixth in their division. Bohemians topped the women's league with an average of 521 attendees.

The figures, released by the League of Ireland on Monday, November 16, show that total attendances across all national competitions reached 1,053,947 for the 2026 season. This marks the third consecutive year that national league attendances have exceeded the one-million milestone.

Across the Men’s First Division, combined attendances reached 167,091—up seven percent from 155,259 in 2025—with an average of 894 per game. The Men’s Premier Division remained the highest-attended competition, drawing 645,694 spectators across the season, led by Shamrock Rovers with an average home attendance of 5,921.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53905.localAngle: Treaty United's home attendances at Markets Field experienced a significant drop as national league figures crossed the one million mark for the third year running.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53905.originalTitle: Treaty United attendances contribute to League of Ireland’s million milestone

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363621.headline: Family of Jeffrey Hannan issue fresh appeal 19 years after Southill murder
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363621.summary: The family of 19-year-old Jeffrey Hannan have renewed calls for information on the 19th anniversary of his murder in Southill. No one has ever been charged for the killing, despite Gardaí making over 20 arrests.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363621.story:
Nineteen years after 19-year-old Jeffrey Hannan was bludgeoned to death with an axe in Limerick, his family have made a fresh public appeal for information to bring his killer to justice. Mr Hannan was attacked on November 22, 2007, as he attended a bonfire near his home at O’Malley Park in Southill. He sustained at least 10 blows to the head, and his body was dragged across a green area.

Despite Gardaí making more than 20 arrests and submitting a file to the Director of Public Prosecutions over the last nearly two decades, no charges have ever been brought in connection with the killing. Investigators believe the innocent teenager, who had no links to crime, was attacked in front of several witnesses while walking home from a house party.

Speaking ahead of the anniversary, the victim's father, Alan Hannan, urged anyone with knowledge of the night's events to come forward to Gardaí at any station in Ireland. He stated that Gardaí have indicated further information is needed to resubmit an investigation file to the DPP. The victim's 20-year-old daughter, Nikita Hannan, who was a toddler when her father died, also pleaded for witnesses to speak up.

"I’m begging people who know what happened to contact the guards, I’m just looking for someone to tell the Gardaí what happened," she said. While repeated family requests for a cold case review have been unsuccessful, local Gardaí have conducted a peer review of the case.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363621.localAngle: The murder and the ongoing campaign for justice centre on the O'Malley Park area of Southill in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363621.originalTitle: ‘I wish I could have had more time with my father’: Family of murdered Jeffrey Hannan appeal for witnesses to come forward on 19th anniversary

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363564.headline: UCH aims to give 1,500 children free panto tickets this Christmas
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363564.summary: The University Concert Hall is calling for public and business support to reach its goal of providing 1,500 free tickets for 'Jack & the Beanstalk' to local children and families. Every donation made to the Panto For All campaign is matched by UCH and Specsavers Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363564.story:
The University Concert Hall (UCH) has launched an appeal for charities, community groups, businesses, and the public to help fund free panto tickets for local children and families this Christmas.

The venue aims to reach a milestone of 1,500 total beneficiaries through its Panto For All campaign by the end of this year's run of the Specsavers Limerick Panto, 'Jack & the Beanstalk'. Since the initiative started in 2024, more than 930 children and families have attended the show for free. The campaign recently won the Creative Access Award at the Business to Arts Awards 2026.

Charities and community organisations supporting families who might otherwise miss out are now invited to apply for tickets. Every donation to the campaign is matched by UCH and Specsavers Limerick, doubling the impact of each contribution.

"Panto is such a special Christmas tradition and we want as many children and families as possible to have the chance to experience it," said UCH director Sinéad Hope. The panto runs at the venue from December 14 to January 10, 2027. Donations and community applications can be made at uch.ie/donate.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363564.localAngle: The Panto For All campaign provides free University Concert Hall panto tickets to children and families across Limerick who might otherwise not be able to attend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363564.originalTitle: University Concert Hall aims to bring panto magic to 1,500 children and families this Christmas

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363665.headline: South Limerick and City Share Spoils in Cumann na mBunscol Football Finals
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363665.summary: South Limerick retained the girls' title with a 4-6 to 3-2 win over City, while Limerick City claimed the boys' Sarsfield Cup 4-9 to 3-4 at the Gaelic Grounds.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363665.story:
The Gaelic Grounds provided the venue for a chilly autumn night of schools football as the Allianz Cumann na mBunscol Interdivisional finals delivered two competitive encounters.

In the girls' decider, holders South Limerick successfully retained their title with a hard-fought 4-6 to 3-2 victory over their City counterparts. Chloe Lynch contributed two goals for the winners, while captain Lucie Fitzgerald of Herbertstown NS added an impressive 1-3.

Meanwhile, Limerick City secured the Sarsfield Cup in the boys' final, overcoming South Limerick on a scoreline of 4-9 to 3-4. Triumphant captain Conor English of Gaelscoil Chaladh an Treoigh led the way with a standout 2-3. For the runners-up, Tomás Fox of Ballylander NS put in a strong performance with a superb 3-2. Philip Dee officiated the matches as referee.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363665.localAngle: The annual Allianz Cumann na mBunscol Interdivisional finals showcase young Gaelic football talent from across Limerick City and County at the Gaelic Grounds.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363665.originalTitle: Schools football finals at Gaelic Grounds

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363636.headline: St Mary’s Cathedral to host memorial concert for late Michael Plowman
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363636.summary: A special night of music and community will be held at St Mary’s Cathedral on Friday, November 20, to remember Michael Plowman and support the King’s Island Family and Community Resource Centre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363636.story:
St Mary’s Cathedral will host ‘When I Needed a Neighbour’ this Friday night (November 20), a special event of song, community, and compassion dedicated to the memory of the late Michael Plowman, who passed away in August.

The evening will feature performances from a host of musical acts, including ICO Youth and Friends, the Irish Chamber Orchestra Youth Orchestra, Yonit Kosovske, Wolodymyr Smishkewych, Shirley Keane, and Janet Woods.

Admission to the cathedral event is free, with donations being gratefully accepted on the night in support of the King’s Island Family and Community Resource Centre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363636.localAngle: The memorial event takes place at St Mary's Cathedral in support of the King's Island Family and Community Resource Centre, remembering a valued local neighbour.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363636.originalTitle: A good man and a good neighbour to be remembered in song at St Mary’s Cathedral

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363753.headline: Limerick City and County Council buys historic Sailors' Home on O'Curry Street
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363753.summary: Limerick City and County Council has completed the purchase of the landmark Sailors' Home on O'Curry Street, bringing the 170-year-old heritage building back into public ownership to be developed as a cultural facility.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363753.story:
Limerick City and County Council has secured the future of the iconic Sailors’ Home on O’Curry Street after completing the purchase of the landmark property this week. Originally designed in 1854 and constructed between 1856 and 1857, the building was created to provide accommodation and support for seafarers arriving into Limerick during its era as one of Ireland's major trading ports.

The acquisition fulfills a commitment in the mayor’s programme and places the distinctive heritage structure back into public hands via the mayor’s fund. Local authorities plan to bring the building back into active use as a cultural, community, and civic asset, while tying its restoration into ongoing regeneration efforts across the O’Curry Street, Mallow Street, Henry Street, and Steamboat Quay areas.

"Securing the Sailors’ Home was a commitment in my mayor’s programme, and today it has been delivered," Mayor John Moran said. "Our aim is not just to preserve it but to bring it back to life, so that it once again welcomes locals through its doors and serves Limerick for generations to come."

Dr Pat Daly, Council Director General, noted that public ownership allows the local authority to plan for the building's long-term future. The Council stated that further details regarding the future development and use of the site will be announced as plans progress.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363753.localAngle: The purchase secures the future of one of Limerick's most distinctive maritime heritage buildings located on O'Curry Street.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363753.originalTitle: Council completes acquisition of iconic Sailors’ Home

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53937.headline: Treaty United captain named SSE Airtricity Women's Premier Division Young Player of the Year
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53937.summary: Treaty United captain Lawlee was named Young Player of the Year at Dublin's Stella Cinema on November 19. She also earned a spot in the Team of the Year following an impressive season.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53937.story:
Treaty United's captain capped off an impressive season by winning the 2026 SSE Airtricity Women’s Premier Division Young Player of the Year award. The midfielder received the prestigious accolade at Thursday night’s ceremony, held at Dublin’s Stella Cinema on November 19, having beaten off competition from the Shelbourne duo of Halle Harcourt and Maeve Wollmer.

The award recognises the division’s standout emerging talent and crowns a stellar individual campaign for the Treaty skipper, who has led the senior women's side throughout 2026. Lawlee was also named in the Women’s Premier Division Team of the Year in midfield, alongside Shelbourne’s Alex Kavanagh, Sligo Rovers’ Cara Jordan, and Athlone Town captain Hannah Waesch.

Her latest recognition follows a strong year that also saw her claim the league’s Player of the Month award for June, highlighted by a memorable long-range equaliser against Sligo Rovers. The young talent could secure even more silverware this weekend, as she is nominated for Young Player of the Year and shortlisted once again for the Team of the Year at the upcoming Professional Footballers’ Association of Ireland (PFA Ireland) Awards, where she is joined by Treaty teammate Madison McGuane.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53937.localAngle: The Treaty United captain's national recognition highlights a strong year of individual achievements for the Limerick club's senior women's side.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53937.originalTitle: Treaty United captain picks up prestigious league award

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363635.headline: Limerick charities can now apply for a share of €100,000 creative fund
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363635.summary: Creative charities across Limerick have until midnight on November 30 to apply for grants of up to €12,000 from Amazon's Regional Creatives Fund Ireland.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363635.story:
Creative charities in Limerick are being urged to apply for funding as part of the €100,000 Regional Creatives Fund Ireland. The Amazon annual grant programme is designed to support charities that help people from underserved communities build skills, confidence, and careers within the creative industries.

The initiative offers grants of up to €12,000 to organisations registered with the Charities Regulator. Funding is targeted at supporting individuals pursuing careers in sectors such as publishing, music, gaming, film, television, fashion, visual arts, and podcasting.

Organisations interested in applying must submit their applications via smartsheet.com before the deadline at midnight on November 30.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363635.localAngle: Local Limerick charities have the opportunity to secure up to €12,000 each to support creative skills development in underserved communities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363635.originalTitle: Call for Limerick charities to apply for €100,000 creative fund

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53891.headline: UL Vikings American Football Club Welcomes New Players Following Historic Season
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53891.summary: The University of Limerick's American Football team is recruiting new players after securing a sixth-place finish in Denmark and a fifth-place spot in the Premier Division. Both squads are now turning their attention to upcoming college championship fixtures against UCD.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53891.story:
The University of Limerick (UL) American Football team is currently welcoming new players of all experience levels as it builds on a successful domestic and international season. Founded in 1999 by two American exchange students, the club developed into a senior kitted team with support from UL and has competed in the Irish American Football League since 2001.

Head coach Reece Moloney noted that the club benefits from a unique local advantage at Maguires Pitches, housing Ireland's only purpose-built American Football pitch complete with dedicated goalposts. The team offers both non-contact flag football and 11-a-side full contact kitted football, with no prior experience required for newcomers.

On the pitch, the UL Vikings made history in May by competing in their first international tournament, travelling to Denmark for the Copenhagen Bowl and placing sixth in their division after defeating teams from Germany, Denmark, and Finland. Domestically, the senior kitted team finished fifth in the Premier Division, marking their best finish since returning to the top tier in 2024.

Attention now shifts to college competitions, with the Kitted Intervarsity squad facing University College Dublin (UCD) on November 21 in the College Championship. The Flag Football Intervarsity squad will follow on November 28, travelling to UCD as they begin their campaign to retain the College Championship title.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53891.localAngle: Based at the University of Limerick, the UL Vikings provide the local area with Ireland's only purpose-built American Football facilities and compete nationally and internationally representing Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53891.originalTitle: ‘More than just a sports team’ as American Football grows in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363632.headline: Abbeyfeale pianist claims €300 bursary at national classical music final
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363632.summary: Colaiste Ide agus Iosef student Oluwalonimi Adegbola reached the final of Ireland's largest secondary schools classical music competition in Dublin, earning a €300 bursary for his performance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363632.story:
Abbeyfeale musician Oluwalonimi Adegbola has been named a finalist at the 2026 TopSec Frank Maher Classical Music Awards, Ireland's largest classical music competition for secondary schools. 

The sixth-year student at Colaiste Ide agus Iosef was selected as one of only six finalists to perform at the Royal College of Physicians in Dublin. Hosted by Lyric FM presenter Marty Whelan, the evening featured performances of two pieces by the young pianist: Sergei Rachmaninov's 'Romances Opus 21, No 5' and Claude Debussy's 'Prelude La fille aux cheveux de lin'. 

Following the performances, Oluwalonimi and the other five finalists each received a €300 bursary. The awards, established in 2001 by Top Security chairman Emmet O’Rafferty, mark their 25th anniversary this year and were created to honour his late teacher, Fr Frank Maher.

Emmet O’Rafferty praised the standard of talent at the milestone event. "It was a great pleasure to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the TopSec Frank Maher Classical Music Awards and to experience the extraordinary standard of young musical talent coming through Irish schools," he said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363632.localAngle: An Abbeyfeale secondary school student represented Limerick at a prestigious national music competition in Dublin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363632.originalTitle: Abbeyfeale musician wins bursary at national final

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363647.headline: Limerick workers coming off social welfare could claim Back to Work Family Dividend
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363647.summary: Parents in Limerick transitioning from jobseeker payments into full-time work may be eligible for a two-year financial boost. The Back to Work Family Dividend offers weekly payments per child to help families make the switch to employment.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363647.story:
Families across Limerick navigating the transition from social welfare into full-time employment are being reminded of additional financial supports available to them. While many jobseekers are familiar with the Working Family Payment, the Back to Work Family Dividend (BTWFD) provides an extra layer of assistance for parents leaving primary social welfare schemes for work or self-employment.

The dividend is paid for up to two years to eligible claimants with children who stop claiming a jobseeker’s payment or a One-Parent Family Payment. During the first year in employment, recipients receive a weekly Child Support Payment—formerly known as the Increase for a Qualified Child—for up to four children. This amount is then halved for the second year.

Rates introduced in January 2026 stand at €58 per week for a child under 12, and €78 for a child aged 12 and over, dropping to €29 and €39 respectively in the second year. To qualify, all family members must sign off primary social welfare payments, and applicants must satisfy the habitual residence condition. The payment is not taxable and can be combined with the Working Family Payment.

Applicants looking to secure the dividend must complete the BTWFD1 application form and submit it alongside supporting documentation to their local Intreo Centre or Social Welfare Branch Office. While payments generally begin from the claim date, deciding officers can backdate the support for up to six months if there is good cause for a delay.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363647.localAngle: The financial support is available to Limerick jobseekers transitioning into employment through local Intreo Centres and Social Welfare Branch Offices.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363647.originalTitle: Citizen’s Corner – Understanding the Back to Work Family Dividend

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363774.headline: Limerick Council Launches 2026 Christmas Festival Featuring City-Wide Festive Trail
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363774.summary: Limerick City and County Council has officially launched its Christmas in Limerick 2026 festival, featuring a connected festive trail from King John's Castle to The Crescent. The programme kicks off with the Light Up Limerick procession on Saturday, 21 November.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363774.story:
A new trail of Christmas experiences stretching from King John’s Castle through the city centre to The Crescent on O’Connell Avenue forms the core of Limerick City and County Council’s Christmas in Limerick 2026 festival. The full programme was unveiled at King John’s Castle ahead of the official start of principal events on Saturday, 21 November, running under the theme ‘Together for Christmas in Limerick'.

The festive lineup introduces several major attractions, including a new Georgian Christmas Fayre at The Crescent on O’Connell Avenue, running from 21 November to 23 December. The fayre will transform the distinctive Georgian setting with market stalls, artisan gifts, festive food, and a traditional carousel. Other headline features include Castle Christmas at King John’s Castle, festive activities at Arthur’s Quay Park—complete with ice skating and a panoramic wheel—and a festive train through the city.

The celebrations officially begin on Saturday, 21 November, with the Light Up Limerick Procession produced by LUXE. Departing from Brown Thomas at 7pm, the procession will travel down O’Connell Street to Lower Glentworth Street for live entertainment, performances, and the switching on of the city's Christmas lights. Over 150 listings are available on Limerick.ie/Christmas, incorporating both Council-supported programming and community-led events designed to encourage visitors to explore the city and support local traders.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363774.localAngle: The festival spans key locations across Limerick city centre, aiming to boost local trade and community engagement throughout the holiday season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363774.originalTitle: Christmas in Limerick 2026 Creates Festive Trail Across the City

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363591.headline: Four Limerick acts to feature in free RTÉ 2fm live recording at Dolans
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363591.summary: Strange Boy, Layen, T.A. Narrative and Mother of Pearl will perform at Dolans on Thursday, November 26, as RTÉ 2fm's Sessions from Oblivion stages its first live Limerick show.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363591.story:
Music fans in Limerick will have the chance to attend a free live broadcast recording next week when RTÉ 2fm's Sessions from Oblivion (SFO) brings an all-Limerick line-up to Dolans on Thursday, November 26.

The bill features acclaimed Limerick rapper Strange Boy, alt-rock and metal crossover artist Layen, eclectic outfit T.A. Narrative, and post-hardcore, shoegaze and grunge-influenced band Mother of Pearl. Beta Da Silva of 2fm's New Music Show will compere the evening.

In keeping with SFO tradition, the running order for the night will be drawn from a hat on the day and will not be announced in advance, meaning audience members must arrive early to catch specific acts. 

Limerick is the first stop on a four-date live tour for the current season of SFO, which will also visit Dublin and Belfast. While SFO has previously recorded live shows in Cork and Galway, this marks the first time the programme has staged a live recording in Limerick. Free tickets can be booked through the Dolans website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363591.localAngle: The event marks the first time RTÉ 2fm's Sessions from Oblivion has staged a live recording in Limerick, showcasing four homegrown musical acts to a national audience.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363591.originalTitle: Free RTÉ 2fm live recording comes to Dolans with all-Limerick line-up

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363508.headline: Greenmount Park launches 26th annual Christmas Racing Festival
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363508.summary: Limerick Racecourse has officially launched its four-day Mr Binman Christmas Racing Festival, expecting over 20,000 racegoers to attend Greenmount Park in Patrickswell between December 26 and 29.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363508.story:
Greenmount Park in Patrickswell has officially launched its four-day Mr Binman Christmas Racing Festival, marking the 26th edition of the popular post-Christmas sporting fixture.

Thousands of punters are expected to pass through the gates between December 26 and 29, with organisers targeting attendances of over 5,000 people each day. Locally based Big Boss Group is returning as a partner for the event.

Riann O’Dwyer, director at Big Boss Group, said: “It’s a partnership we’re incredibly grateful for, and we’re thankful to the directors and the entire Limerick Racecourse team for their continued trust in us.”

The four-day festival features a diverse lineup of events, beginning with the atmosphere of St Stephen’s Day, followed by Ladies Day on December 27. The racing highlight takes place on December 28 with the Grade One Diageo Faugheen Novice Steeplechase, concluding with a Family Fun Day on December 29.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363508.localAngle: The four-day Christmas racing festival takes place locally at Greenmount Park in Patrickswell, drawing thousands of attendees from across Limerick and the wider region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363508.originalTitle: Timely launch of Christmas Racing Festival

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53942.headline: Jack Brady and Richkov Boevi sign as first players for Limerick FC in 2027
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53942.summary: Goalkeeper Jack Brady and defender Richkov Boevi have become the first two players to re-sign for Tommy Barrett’s squad ahead of the club's return as Limerick FC next season.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53942.story:
Goalkeeper Jack Brady and defender Richkov Boevi have committed to Tommy Barrett’s squad as the club prepares to officially compete as Limerick FC in February 2027.

Brady returns following an impressive 2026 campaign at the Markets Field where he made 34 appearances, kept nine clean sheets, and swept the club's player of the year awards. The 2027 season marks another chapter for the goalkeeper, who previously represented Limerick FC in 2018.
