Meanwhile, 22-year-old defender Boevi enters his third full senior season after breaking into the first team in 2024 and helping Treaty United reach the First Division play-off final in 2025.

Welcoming the retentions, manager Tommy Barrett said: “Jack was a big player for us last season. He made saves that won us points, and the younger lads have someone they can lean on in him. Richkov had a frustrating year with injuries, but he worked hard to get back and showed what he can give us in those last few games. I’m delighted we’ll have both of them with us when we take to the pitch as Limerick FC in February.”

The club will mark its 90th anniversary since being founded in 1937 with a dedicated Heritage Season throughout 2027. Supporters will get their first look at the new Limerick FC identity on December 15 when the club unveils its new crest and kits, ahead of the League of Ireland fixture release on December 16.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53942.localAngle: The historic Limerick FC name returns to the Markets Field for the 2027 League of Ireland season, marking 90 years since the club's founding in the city.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53942.originalTitle: Brady and Boevi lead first Limerick FC retentions

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363425.headline: Crescent College Celebrates Class of '86 and 1986 Rugby Cup Winners
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363425.summary: Crescent College Past Pupils Union held its annual dinner at the Strand Hotel, celebrating the Class of 1986 and marking the 40th anniversary of their Munster Senior Rugby Cup victory.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363425.story:
Alumni gathered at the Strand Hotel in Limerick on November 14 for the Crescent Comprehensive Annual Past Pupil Union Dinner. The evening was highlighted by celebrations for the Class of 1986, which included marking 40 years since the historic win by the 1986 Munster Senior Rugby Cup winning team.

During the event, several special accolades were handed out to notable past pupils. Limerick athlete Ava Crean and Dr Patrick O’Donnell were both honoured with Special Recognition Awards for their respective achievements.

Additionally, Brian Nolan, president of the Crescent College Past Pupils Union, presented the Roll of Honour Award to Barry O’Brien. O'Brien, a Meadowvale student from the Class of 1995, currently works with Goldman Sachs in New York City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363425.localAngle: The event brought together Limerick alumni at the Strand Hotel to celebrate local sporting history and community achievements.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363425.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Crescent College past pupils dinner

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363655.headline: Croom Development Association hosts fifth annual Christmas Craft Market this Sunday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363655.summary: The fifth annual Christmas Craft Market takes place this Sunday at Croom Sports Hall from 10am to 3pm. Organised by the Croom Development Association, the event features local makers selling honey, handmade jewellery, and gifts.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363655.story:
Festive events return to County Limerick early this weekend as the fifth annual Christmas Craft Market gets underway this Sunday in Croom.

Running from 10am to 3pm at the Croom Sports Hall, the market is organised by the Croom Development Association and features a range of stalls from local crafters. Visitors can browse locally produced goods ranging from honey to handmade jewellery, alongside festive treats and unique gifts.

Speaking ahead of her first craft market in the role, Croom Development Association CEO Amy White said: "I am really looking forward to my first Croom Christmas Craft Market. It is a wonderful opportunity to bring people together, showcase the talent and creativity of local makers and small businesses, and celebrate everything that makes Croom such a great community."

Admission details and further information on the stalls are available through the organising association as the community event opens its doors to shoppers this Sunday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363655.localAngle: The annual Christmas Craft Market brings together local makers, small businesses, and shoppers in Croom for a community festive event.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363655.originalTitle: Christmas comes to Croom this Sunday

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363652.headline: New Bruff Traders and Community Committee forms to push for local road and safety upgrades
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363652.summary: Traders and residents in Bruff have established a new committee to lobby Limerick City and County Council for traffic calming, pedestrian crossings, and parking improvements. The group will hold its next public meeting on November 26.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363652.story:
A new community group has been officially established in Bruff with the aim of collaborating on local projects and engaging with Limerick City and County Council on village improvements.

The Bruff Traders and Community Committee has already opened discussions with the local authority regarding several key initiatives. Among the priorities are the appointment of a traffic crossing person for Scoil Dean Cussen, traffic calming measures on approach roads, a pedestrian crossing at the church side gate, additional off-street parking, and the upgrading of the local water tower.

A committee spokesperson said the group wants to ensure local voices remain at the heart of future developments in the area. "This is about bringing people together and working positively for Bruff," the spokesperson said. "There is a huge amount of pride in our village, and by working together as a community, we can help ensure that Bruff continues to thrive for future generations."

The committee is inviting residents, business owners, and local organisations to get involved and share their ideas. The next public meeting is scheduled for November 26 at 7.30pm at CareBright, with all members of the community welcome to attend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363652.localAngle: The newly formed committee is actively engaging with Limerick City and County Council to secure infrastructure and safety improvements for the County Limerick village of Bruff.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363652.originalTitle: New committee to help shape future of Bruff

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363716.headline: Ardagh man Christopher O'Mahony jailed for 16 months over 1970s abuse
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363716.summary: A 68-year-old County Limerick man already serving a nine-year prison sentence has been handed an additional 16-month jail term after pleading guilty to indecently assaulting a third victim in the 1970s.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363716.story:
Christopher O’Mahony, of Kerrykyle, Ardagh, County Limerick, was sentenced at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court after admitting two counts of indecent assault. The court heard the victim came forward to the Gardaí after reading an online news article last year detailing O’Mahony’s conviction for abusing his daughter and sister-in-law.

Prosecuting barrister Lily Buckley BL told the court that the abuse occurred when the victim was aged five and 13. The victim remained silent for 54 years before seeing the media report that sparked her to contact Henry Street Garda Station.

Judge Mary Morrissey imposed a headline sentence of 36 months, which was reduced due to an early guilty plea, expressions of remorse, and his current prison sentence. O’Mahony was handed a 20-month sentence with the final four months suspended, to run consecutively to the nine-year sentence he is currently serving at Midlands Prison.

Readers affected by issues in this article can contact the 24-hour Rape Crisis Helpline on 1800 778 888 or the Garda Confidential Line on 1800 666 111.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363716.localAngle: The offender is from Ardagh, County Limerick, and the case was heard at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363716.originalTitle: ‘Monster’ paedophile jailed after admitting indecent assaults on third young victim

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363756.headline: SIPTU Announces New Strikes at Abbeyfeale Kostal Plant Amid 140 Job Cuts
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363756.summary: SIPTU members at Kostal in Abbeyfeale will stage a 24-hour stoppage, work-to-rule, and overtime ban from December 1. The escalation follows management's plan to cut 140 jobs by March 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363756.story:
Industrial unrest at the Kostal plant in Abbeyfeale is set to escalate next month after SIPTU announced a series of fresh actions, including a 24-hour stoppage, a work-to-rule, and an overtime ban starting on December 1. The dispute centres on planned redundancies that will see 140 workers lose their jobs by the end of March 2027. Workers previously held demonstrations outside the plant from Monday to Wednesday last week.

Sinn Féin Senator Joanne Collins has stepped into the fray, pledging her full backing to the workforce after meeting them on the picket line. She called on plant management to immediately enter negotiations with SIPTU to secure fair redundancy terms and provide clarity for employees whose jobs remain under threat.

Responding to company assertions that the union's industrial action is unhelpful, Senator Collins argued that direct talks are the only way forward. She noted that the union is prepared to engage either directly or through the Workplace Relations Commission, emphasizing that West Limerick can ill afford further major job losses following a decade of economic challenges in the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363756.localAngle: The dispute directly impacts 140 jobs and the wider local economy in Abbeyfeale and West Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363756.originalTitle: Senator Collins backs Kostal workers as SIPTU announces further industrial action

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53964.headline: Free sporting equipment lockers launched at Mungret Park
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53964.summary: Visitors to Mungret Park can now borrow rugby balls, soccer balls, and other gear free of charge using a smartphone app, following the rollout of the BoxUp initiative.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53964.story:
Visitors to Mungret Park can now enjoy a range of sporting activities free of charge following the introduction of the BoxUp initiative, which allows the public to borrow gear using a mobile app.

The scheme provides access to rugby balls, soccer balls, basketballs, and frisbees directly in the park, allowing people of all ages and abilities to get active without needing to bring their own equipment. Mungret Park joins O’Brien Park on Clare Street as the second Limerick location to offer the service.

Tom Clancy, Assistant Staff Officer at Limerick City and County Council’s Regeneration, Community, Sport and Rural Development Directorate, said the initiative is designed to remove financial barriers and make sports accessible to everyone. "It also allows people from lower-income backgrounds to access sporting equipment for free, in a safe, public space," he said.

First introduced to Ireland in 2023 through Local Sports Partnerships and the Active Cities programme, BoxUp stations operate across Europe and North America. Clancy confirmed that Limerick City and County Council and the Limerick Sports Partnership have ambitions to introduce further stations in the future as usage data is monitored.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53964.localAngle: The BoxUp initiative has expanded to Mungret Park, joining the existing station on Clare Street to give Limerick residents free access to sports equipment.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53964.originalTitle: Free sporting equipment initiative launched at Mungret Park

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363676.headline: Taylor Morden’s slasher-comedy-horror 'Bampire' misses the mark with a two-star rating
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363676.summary: Taylor Morden's bargain-basement film 'Bampire' has been awarded a two-star review following its release. The low-budget feature blends live action and hand-drawn animation in a story about a mythical fanged deer.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363676.story:
Film critics have delivered a lukewarm verdict on Taylor Morden’s latest feature, 'Bampire', awarding the slasher-comedy-horror a modest two out of five stars. Described as a bargain-basement production, the film follows an ill-fated professor and a group of misfit students into the woods to track down a mythical fanged deer.

Instead, the characters encounter a half-deer, half-human creature protesting the mistreatment of the environment. The production combines live-action footage with hand-drawn animation, drawing comparisons to an eclectic mix of styles, though reviewers noted the end result struggles to connect with audiences beyond its enthusiastic cast and crew.

While acknowledging the production team's energetic approach and refusal to take itself too seriously, reviewers concluded that the offbeat humor and spoofs ultimately fail to land. The low-quality feature leaves viewers with a uniquely bizarre take on classic woodland tales.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363676.localAngle: Local film enthusiasts looking for new cinematic releases can take note of the critical reception surrounding this latest indie horror-comedy.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363675.headline: Limerick HR Experts Warn Workers Over Workplace Risks of Messaging Screenshots
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363675.summary: Local employment specialists have issued a warning to Limerick workers and managers that private WhatsApp messages and informal group chats can easily be screenshotted and used as formal workplace evidence. Experts stress that digital communication often creates a false sense of privacy that can severely impact professional reputations and team relationships.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363675.story:
Limerick-based human resource management and employment law experts HR Hub have issued a stark warning regarding the dangers of screenshot culture in modern workplaces. According to the O’Connell Street firm, many employees and managers still mistakenly treat WhatsApp messages and private chats as consequence-free, informal conversations.

In recent workplace investigations conducted by the firm, impulsive messages or shared frustrations have frequently been screenshotted and forwarded to managers, HR departments, or investigators. Experts note that digital messaging often encourages a level of casual and emotional communication that individuals would never use in formal settings, leaving comments vulnerable to being taken out of context.

The firm emphasizes that this issue affects managers just as much as employees, with internal discussions and informal staff comments risking severe damage to trust and professionalism if circulated widely. Furthermore, messages in supposedly private workplace groups are rarely secure, as they can be copied, forwarded, or retained indefinitely even after deletion.

HR Hub advises that standard levels of professionalism and respect must apply across all private chats and group messages. A recommended rule of thumb for local workers is to avoid sending any digital message that they would feel uncomfortable having read aloud during an official workplace meeting.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363675.localAngle: The advice was issued by HR Hub, an employment law and human resource management firm based on O’Connell Street in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363675.originalTitle: Employment Matters: Screenshot culture and when private messages become public

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363606.headline: Touring Ska Theatre Show Hits University Concert Hall Ahead of West End Debut
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363606.summary: Too Much Too Young brings the history of 2 Tone to Limerick on November 26 before heading to London's West End next spring.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363606.story:
Ska fans in Limerick will get a taste of the 2 Tone era this week when the UK's first dedicated touring ska theatre show arrives at the University Concert Hall on Thursday, November 26. 

Too Much Too Young – The Music of 2Tone & Beyond takes audiences through a two-hour journey from Jamaican roots to the British revival of the late 1970s and early 1980s. The production features a live band with a full brass section performing tracks by iconic acts including The Specials, Madness, The Selecter, The Beat, and Bad Manners, accompanied by narration and on-screen visuals.

The production carries direct connections to the genre's origins, having been endorsed by Lynval Golding of The Specials and Neol Davies, a founding member of The Selecter. Brian, the show's saxophonist and narrator, is also a cousin of Golding.

The Limerick performance comes just ahead of the production's West End debut at the Dominion Theatre in London on April 18, 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363606.localAngle: The acclaimed UK touring production is stopping at the University Concert Hall on November 26 ahead of its West End debut.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363606.originalTitle: UK’s first touring ska theatre show brings the sound of 2 Tone to Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363511.headline: Fr Casey's carry Limerick's last Munster club football hopes against Nemo Rangers
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363511.summary: Abbeyfeale's Fr Casey's face Cork's Nemo Rangers in the Munster Senior Club Football Championship semi-final at Páirc Uí Rinn this Sunday. They are Limerick's last remaining representatives in provincial club competitions this season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363511.story:
Limerick's remaining interest in the 2026 Munster Club Football Championship rests entirely with Fr Casey's of Abbeyfeale this weekend. The newly crowned county champions travel to Páirc Uí Rinn in Cork on Sunday to face Nemo Rangers in the senior semi-final, with throw-in scheduled for 1.15pm under referee Eoin Morrissey of Waterford. 

Keith Harnett's side secured their place in the provincial series three weeks ago by bridging a 20-year gap to claim the Limerick title against Kildimo/Pallaskenry in Rathkeale, backboned by standout players including captain Diarmuid Buckley, Seán Kilbridge, and Man of the Match Adrian Enright. Sunday's challenge is formidable, however, as Nemo Rangers hold a record 17 Munster titles.

Only one Limerick team, Dromcollogher/Broadford in 2008, has ever won the Munster Senior crown. While an upset by the nine-time Limerick champions is seen as unlikely, a strong showing on Leeside remains the immediate goal.

Elsewhere in provincial action earlier in the month, Na Piarsaigh and Athea were narrowly defeated in the intermediate and premier junior grades respectively, while Galtee Gaels prepare to enter the upcoming Munster Junior B Competition in Knockaderry.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363511.localAngle: Fr Casey's carry the final piece of Limerick silverware hopes in the Munster Club Football Championship after a historic county final win last month.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363511.originalTitle: Remaining football hope rests with Fr Casey’s

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363576.headline: Imelda May announces UCH concert with Limerick duo The Woodgies
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363576.summary: Imelda May will bring her new 'Raised On Songs & Stories: The Lock In' tour to the University Concert Hall on Sunday, February 28, 2027, featuring Limerick-based sibling duo The Woodgies as special guests.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363576.story:
Irish singer-songwriter Imelda May has announced a Limerick date for her upcoming tour, confirming she will play the University Concert Hall (UCH) on Sunday, February 28, 2027. She will be joined on the night by Limerick-based duo The Woodgies as special guests.

The show forms part of May’s new Raised On Songs & Stories: The Lock In tour, which follows her recent nationwide run. The upcoming performances shift from a sitting room setting to a traditional Irish lock-in format, featuring stripped-back versions of her own catalogue alongside audience participation and personal storytelling.

“I’m bringing my Raised on Songs & Stories tour back to you this spring thanks to your requests,” May said. “It’s not the exact same show as before, but it’ll have the same elements of being a loose, intimate, personal night of story and song, but this time in a lock-in environment instead of the previous sitting room.”

The concert will also feature The Woodgies, a duo formed by sisters who grew up in Geneva before relocating to Limerick to immerse themselves in the local traditional music scene. The pair studied traditional song and chant, building a distinct vocal-focused sound connected to their family's musical background.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363576.localAngle: Limerick-based sibling duo The Woodgies will join Imelda May as special guests for her University Concert Hall performance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363576.originalTitle: Imelda May to bring Lock In show to UCH with Limerick duo The Woodgies

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363490.headline: UL presents honorary doctorates to Rachael Blackmore and Jean Butler
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363490.summary: Grand National-winning jockey Rachael Blackmore and Riverdance star Jean Butler have been awarded honorary doctorates by the University of Limerick at a ceremony in Plassey House.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363490.story:
Trailblazing jockey Rachael Blackmore and internationally acclaimed dancer and choreographer Jean Butler were presented with honorary doctorates by the University of Limerick during a ceremony at Plassey House.

Ms Blackmore, who made history as the first female jockey to win the Grand National before retiring from racing in 2025, was conferred as an Honorary Doctor of Science. A native of Killenaule, County Tipperary, she is also a graduate of UL’s Equine Science programme.

She was joined at the ceremony by Riverdance star Jean Butler, with both figures receiving the university’s highest honour in recognition of their respective achievements in sport and the arts.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363490.localAngle: The University of Limerick hosted the conferring ceremony for both high-profile figures at Plassey House, with Rachael Blackmore also being an alumnus of the institution's Equine Science programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363490.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: UL presents honorary doctorates to Rachael Blackmore and Jean Butler

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363643.headline: The History of Dr Sylvester O'Halloran, Namesake of Limerick's Memorial Bridge
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363643.summary: We look at the life and legacy of 18th-century Caherdavin-born surgeon and historian Dr Sylvester O'Halloran, whose pioneering medical work and advocacy led to the creation of the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363643.story:
Wandering around Limerick City, locals and visitors alike may cross the Sylvester O’Halloran Bridge, but many might wonder what the medical pioneer did to earn the tribute. Born in Caherdavin on December 31, 1728, to a devout Catholic family, O'Halloran received his early education under Gaelic poet Seán Clárach Mac Domhnaill. After witnessing the suffering caused by premature blindness and a local shortage of medical personnel, he pursued medical and surgical training in London, Leiden, and Paris, as penal laws made study in Dublin impossible for Catholics.

Returning to his native city, O'Halloran dedicated his career to improving local healthcare. He served at St John’s Hospital, provided free care at a lying-in hospital for pregnant women established with Dr Patrick Unthank in 1773, and helped lay the groundwork for the Limerick County Infirmary. His medical ambitions also reached a national scale; inspired by French surgical academies, his writings helped pave the way for the establishment of the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland in 1784. Alongside his medical achievements, he published A New Treatise on Glaucoma in 1750 and New Method of Amputation in 1765.

Beyond medicine, O'Halloran was an avid historian who wrote A History of Ireland in 1774, a controversial work published three years before his death. He passed away at his home near St Mary’s Cathedral on August 11, 1807, and was laid to rest in Killeely graveyard. Today, the foundation stone of the Limerick County Infirmary—which he helped establish—is preserved at the Sylvester O’Halloran Postgraduate Centre at University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363643.localAngle: The story examines the life of Limerick-born surgeon Dr Sylvester O'Halloran, the historical figure behind the city's memorial bridge and local medical institutions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363643.originalTitle: Medical marvel the namesake for well-known Limerick City bridge

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363683.headline: St Munchin’s Church to host remembrance mass for local families
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363683.summary: A special service will take place at St Munchin’s Church on Clancy’s Strand this Wednesday, November 25, at 7pm to remember late residents and support bereaved families in the parish.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363683.story:
St Munchin’s Church on Clancy’s Strand will host a special remembrance mass this coming Wednesday, November 25, starting at 7pm.

The service is dedicated to honoring beloved late members of St Munchin’s Parish and local residents who have passed away. Organisers have designed the evening to provide a welcoming space for bereaved families to unite in commemoration and shared bereavement.

A representative for the parish has confirmed that all members of the public are welcome to attend the Wednesday evening service in Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363683.localAngle: The remembrance mass provides a local gathering space for families in St Munchin’s Parish and Limerick City to commemorate deceased loved ones.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363683.originalTitle: Remembrance Mass to be held for residents and families of St Munchin’s Parish

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363682.headline: Giddygoat Patchwork exhibition and free workshops open at Ellen Street
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363682.summary: A pre-Christmas exhibition celebrating Limerick's textile heritage opens at 14 Ellen Street this week, accompanied by free workshops led by artist Gerardine Cahil.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363682.story:
A new pre-Christmas exhibition celebrating patchwork, embroidery, and traditional stitching opens this week at 14 Ellen Street in Limerick City, running from November 24 to 28. 

Led by artist Gerardine Cahil and supported by the Limerick Creative Ireland Creative Communities Programme, the Giddygoat Patchwork project showcases local makers and the city's textile heritage. "This project celebrates the creativity of participants while helping to preserve traditional skills that have been passed from generation to generation," Ms Cahil said.

In addition to the exhibition, a series of free workshops will take place on November 24, 25, 26, and 28. Participants can learn to make mini Christmas tree wallhangings, baubles, table runners, and bobbin rolls. 

Places for the workshops are limited, and booking is recommended through limerick.ie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363682.localAngle: The exhibition at Ellen Street celebrates Limerick's rich textile heritage and showcases local makers with support from the local Creative Ireland programme.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363680.headline: Limerick motorist facing car repairs after collision with runaway shop bin
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363680.summary: A Limerick commuter whose car was severely damaged by a runaway wheelie bin during a recent windstorm has been advised on how to pursue compensation from the local business.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363680.story:
A local commuter traveling to work early one morning during a recent high-wind spell collided with a wheelie bin that had rolled into the street. In a hurry to reach work, the driver simply pushed the bin back and continued on their journey, only for the car to break down later that day and require towing due to substantial suspension and bodywork damage.

With the car off the road and subsequent unpaid days off work, the motorist identified the local shop whose name was on the bin. Legal guidance indicates that property owners have a positive duty to ensure items on their land do not encroach on the public roadway, and can be strictly liable for resulting damage if the bin came directly from their property rather than a refuse company.

Affected drivers are advised to retain photographs of the bin and vehicle, secure a formal written repair estimate, and check the area for CCTV footage. While some parties may attempt to defend such claims using an "act of god" argument due to the weather, legal experts note that this defense typically requires a once-in-a-generation storm rather than merely exceptionally bad weather.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363680.localAngle: The advice addresses local commuter liabilities following stormy weather on Limerick streets.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363680.originalTitle: Lawlink – Shop’s wheelie bin hit my car during a big storm, can I make a claim?

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363701.headline: Over €23 Million Paid Out to Limerick Farmers in Advance Support Funds
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363701.summary: Nearly 4,500 Limerick farmers have received advance payments totalling more than €23 million following delays caused by public sector industrial action.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363701.story:
Almost 5,000 farming households across Limerick have received a financial boost with the release of advance payments under key agricultural support schemes.

A total of 4,449 payments, worth upwards of €23 million, have been issued to Limerick recipients under the 2026 Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) and the Complementary Redistributive Income Support for Sustainability (CRISS).

Niall Collins, Minister of State at the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine and TD for Limerick County, welcomed the rollout of the funds. He acknowledged that the payments were "absolutely vital" for the local agricultural community and noted that the Department had worked intensively to resolve delays caused by recent public sector industrial action.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363701.localAngle: The payments directly benefit 4,449 farming households across Limerick, injecting over €23 million into the local rural economy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363701.originalTitle: Almost 5,000 payments made to Limerick farmers under BISS and CRISS

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363692.headline: Six Limerick Red Cross volunteers shortlisted for national awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363692.summary: Six volunteers from the Limerick City and East Limerick branches have been shortlisted for the Irish Red Cross National Volunteer Award 2026 for their work in emergency response and community support.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363692.story:
Six local volunteers representing the Limerick City and East Limerick branches of the Irish Red Cross have been shortlisted for the Irish Red Cross National Volunteer Award 2026.

The nominees have been recognised for their contributions across several areas, including first aid training, emergency response, youth development, and community support.

The Limerick nominees include Niall Healy for Instructor of the Year (Limerick City), Amy O'Dwyer for Newcomer of the Year (East Limerick), and Elisa Sanchis Arderius for Newcomer of the Year (Limerick City). 

Cathal Flannery has been shortlisted for Volunteer of the Year for Limerick City, while Leo Armstrong (East Limerick) and Amelia Protasiuk (Limerick City) are both nominated in the Young Volunteer of the Year category.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363692.localAngle: Six volunteers from across the Limerick City and East Limerick Red Cross branches have been recognized nationally for their local community service.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363692.originalTitle: Limerick Red Cross volunteers shortlisted for honours

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363699.headline: Irish Blood Transfusion Service schedules four donation clinics across Limerick this week
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363699.summary: Four blood donation clinics are taking place across Limerick this week as the Irish Blood Transfusion Service works to maintain hospital supplies. Donors can book appointments by calling 1800 222 111.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363699.story:
The Irish Blood Transfusion Service has announced a series of blood donation clinics across Limerick this week, reminding the public that the need for blood in local hospitals remains constant.

The schedule begins this Monday, November 23, at the Devon Inn in Templeglantine, running from 4.50pm to 8.10pm. On Tuesday, November 24, a clinic will be held at the Caherconlish Community Centre during the same times.

Midweek clinics continue on Wednesday, November 25, at the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints in Dooradoyle from 4.20pm to 7.40pm. The final scheduled clinic takes place on Thursday, November 26, at the Church of Abundant Life on Henry Street from 3.50pm to 7.10pm.

Anyone wishing to donate blood at any of the Limerick locations can schedule an appointment by calling 1800 222 111.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363699.localAngle: The clinics are being held at various venues across County and City Limerick to support hospital blood supplies.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363699.originalTitle: Plenty of opportunity for blood donors in Limerick this week

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363690.headline: Martins Construction to build six social homes at former Thomondgate pub
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363690.summary: Limerick City and County Council has signed a contract for six new social homes at 52 New Road. The project will see the demolition of the former Whelan's Public House to make way for the energy-efficient housing development.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363690.story:
Work on a new social housing development in Thomondgate is set to begin this month after Limerick City and County Council signed a contract with Martins Construction Ltd. 

The project at 52 New Road involves demolishing existing structures on the site, including the two-storey former Whelan's Public House, an upstairs apartment, and a two-storey rear extension. In their place, developers will build four one-bedroom apartments and two two-bedroom homes.

Funded by the Department of Housing, Local Government, and Heritage, all six properties will feature air-to-water heating systems and achieve a BER A rating. Construction is scheduled to wrap up in the second quarter of 2028.

Mayor of Limerick John Moran said the project helps build the housing pipeline needed in the city. "This project will add six energy-efficient social homes within a well-established community in Thomondgate and brings new life to a vacant site," he said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363690.localAngle: The development brings new life to a vacant site in the established Thomondgate neighbourhood close to Limerick City Centre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363690.originalTitle: New social homes at former pub get thumbs up for Thomondgate

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363687.headline: Limerick native Sonya Stokes named Unsung Hero at Laois Community Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363687.summary: Limerick woman Sonya Stokes has received the Laois Community and Voluntary Awards Unsung Hero title for 2026. The award honours her advocacy with Victims Voices and local groups in her adopted home.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363687.story:
Limerick woman Sonya Stokes was named the Laois Community and Voluntary Awards Unsung Hero for 2026 at a ceremony held recently. Ms Stokes was presented with the accolade in recognition of her work with Victims Voices, an organisation representing survivors of sex crimes, alongside her efforts with local groups in her adopted home county of Laois.

Those who nominated her praised her advocacy for victims and her role in supporting residents to foster a safer and more inclusive community. Accepting the honour, Ms Stokes said: “No words can describe how I feel right now. I’m shaking. I’m not the only winner; every person (nominated) in this room was a winner.”

The award comes as Ms Stokes and fellow Limerick campaigners Leona O’Callaghan and Shaneda Daly prepare for crucial legislation to reach the Dáil on November 24. The Victims of Sexual Violence Civil Protection Orders Bill 2025, sponsored by Sinn Féin’s Matt Carthy, seeks to empower courts to issue civil protection orders preventing perpetrators from approaching victims upon their release from prison.

The Limerick campaigners have previously shared their lived experiences of sexual abuse with members of the Oireachtas during the bill's progression through committee stages. Addressing committee members previously, Ms O’Callaghan stated: “You cannot understand the need for protection until you understand the fear that drives it.”
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363687.localAngle: Limerick native Sonya Stokes has been recognised with a major community award for her advocacy work alongside fellow Limerick campaigners.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363687.originalTitle: Award sings praises of unsung hero Sonya

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363736.headline: Crowds pack Limerick City Gallery of Art for two new international exhibitions
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363736.summary: Art enthusiasts turned out in force for the launch of Stephen Brandes' solo exhibition and a global collaborative showcase at LCGA.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363736.story:
Crowds turned out in large numbers for the launch of two new major exhibitions at the Limerick City Gallery of Art (LCGA). 

The first exhibition, 'The Death of Socrates', is a new solo showcase by artist Stephen Brandes. It runs alongside 'Thinking of Place IV: Fleet', an expansive collaborative project featuring works from artists across the globe, including contributions from Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Japan, Ireland, Guam, Serbia, and Poland.

Attendees at the opening night event included Alan James Burns, Elio Maeoca, Tryke Roche, Patricia Kiernan, Timothy Emelyn Jones, and Serhii Matviichuk, as the gallery welcomed the international collection to the city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363736.localAngle: The Limerick City Gallery of Art hosted the launch of two major exhibitions, drawing local art enthusiasts and international artists to the city centre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363736.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Two exhibitions opened at LCGA

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363955.headline: Ballymac Deniro claims €30,000 Irish St Leger Final in record time at Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363955.summary: Kerry-bred greyhound Ballymac Deniro remained unbeaten throughout the Classic to win the 1X Bet Irish St Leger Final at Limerick Greyhound Stadium, equalling his own track record of 29.14.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363955.story:
Ballymac Deniro delivered a dominant display to secure the €30,000 1X Bet Irish St Leger Final in front of a large crowd at Limerick Greyhound Stadium over the weekend.

Bred, owned, and trained by Liam Dowling from County Kerry, the standout greyhound completed the Classic campaign entirely unbeaten. In capturing the final, Deniro equalled his own track record time of 29.14, marking the fastest clock recorded across the 94-year history of the event.

Supporters turned out in force for the feature race meeting, filling the stands as racing enthusiasts gathered to witness the historic track performance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363955.localAngle: The historic greyhound racing final took place before a massive crowd at Limerick Greyhound Stadium.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363955.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Crowds turn out as brilliant Deniro wins Classic at Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363703.headline: Former Villiers School pupil Art Thornbury wins 2026 Naughton Foundation Scholarship
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363703.summary: A former Limerick student now studying engineering at the University of Galway has received the prestigious 2026 Naughton Foundation Scholarship at a ceremony in Trinity College Dublin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363703.story:
Former Villiers School pupil Art Thornbury has been named as a recipient of the prestigious 2026 Naughton Foundation Scholarship at an annual awards ceremony held at Trinity College Dublin.

Mr Thornbury, who is now studying engineering at the University of Galway, was among 37 STEM students recognized at the event, which took place at the Trinity Business School. He was joined at the ceremony by school representative Jill Stoney, Carmel Naughton, and Minister for Health Jennifer Carroll MacNeill TD.

The annual scholarship program was established in 2008 by Dr Martin and Carmel Naughton to support students pursuing third-party degrees in engineering, science, technology, and mathematics. The foundation has awarded €7 million in scholarships to nearly 500 students across Ireland since its inception.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363703.localAngle: The recipient is a past pupil of Limerick's Villiers School who grew up in the local area before beginning his third-level engineering studies.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363703.originalTitle: Top scholarship award for Limerick student

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363595.headline: Adare comedian Marty Gleeson brings award-winning show to Dolan's Warehouse
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363595.summary: Award-winning Limerick comedian Marty Gleeson will bring her debut show, Dog Ear, to Dolan's Warehouse on Wednesday, March 10, 2027, as part of an Irish tour. Tickets are available now on Ticketmaster.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363595.story:
Adare comedian Marty Gleeson is bringing her critically acclaimed debut show, Dog Ear, to Dolan’s Warehouse next March. The Limerick performer will take to the stage at the Dock Road venue on Wednesday, March 10, 2027, as part of her upcoming Irish tour.

Gleeson recently made history at the Edinburgh Fringe, becoming the first Irish woman to win Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Comedy Awards for the sell-out show. Her Edinburgh run also saw her claim the Comedians’ Choice Award for Best Newcomer, earn a spot on Rolling Stone’s 12 Rising Stars list, and receive a shortlist nomination for the ISH awards. Directed by Abby Wambaugh, Dog Ear is inspired by Gleeson's time in art school and features bodhrán playing, unexpected news reporters, and reflections on human flaws.

A former student of Crescent College Comprehensive and the Limerick School of Art and Design, Gleeson relocated to London after selling a laptop won in a card design competition. Her career has accelerated rapidly in recent years, including a 2024 stint with the Pleasance Comedy Reserve, finalist spots for the Sean Lock Comedy Award and BBC New Comedy Award, and being named LGBTQ+ New Comedian of the Year.

Tickets for the Dolan’s Warehouse performance on March 10, 2027, are on sale now through Ticketmaster.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363595.localAngle: Limerick native and Adare comedian Marty Gleeson is returning home to perform her award-winning debut show at Dolan's Warehouse.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363595.originalTitle: Adare comedian Marty Gleeson brings award-winning Dog Ear to Dolan’s Warehouse

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363579.headline: Limerick Choral Union performs Handel's Messiah at University Concert Hall
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363579.summary: Limerick's longest-serving choir will stage its biennial performance of Handel's Messiah at the University Concert Hall on Saturday, November 28, featuring the LCU Orchestra and a quartet of guest soloists.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363579.story:
Limerick Choral Union (LCU) returns to the University Concert Hall stage on Saturday, November 28, for its biennial performance of Handel’s much-loved oratorio, Messiah. The seasonal concert begins at 8pm and features the city's longest-serving choir alongside the LCU Orchestra.

The performance will be directed by Malcolm Green and features a line-up of four soloists: soprano Rachel Croash, mezzo-soprano Gemma Ni Bhriain, tenor Andrew Gavin, and bass Jakob Mahase. 

Speaking ahead of the concert, LCU assistant chairperson and PRO Lorraine MacMahon highlighted the deep bonds within the choir. “In our choir, we don’t just blend our voices; we blend our lives. The unique harmony built between our choristers isn’t just made of music – it is forged in shared breaths, mutual trust, and the beautiful realisation that we are creating something greater together than we ever could alone,” she said.

Tickets for the University Concert Hall performance are available from the venue's box office at (061) 331549 or online via www.uch.ie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363579.localAngle: The concert brings Limerick's longest-serving choir and local musicians together at the University Concert Hall to mark the start of the festive season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363579.originalTitle: Limerick Choral Union to bring Handel’s Messiah to University Concert Hall

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363735.headline: Award-Winning Documentary on Mixed Ability Rugby Celebrated at Belltable
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363735.summary: The Belltable hosted a special reception and screening for 'Try', an acclaimed documentary about mixed ability rugby directed by Oisín Misteál and produced by Claire McCabe. The award-winning film drew figures from Munster Rugby and the IRFU for the Limerick event.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363735.story:
The Belltable in Limerick was the venue for a special reception celebrating 'Try', a critically acclaimed documentary focusing on mixed ability rugby. Directed by Oisín Misteál and produced by Claire McCabe, the film has already enjoyed significant success on the festival circuit, picking up the Audience Award at the 2026 IFI Documentary Festival as well as Best Irish Feature Documentary at the Galway Film Fleadh.

A lively gathering of guests attended the Limerick screening, including notable figures from the rugby community. Among those present at the event were Munster Rugby players Calvin Nash and Peter Sileke, alongside Jim Donovan of Munster Rugby and Gerry O'Shea representing the IRFU. Also in attendance were producer Claire McCabe, Fiona O'Sullivan, Pierce Long, Liam Maher, Jim Gibson, Kelley McDaniel, Steven Casey, and Andrew and Samantha Brace.

The documentary's recent accolades highlight the growing recognition of mixed ability sports. The Limerick reception provided an opportunity for filmmakers, local sports representatives, and supporters to celebrate the feature's ongoing success following its major festival wins.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363735.localAngle: The acclaimed documentary was celebrated with a special reception and screening at Limerick's Belltable venue, attended by prominent figures from Munster Rugby and the IRFU.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363735.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Big Try at Belltable

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363777.headline: Foot Solutions on O’Connell Street Issues Five Warning Signs for Bad Shoes
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363777.summary: Limerick foot health experts have released five warning signs that indicate footwear is harming your posture and mobility. Store manager Amy Kenna is advising locals to watch out for persistent pain, blisters, and uneven sole wear.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363777.story:
Limerick residents experiencing foot pain or discomfort are being urged to check their footwear by specialists at Foot Solutions on O’Connell Street. Experts at the city centre store note that wearing the wrong shoes can cause ongoing pain, skin irritation, and long-term posture issues that impact daily mobility.

Store Manager Amy Kenna warned that mass-produced shoes and standard over-the-counter orthotics often fail to accommodate the natural differences between a person's left and right foot, leaving many locals living with avoidable structural problems.

"Foot pain can seriously impact your quality of life," Ms Kenna said. "We regularly see customers dealing with anything from mild discomfort after activity to persistent daily pain. This can limit movement and affect overall health. The right footwear can make a real difference, helping people move more comfortably and confidently."

To help locals identify potential issues, the store has published five key warning signs: persistent foot pain when walking or standing, blisters or calluses from rubbing, heel or arch pain from poor support, tingling or numbness from tight footwear, and uneven wear on shoe soles indicating misalignment. Free foot assessments are currently available at the O’Connell Street premises.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363777.localAngle: The advice is issued directly by the Foot Solutions team operating on O’Connell Street in Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363777.originalTitle: 5 Signs You Need Better Footwear – Foot Solutions Limerick Shares Expert Advice for Healthier Feet

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363896.headline: Pallasgreen carer Fiona Byrnes named Limerick finalist in national awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363896.summary: Family Carers Ireland has announced Pallasgreen native Fiona Byrnes as the Limerick finalist in the 2026 Lidl Family Carer of the Year awards. She was recognised for providing round-the-clock care to her husband and son.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363896.story:
A Pallasgreen woman has been named the Limerick finalist in the 2026 Lidl Family Carer of the Year awards by Family Carers Ireland.

Fiona Byrnes provides care for her son, Sean, who has spina bifida and uses a wheelchair, alongside her husband, John, who lives with a blood disorder. Sean described his mother as the anchor of the family, offering vital practical care, emotional support, and reassurance through daily challenges. Alongside her care work, she has served as his primary advocate in securing necessary services, support, and opportunities for an independent life.

The overall winners of this year’s Family Carer of the Year awards will be announced at a ceremony taking place on November 26.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363896.localAngle: Fiona Byrnes from Pallasgreen has been selected to represent County Limerick at the national Family Carer of the Year awards.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363896.originalTitle: Super carer Fiona recognised for years of care, love, and deciation

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364121.headline: KLM launches first-ever direct daily Shannon to Amsterdam service starting March 28
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364121.summary: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines will operate its first-ever flights from Shannon Airport next spring, offering a new daily service to Amsterdam from March 28. The route connects local travellers to 160 global destinations via Amsterdam Airport Schiphol.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364121.story:
Shannon Airport has announced that KLM Royal Dutch Airlines will operate flights from the airport for the first time, beginning with a new daily service to Amsterdam on March 28. The route will be operated by KLM Cityhopper using Embraer E175 and E190 aircraft, with flight times varying by day and season alongside an adjusted schedule for the peak summer months.

The new connection gives passengers across the region direct access to the Netherlands and onward travel to 160 worldwide destinations through Amsterdam Airport Schiphol. Travellers can connect to key European cities including Brussels, Copenhagen, Geneva, Milan, Munich, Oslo, Prague, and Stockholm, as well as long-haul routes to North America, Africa, and Asia.

Ray O’Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, described the new route as a major win for the region that brings the airport's total number of operating routes from 40 to 44 in 2027. Jerome Salemi, Air France-General Manager for the UK and Ireland, expressed excitement over launching Shannon as KLM's third departure point in Ireland and stated that the service aims to contribute to regional economic, touristic, and cultural development.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364121.localAngle: The new daily KLM service directly boosts travel connectivity for passengers across Limerick and the wider West of Ireland.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364121.originalTitle: KLM Royal treatment available for the first time from Shannon on new Amsterdam route

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364110.headline: Construction on Mary Immaculate College's new 5,000 sq m Limerick library begins January
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364110.summary: Mary Immaculate College has received final approval to start construction on its new 5,000 square metre library and learning resource centre at its Limerick campus, with works beginning on January 4, 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364110.story:
Construction is set to begin on January 4, 2027, for a major new library and learning resource centre at Mary Immaculate College (MIC) in Limerick. The approval marks a defining milestone for the campus, bringing together digital resources, creative practices, and distinctive collections into one central facility.

Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation, and Science, James Lawless TD, welcomed the announcement, noting that the facility will serve as a modern focal point for students to study and collaborate. The approximately 5,000 square metre development will feature flexible and inclusive study spaces, early education resources, media spaces, and a new public plaza with landscaped surroundings.

MIC President Professor Dermot Nestor stated that the current library was built for a much smaller college with different academic needs. The new building aims to accommodate modern research and learning demands while remaining open to local schools and the wider Mid-West community. Sustainability and inclusivity have also been made central to the design of both the building and its surrounding environment.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364110.localAngle: The development represents a major educational infrastructure investment directly at the heart of Mary Immaculate College's Limerick campus, serving students and the local Mid-West community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364110.originalTitle: Green light for new library at Mary Immaculate College

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364102.headline: Prosecution Case Rests in Trial Over Death of Limerick Woman Scarlett Faulkner
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364102.summary: The prosecution has concluded its evidence in the murder trial at the Central Criminal Court in Dublin. The case follows the death of Limerick woman Scarlett Faulkner after an incident in Tipperary earlier this year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364102.story:
The presentation of evidence by the prosecution in the Scarlett Faulkner murder trial concluded today at the Central Criminal Court in Dublin.

Ms Faulkner, who had an address at Longpavement in Limerick, passed away on April 13 following an incident in Birdhill, County Tipperary, on March 21. 

A 17-year-old girl, who cannot be identified due to her age, has pleaded not guilty to Ms Faulkner’s murder but has entered a guilty plea to manslaughter. Meanwhile, a 41-year-old woman has pleaded not guilty to murder, alongside separate charges of burglary, entering a building as a trespasser, and causing criminal damage at a Tipperary address on March 20. She has also entered a not guilty plea to a third charge of burglary and assault causing harm at an address in Limerick on March 21.

Now in its third week, the trial before Mr Justice Kerida Naidoo and a 12-person jury has heard evidence from investigating Gardaí, witness testimony, and Garda interviews with the accused. The court case continues tomorrow.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364102.localAngle: The victim, Scarlett Faulkner, had an address at Longpavement in Limerick, and the charges include an alleged offence at a Limerick address.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364102.originalTitle: Prosecution evidence concluded in Scarlett Faulkner murder trial

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364091.headline: Steven Spielberg to Direct Film Adaptation of Former Limerick Journalist's Novel
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364091.summary: Hollywood director Steven Spielberg is adapting former Limerick Post journalist Kevin Barry's 2024 novel, The Heart in Winter. The 19th-century western will feature an all-star cast including Cillian Murphy and Jessie Buckley, with a script by Paul Thomas Anderson.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364091.story:
Steven Spielberg is set to direct a new film adaptation of The Heart in Winter, a 2024 novel by acclaimed author and former Limerick Post journalist Kevin Barry. The project will feature a screenplay by multiple Oscar winner Paul Thomas Anderson.

According to entertainment publication Deadline, the 19th-century western will boast an all-star cast of Oscar-winning actors, including Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy, and Mark Rylance. Set between Montana and California, the story follows Tom Rourke and Polly Gillespie as they go on the run. A release date is anticipated for 2028.

Spielberg expressed enthusiasm for the project, telling Deadline that the story quickly became close to both his and Anderson's hearts. Barry, whose previous novel City of Bohane won the 2013 International Dublin Literary Award, previously reflected on how his childhood growing up in Limerick City in the 1970s and 80s influenced his writing, noting that his experiences have occasionally made their way into his westerns.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364091.localAngle: The book's author, Kevin Barry, is a former Limerick Post journalist who grew up in Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364091.originalTitle: Former Post journalist to have his book adapted for new Spielberg film

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363885.headline: Limerick Milk Market Unveils Packed Festive Programme Starting November 28
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363885.summary: The historic Limerick Milk Market has announced a month-long Christmas schedule running from November 28 to Christmas Eve, featuring local food, artisan crafts, live music, and charity events.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363885.story:
The Limerick Milk Market is preparing for a busy festive season with a packed programme of events running from Saturday, November 28, through to Christmas Eve. Visitors can expect a range of seasonal experiences, including weekend festive food and craft markets, live music, art exhibitions, community events, and appearances from Santa and his elves.

The Christmas Main Series is supported by Limerick City and County Council alongside Lyons of Limerick, bringing together local organisations and businesses for the historic venue's celebrations. The opening weekend on November 28 will feature a charity Santa visit in aid of Limerick Suicide Watch, accompanied by Christmas Elves from Fidget Feet and live entertainment.

Additional highlights include a Christmas cupcake fundraising day for the Rising Together Training Centre on December 4, a Lego-inspired Santa's grotto, and an art fair with over 35 local stalls on December 5. Later in the month, the market will host the TY Student Enterprise Market, the Limerick Opera Festival, an Irish-German Christmas event on December 11, and the Christmas Ivory Elephant Market alongside the Boherbuoy Band Christmas Concert on December 13.

“We’re thrilled to welcome everyone back for another magical Christmas series,” said David Fitzgerald, Manager of the Limerick Milk Market. “Our community spirit, local food, and festive atmosphere make the market a truly special place to celebrate Christmas in Limerick.”
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363885.localAngle: The historic Limerick Milk Market serves as a central festive hub for the city, bringing together local traders, charities, and shoppers throughout the holiday season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363885.originalTitle: T’is the season for Milk Market Christmas delights

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363882.headline: Flood Street Man Denied Bail After Christmas Day Toy Theft and Salon Break-In
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363882.summary: A 37-year-old Limerick man facing 15 charges, including stealing children's toys on Christmas Day and taking staff tips from a city salon, has been refused bail by the District Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363882.story:
A 37-year-old Limerick man accused of stealing children’s toys from a car on Christmas Day and robbing staff tips from a city hair salon has been refused bail following Garda objections.

Judge Patricia Harney presided over the Limerick District Court hearing for Joseph Sheehan, of 40 Flood Street, who faces a total of 15 charges relating to alleged thefts and burglaries across different dates and locations. Among the allegations, Gardaí stated that Mr Sheehan stole children’s toys, Brown Thomas vouchers, shoes, and a Munster rugby jacket from a car boot on December 25. None of the items have been recovered.

The court also heard allegations that Mr Sheehan broke into the Bellissimo beauty salon on December 16, making off with 40 envelopes containing staff tips totaling €2,000. Further charges include stealing a €725 bicycle, taking an Audi A3 without permission, causing €2,500 in damage to the door of Roberts Auctioneers on Henry Street, attempting to use a stolen bank card, and trying to escape from Garda custody while visiting University Hospital Limerick on March 9.

Garda Shane Stanley objected to bail over fears the accused might commit further offences and fail to appear in court, noting Mr Sheehan had previously informed Gardaí of a chronic crack cocaine addiction. Defence representation argued that the accused had been in custody since March, remained drug-free, and would obey any imposed conditions. While acknowledging the presumption of innocence, Judge Harney ultimately refused the bail application.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363882.localAngle: The case involves alleged crimes committed at various locations across Limerick City, including a local salon, a Henry Street business, and University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363882.originalTitle: No bail for man accused of stealing toys on Christmas Day

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364025.headline: Askeaton Jockey Áine O’Connor Rides Ifuknowuknow to Punchestown Victory
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364025.summary: Askeaton jockey Áine O'Connor secured a three-length victory aboard Ifuknowuknow in a competitive bumper at Punchestown over the weekend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364025.story:
Talented Askeaton jockey Áine O’Connor rode Ifuknowuknow to a decisive three-length victory in a competitive bumper at Punchestown over the weekend. Sent off at 4/1, the winner is owned by Sarah-Ann Madden and trained in County Kildare by Sonny Carey.

The successful partnership is already familiar with the winner's circle, having previously scored with Ifuknowuknow back in September at Downpatrick.

Meanwhile, O’Connor’s family enjoyed further success on the track as her sister, Ciara, and her trainer-husband Harry Fry teamed up for a win earlier the same afternoon with Miss Goldfire (12/1) at Ascot.

The local racing spotlight now turns toward the upcoming four-day Mr Binman Christmas Racing Festival, which features a prize fund of €600,000.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364025.localAngle: The winning jockey, Áine O'Connor, hails from Askeaton in County Limerick.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364028.headline: Limerick Council pays tribute to late boxer Lee Reeves
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364028.summary: Limerick City and County Council has passed a vote of sympathy following the tragic passing of 31-year-old boxer Lee Reeves, three months after he suffered serious injuries in a bout at Dublin’s 3Arena.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364028.story:
Limerick City and County Council has passed a formal vote of sympathy in tribute to local boxer Lee Reeves, who has passed away three months after sustaining serious injuries in a bout at Dublin’s 3Arena.

Elected representatives across the chamber paid emotional tributes to the 31-year-old southpaw at this week's council meeting. Fianna Fáil councillor Catherine Slattery, who previously hosted a civic reception for Reeves during her time as Príomh Chomhairleoir, remembered him for his extensive work with youths in sport and mental health advocacy. 

Mayor John Moran and fellow councillors—including Sarah Beasley, Pádraigh Reale, and Sharon Benson—hailed Reeves as a charismatic and positive role model. They highlighted his dedication to local disadvantaged communities and ambassadorial work with Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention.

Reeves was remembered not only as a sporting star and soldier, but as a devoted son, brother, grandson, and nephew who left a lasting, profound impact on the entire city of Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364028.localAngle: The story centers on a beloved Limerick boxer and the official tribute paid to him by the local municipal council.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364028.originalTitle: Local reps pays tribute to ‘inspirational’ Lee Reeves

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364129.headline: Limerick Education Support Centre Backs National Campaign to Put Nature in Schools
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364129.summary: Limerick schools are being urged to sign up for 'Our Dúlra Agreement', a new national initiative designed to embed biodiversity into daily school life. The Limerick Education Support Centre is backing the scheme and offering free online training resources for local teachers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364129.story:
Limerick schools are being encouraged to give nature and biodiversity a greater place in the classroom under a new national initiative supported locally by the Limerick Education Support Centre (ESC).

'Our Dúlra Agreement' was launched in Dublin on November 12 by Minister of State for Nature, Heritage and Biodiversity Christopher O’Sullivan. Developed by the Irish Schools Sustainability Network (ISSN), the agreement invites educational bodies to take practical steps to help nature thrive within school communities by making biodiversity a priority in school management and development.

Norma O’Brien, Director of Limerick ESC, said local schools are already doing wonderful work connecting young people with nature and that the centre wants to help build on those efforts. "There is increasing demand for professional learning and support in the areas of nature, biodiversity and climate education," Ms O’Brien said. "We want to support teachers and schools in building their knowledge and confidence, and in creating meaningful opportunities for children and young people to engage with the natural world around them."

To support teachers locally, Limerick ESC is running a free 15-minute online session titled 'Bitesize Biodiversity' every Monday at 4pm, focusing on Irish plants, birds, insects, and mammals, alongside regular free webinars in conjunction with the ISSN. Teachers can register for the sessions through the Limerick ESC website, while further resources are available via the ISSN.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364129.localAngle: The Limerick Education Support Centre is actively encouraging local schools to adopt the new biodiversity agreement and is providing free training sessions for teachers across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364129.originalTitle: Limerick schools encouraged to make more room for nature

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363899.headline: People's Park wins prestigious UK noise award for peaceful environment
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363899.summary: Limerick City and County Council has won a John Connell Local Authority Award for establishing the People's Park as a statutory quiet area. The accolade was presented at the Palace of Westminster in London.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363899.story:
Limerick City and County Council has been recognised on an international stage, taking home the prestigious John Connell Local Authority Award for 2026 at a ceremony in London.

The accolade, presented at the Palace of Westminster, acknowledges the local authority's successful efforts to establish the People's Park in the city as a statutory quiet area. The annual honours, frequently referred to as the 'Noise Oscars', celebrate achievements in improving sound environments and reducing the impact of unnecessary noise.

The council earned the recognition following a comprehensive three-year project at the park. The initiative integrated acoustic measurements, active listening exercises, and community participation to better understand and protect the local soundscape.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363899.localAngle: The award directly recognises environmental work carried out at the People's Park in Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363899.originalTitle: Award recognises peace and quiet at People’s Park

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364124.headline: Man Remanded in Custody Over Attempted Murder of Teenager in Limerick City
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364124.summary: John Bourke appeared before Limerick District Court charged with the attempted murder of a 16-year-old boy on Parnell Street. The 39-year-old made no reply to the charge and was remanded in custody until December.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364124.story:
A 39-year-old man has appeared in court charged with the attempted murder of a 16-year-old boy in Limerick City earlier this year.

John Bourke, of no fixed abode in Limerick, appeared before Limerick District Court on Tuesday. Detective Garda Shane Kirwan of Roxboro Road Garda Station told the court that he arrested and charged Mr Bourke, noting that the accused “made no reply” to the charge. The court heard that the offence is alleged to have taken place on June 12, 2026, at Parnell Street, contrary to Common Law.

Mr Bourke faces an additional charge of possessing a knife with intent to cause injury at the same location on the same date, contrary to the Firearms and Offensive Weapons Act, 1990. Sergeant Aisling O’Neill informed the court that the Director of Public Prosecutions has directed a trial on indictment.

Defence solicitor Sarah Ryan told the court that her client was not seeking bail. Judge Patricia Harney remanded Mr Bourke in custody to appear again before Limerick District Court on December 1 for the presentation of a book of evidence.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364124.localAngle: The case involves a serious alleged incident on Parnell Street in Limerick City and was heard at Limerick District Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364124.originalTitle: Man charged with attempted murder of boy (16) in Limerick City

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364116.headline: Limerick City and County Council Passes €1.6bn Budget with Four Per Cent Commercial Rate Hike
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364116.summary: Limerick councillors have voted through a total €1.6bn Revenue and Capital Budget for 2027, which includes a four per cent increase in commercial rates. To offset the impact on small and medium enterprises, the Small and Medium Business Support Scheme grant will rise from 17.5 to 19 per cent.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364116.story:
Limerick City and County Council agreed its 2027 budget on Monday evening, securing a total proposed Revenue and Capital Budget of €1.6bn with cross-party support. Often dubbed "the Mayor’s budget" by councillors, the financial plan focuses heavily on housing, infrastructure, community services, and the implementation of the 'More for Limerick' mayoral programme.

While the budget introduces a four per cent increase in commercial rates, local officials have moved to cushion the blow for local businesses. The Small and Medium Business Support Scheme grant percentage will increase from 17.5 per cent to 19 per cent to mitigate the rising costs. The majority of the overall funding—€587 million—is allocated to the Housing Assistance Payment Shared Services Centre operated by Limerick on behalf of local authorities nationwide, alongside €321 million for day-to-day services and €681 million in anticipated capital expenditure.

Major capital projects slated in the programme include €327 million for social and affordable housing schemes such as cost rental, as well as continued development on strategic transport links including the Foynes to Limerick Road Project and the N/M20 Cork to Limerick Project. Local Property Tax rates remained unchanged after a proposal to raise them did not secure enough support from members earlier in the autumn.

“When we ask businesses and residents to contribute more, they are entitled to see what that investment delivers," Mayor John Moran said following the vote. Council Director General Dr Pat Daly added that the financial framework will support over 700 council services and investments across transport, the public realm, and environmental services throughout the year ahead.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364116.localAngle: The newly passed €1.6bn budget directly dictates local spending on housing, roads, and municipal services across Limerick for the coming year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364116.originalTitle: Limerick Council delivers balanced budget despite the ‘elephants in the room’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363887.headline: Thomond Community College students open time-capsule letters from their past selves
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363887.summary: Second-year students at Thomond Community College received letters they wrote to themselves at the start of first year as part of an An Post initiative. The return mail gave pupils a chance to reflect on their personal growth and goals.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363887.story:
Second-year students at Thomond Community College recently received a special delivery of letters written by their past selves at the beginning of first year. The return of the mail was organised as part of the An Post Letter to My Future Self initiative.

Pupils used the opportunity to reflect on their personal journeys, looking back at the hopes, goals, and aspirations they had set down on paper a year prior. Students reviewed how much they have grown and considered whether they managed to achieve the targets they set for themselves when they first entered the school.

Evaluation data from the initiative highlighted that writing the initial letters marked the first time over 50 per cent of the participants had ever written a physical letter. An overwhelming 86 per cent of the students reported feeling a sense of happiness and nostalgia upon reading their past messages, while also acknowledging the significant personal development they experienced over the school year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363887.localAngle: Second-year students at Thomond Community College in Limerick reflected on their personal growth after receiving special return-to-sender post through an An Post initiative.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363887.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Special return to sender mail day at Limerick school

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363880.headline: Pádraic Collins appointed as new Mary Immaculate College hurling manager
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363880.summary: All-Ireland winner Pádraic 'Podge' Collins has taken over as manager of the Mary Immaculate College senior hurling team, succeeding Jamie Wall ahead of the 2026/27 Fitzgibbon Cup campaign.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363880.story:
All-Ireland winner Pádraic ‘Podge’ Collins has been named as the new manager of the Mary Immaculate College (MIC) senior hurling team. He steps into the role to succeed Jamie Wall, who departs following a hugely successful period in charge.

Collins is already well-acquainted with the Limerick-based college's hurling setup, having previously served on the management team as head coach under Wall alongside Aidan Scott and Mark Gennery. An accomplished player with Cratloe, Collins won two All-Ireland Under-21 hurling titles in 2012 and 2013, before helping Clare secure the Liam MacCarthy Cup in 2013—a standout year that also earned him a GAA-GPA All-Star Award and The Sunday Game Player of the Year accolade.

Looking ahead to the upcoming 2026/27 Fitzgibbon Cup campaign, Collins expressed enthusiasm for his new responsibilities. "Having worked under Jamie as head coach for three years, I have learned a huge amount and am ready and excited for this new opportunity," he said.

"With a great bunch of players involved this year, along with a new backroom team, I’m looking forward to developing the squad further and bringing them on a journey where we continue to compete successfully at the highest level." MIC extended its thanks to Jamie Wall for his contributions and wished Collins success as he leads the college's hurling squad into its next chapter.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363880.localAngle: The appointment directly impacts Mary Immaculate College, a prominent third-level institution based in Limerick, as it prepares for the upcoming Fitzgibbon Cup campaign.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363880.originalTitle: Podge named new MIC hurling boss

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363772.headline: Savoy Hotel hosts annual fundraising luncheon in support of St Gabriel's
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363772.summary: Supporters gathered at Limerick City's Savoy Hotel for the annual fundraising luncheon in aid of St Gabriel's. Attendees enjoyed the event, captured in a series of photographs by Brendan Gleeson.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363772.story:
The Savoy Hotel in Limerick City provided the venue for the annual fundraising luncheon in aid of St Gabriel's, drawing a large crowd of local supporters.

Among those in attendance at the city centre hotel were Lucia Randles, Caroline Hurley, Rita Geary, and Jean Wright, who were photographed by Brendan Gleeson as part of the day's proceedings.

Further groups spotted at the annual charity gathering included Lizett Marais, Aideen Shinnors, Maria Gormes, Susan Walsh, Patsy Lyons, Morna Mullally, Marion Barnes, and Aoife Kennedy.

Additional attendees captured at the event included Jackie Fox, Sandra Egan, Mary Considine, Jackie O'Dowd, Deborah Fitzpatrick, and Catherine O'Carroll, as the community turned out to support the local cause.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363772.localAngle: The annual fundraising event took place at the Savoy Hotel in Limerick City in aid of St Gabriel's.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363772.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Successful luncheon for St Gabriel’s

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363907.headline: TD Pleads with Minister to Sign Off on 180 Staff for UHL
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363907.summary: Independent Ireland TD Richard O'Donoghue has called on Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill to approve 180 offered positions at University Hospital Limerick. He argued that chronic overcrowding at the facility stems directly from a lack of permanent staff and adequate facilities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363907.story:
