Independent Ireland TD Richard O’Donoghue has urged the government to immediately clear 180 offered healthcare positions waiting for sign-off at University Hospital Limerick (UHL). Speaking in the Dáil, the County Limerick politician said he learned of the backlog during a recent meeting with HSE Mid West.

Mr O’Donoghue stressed that UHL faces unique pressures compared to other hospitals, serving not only Limerick City and County but also patients from Clare, Tipperary, and north Kerry. He told Leinster House colleagues that overcrowding at the frequently ranked most overcrowded hospital in the country is driven entirely by shortages in staff and facilities, rather than external factors.

The TD also contrasted Limerick's situation with Waterford, noting that while Waterford has been equipped with a step-down facility for long-term care to alleviate hospital pressure, Limerick has missed out due to budget constraints. He criticized the heavy reliance on agency staff, who rotate in and out without providing long-term continuity or accountability.

"For God’s sake, will the Minister sign off on the appointment of the 180 staff who are needed now at UHL and ensure the rest of the staff who are needed are also appointed?" Mr O’Donoghue asked, emphasizing that no price can be put on public health and that regional population growth has outpaced infrastructure since UHL was designated a centre of excellence in 2009.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363907.localAngle: The story directly impacts healthcare delivery and hospital overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick, which serves patients across Limerick City and County.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363907.originalTitle: Limerick TD pleads with Minister over staffing at UHL

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364193.headline: SIPTU Suspends Kostal Strike Action Ahead of WRC Redundancy Talks
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364193.summary: Industrial action at the Kostal Ireland plant in Abbeyfeale has been suspended after management agreed to talks at the Workplace Relations Commission regarding redundancy terms for 140 workers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364193.story:
SIPTU has suspended further industrial action at Kostal Ireland in Abbeyfeale, County Limerick, following a decision by company management to initiate talks at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). 

The suspension covers a scheduled 24-hour work stoppage that was due to take place on Tuesday, December 1. Prior to this, SIPTU members held work stoppages on November 16, 17, and 18, alongside mounting pickets at the West Limerick plant in an ongoing dispute over redundancy terms affecting 140 workers. 

SIPTU Manufacturing Divisional Organiser Neil McGowan said the union welcomed management's decision to engage at the WRC. "The aim will be to ensure those talks result in a fair redundancy agreement for our members," he said. "The workers have shown their determination to bring about a fair outcome and we look forward to positive engagement."

Local political representatives, including Senator Joanne Collins, previously showed their support by joining workers on the picket line outside the facility as the dispute unfolded.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364193.localAngle: The dispute directly affects 140 workers and the local economy at the Kostal Ireland plant in Abbeyfeale, West Limerick.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363905.headline: Limerick Twenty Thirty Appointed to Manage €3m Theatre Royal Redevelopment
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363905.summary: Limerick City and County Council has engaged Limerick Twenty Thirty to oversee the €3 million refurbishment of the historic Theatre Royal on Cecil Street, with early works and cultural use already underway.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363905.story:
Plans to restore the historic Theatre Royal on Cecil Street have moved forward after Limerick City and County Council confirmed that Limerick Twenty Thirty has been appointed to project manage the redevelopment.

Independent councillor Maria Donoghue raised the issue at November’s Metropolitan District meeting, prompting an update on the €3 million capital project. Brendan Troy, Head of Economic and Tourism Development at the Council, outlined that the development will progress through a structured programme including feasibility work, investigative surveys, emergency works, and the procurement of an architect-led design team and planning consultant.

Funding for the project includes a significant allocation from this year’s mayoral fund, with further applications planned in the coming years. While longer-term refurbishment works are being advanced, the Council confirmed that the building is already facilitating appropriate temporary cultural uses alongside initial works on site.

Built in 1833, the Cecil Street venue has a rich history in Limerick life spanning more than 150 years. The building has previously served as an art school, lecture hall, library, theatre, cinema, and live music venue, hosting notable moments such as the filming of a *Father Ted* Eurovision episode, talks by Patrick Pearse and Oscar Wilde, and a post-million-sales performance by Limerick band The Cranberries.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363905.localAngle: The redevelopment of the historic Theatre Royal on Cecil Street brings a landmark city centre cultural venue back into focus for the local community.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363912.headline: Brendan Courtney urges Limerick people to brave the cold for Irish Heart Foundation
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363912.summary: TV presenter Brendan Courtney is calling on the Limerick public to complete 12 cold-water plunges in December to raise funds for heart, stroke, and thrombosis patients.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363912.story:
TV personality and designer Brendan Courtney has launched the Irish Heart Foundation's '12 Dips in December' challenge, urging people across Limerick to take part in the chilly fundraiser.

Courtney, whose father Frank died following a stroke in 2017, braved the Irish Sea to launch the campaign, which is supported by Daybreak. Organisers are asking participants to complete a dozen plunges next month to raise vital funds for patients affected by heart disease, stroke, and thrombosis.

Participants can choose how they complete the challenge to suit their circumstances. "It can be a dip in the sea, a cold shower, a plunge pool, even an ice-bucket challenge 12 times next month, the most important thing is that people in Limerick raise what they can for such a deserving charity," Courtney said.

Those interested in taking part can register for free by visiting the Irish Heart Foundation's website at irishheart.ie.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363912.localAngle: The campaign is actively calling on residents across Limerick to brave the cold water and raise funds for the national charity.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363912.originalTitle: Limerick encouraged to take the dip for December

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363909.headline: Author Michael Christopher Keane publishes new book on Limerick and Kerry families
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363909.summary: Limerick author Michael Christopher Keane has released a new book exploring the history of the Spring Rice and Crosbie families at the turn of the last century. The publication is now available in local bookshops and online.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363909.story:
A new book by Limerick author Michael Christopher Keane explores the history and tales of two prominent families at the turn of the last century.

Titled *The Spring Rices and the Crosbies*, the publication focuses on the Spring Rices of Mount Trenchard in Foynes alongside their cousins, the Crosbies of Ardfest Abbey and Ballyheigue Castle in County Kerry.

The Spring Rices of Foynes trace their lineage to a marriage between the Springs of Castlemaine and the Rices of Dingle. According to the book, four members of the family went on to shape local, national, and international history.

The publication is currently available in bookshops across Limerick and Kerry, as well as online through Amazon.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363909.localAngle: The book details the history of the Spring Rice family of Mount Trenchard in Foynes, County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363909.originalTitle: New book remembers prominent Limerick families

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364183.headline: Gardaí and Europol investigate emailed bomb hoaxes targeting Limerick schools
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364183.summary: Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly has confirmed that local information is feeding into a Europol-led investigation after schools across Limerick and Ireland received emailed bomb threats on November 11. The generic warnings caused widespread distress and school evacuations, though none of the devices were found to be viable.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364183.story:
Gardaí are contributing information to an ongoing Europol investigation into a series of hoax bomb threats that targeted schools and media outlets across Limerick and other parts of the country. 

The latest wave of alerts occurred on November 11, when schools in Limerick county and nationwide received emailed warnings stating that a bomb had been hidden in a plastic bag on their grounds. Several media organisations were also targeted with the same generic message, prompting evacuations and significant distress before it was confirmed that none of the threats were viable.

Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly told reporters that the European Union’s police cooperation agency is coordinating the international probe from The Hague, with Irish authorities actively supplying data. 

"Europol in The Hague are co-ordinating a lot of that work, we’re obviously feeding into that ourselves," Commissioner Kelly said. He urged local businesses and educational institutions to remain vigilant and immediately contact An Garda Síochána if they receive similar alerts.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364183.localAngle: Schools across Limerick county were directly targeted by the emailed bomb threats, causing local evacuations and distress.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364183.originalTitle: Gardaí linking into Europol probe into Limerick school bomb hoax alert

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363903.headline: Shannon Airport Group honours 63 staff with nearly 2,000 years of service
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363903.summary: Sixty-three employees across various departments at The Shannon Airport Group have been recognised at Long Service Award ceremonies for a combined 1,805 years of service, marking career milestones ranging from 25 to 45 years.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363903.story:
Sixty-three employees of The Shannon Airport Group have been honoured for their long-standing commitment to the organisation during special Long Service Award ceremonies. The staff members recognised reached major career milestones of 25, 30, 35, 40, and 45 years of service, accounting for a combined total of 1,805 years.

The employees acknowledged come from multiple departments across the aviation hub, including airport operations, the Police Fire Service, the Search Unit, aviation development, retail, commercial properties, commercial services, and engineering.

Ray O’Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, praised the award recipients for their expertise and hard work. "It was a great pleasure to recognise these 63 team members whose expertise, dedication and hard work have helped shape The Shannon Airport Group over many years and, in turn, have supported the growth and development of the wider region," he said.

HR Director Chris O’Donovan added that the awards celebrate the relationships, knowledge, and experience built over decades. "At The Shannon Airport Group, we are committed to supporting and developing our people, and seeing colleagues build long and successful careers here is something we are incredibly proud of," O’Donovan stated.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363903.localAngle: The awards celebrate long-serving staff at Shannon Airport, a crucial economic and transport driver for the Limerick and Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363903.originalTitle: Nearly 2,000 years of employees service celebrated at Shannon

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363818.headline: Santa visits South Court Hotel to switch on Christmas lights
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363818.summary: Festive season officially begins at the South Court Hotel as Santa Claus drops by to turn on the Christmas lights. Locals and visitors gathered for the celebration, which featured musical performances and special guests.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363818.story:
The festive season is officially underway in Limerick following a special visit from Santa Claus to the South Court Hotel to switch on the annual Christmas lights.

A large crowd gathered at the hotel to witness the seasonal kickoff, which included performances by The Fame Factory. Local attendees spotted enjoying the evening festivities included Ryan O'Shaughnessy, Iwona Pietruszkiewicz, Bernie Fitzgerald, Tara Meehan, Niall McKeogh, Stefan Maidment, Louise Moriarty, Arya Clohessy, and Noreen Clohessy.

Photographer Gareth Williams was on hand to capture the moments as families and community members celebrated the start of the holiday period.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363818.localAngle: The Christmas season kicked off locally with a festive light-switching ceremony held at the South Court Hotel.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53989.headline: UL's Kotryna Pacerinskaite Named National University Athlete of the Year
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53989.summary: University of Limerick student Kotryna Pacerinskaite has been named University Athlete of the Year at the National Athletics Awards following a stellar season in throwing events that included multiple titles, records, and a national record.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53989.story:
University of Limerick athlete Kotryna Pacerinskaite has been named University Athlete of the Year at the National Athletics Awards. Athletics Ireland announced the accolade on November 25, honouring the student's exceptional performances across throwing events that helped secure historic university championship success for UL.

Pacerinskaite’s standout season was marked by multiple Irish Universities Athletics Association (IUAA) titles and records. The Lithuania-born athlete also claimed a national record at the Senior Outdoor Championships, throwing 8.64 metres in the Senior Women’s 28lb Weight for Distance event to finish nearly two metres ahead of the competition. Earlier in the year, she broke her own national record at the Indoor Championships in the same discipline with an 8.70-metre throw, alongside winning three gold medals at the National U23 Track and Field Championships in July.

Reflecting on the recognition, the ULAC women’s captain expressed her gratitude for a successful campaign both individually and as a team. "This award is very special to me, it is always very nice to get an award, but this one in particular, as it was an acknowledgement for everything that I have done for ULAC last year," Pacerinskaite said. "Last year my university season was one of my best, and as a team we did phenomenal."

Athletics Ireland praised the athlete's dominance in the field events throughout the season, highlighting her contribution to the university's collective achievements. The award ceremony was supported by 123.ie, capping off a record-breaking year for the UL student on the national stage.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53989.localAngle: The award celebrates the sporting success of a standout student representing the University of Limerick on the national stage.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53989.originalTitle: UL student named National University Athlete of the Year

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364098.headline: Rian McNamara Scores Hat-Trick as Thomond Rout Scariff 43-10 in Munster Junior Cup
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364098.summary: Thomond secured a comfortable 43-10 victory over Scariff in the opening round of the Bank of Ireland Munster Junior Cup at Liam Fitzgerald Park, led by a three-try performance from captain Rian McNamara.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364098.story:
Thomond made a dominant start to their Bank of Ireland Munster Junior Cup campaign with a commanding 43-10 win over Scariff at Liam Fitzgerald Park.

Inspirational captain Rian McNamara led the charge for the home side, crossing the whitewash for an impressive hat-trick of tries. Further scores from Jack Butler, Jack Purcell, and Paul Oyedeji added to the tally, alongside a penalty try awarded to Thomond. Kicker Aidan Ryan contributed three conversions to round out the 43-point victory.

Elsewhere in the opening round, fellow Limerick side Bruff suffered a 19-7 defeat at the hands of Waterford City, while Galbally fell to a heavy home loss against Clonmel. In the remaining fixtures, Abbeyfeale are set to host Old Crescent on December 12, with the second round scheduled for the start of February.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364098.localAngle: The match took place at Liam Fitzgerald Park as local Limerick rugby clubs begin their campaigns in the Munster Junior Cup.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53981.headline: LSAD students host 'Lights, Camera, Fashion' fundraiser for Limerick Animal Welfare
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53981.summary: Local photographers, artists, and fashion students are showcasing their work at LSAD's Church Gallery this Thursday to raise funds for abandoned animals.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53981.story:
Limerick creatives are joining forces this Thursday evening to host 'Lights, Camera, Fashion' at the Limerick School of Art and Design in aid of Limerick Animal Welfare. 

Kickstarting at 6pm at LSAD's Church Gallery, the ambitious showcase brings together 15 fashion designs from students, 28 photographs from six local snappers, and an art auction featuring 12 donated pieces. Organised as part of an event planning module for creative broadcast and film production, a team of 11 students reached out across the city via Instagram, lecturers, and class reps to unite local talent.

"You’ll have a chance to mingle and chat to other creatives in the city," said Dara McCormack, head of communications and one of the exhibiting photographers for the event, which promises an eclectic mix of local work alongside an interactive model experience.

Attendees can also use a photo prop wall in exchange for a donation to the charity, which provides homes for neglected animals across the county. All proceeds from ticket sales—available on Eventbrite—and the event will go directly to Limerick Animal Welfare, with refreshments provided on the night.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53981.localAngle: The event brings together local Limerick artists, fashion designers, and photographers at LSAD to raise vital funds for Limerick Animal Welfare.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53981.originalTitle: Limerick creatives showcase projects in aid of Limerick Animal Welfare

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363922.headline: Shannon artists launch tandem solo exhibitions at People's Museum of Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363922.summary: Two Shannon artists are running simultaneous solo exhibitions at the People's Museum of Limerick from November 26 to December 10, exploring themes of cultural identity and memory.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363922.story:
Art enthusiasts in Limerick have a double-bill of culture to take in over the coming weeks as the People's Museum hosts concurrent solo exhibitions by two Shannon artists.

Running from November 26 to December 10, the exhibitions feature works by Michelle Hickey Legge and Christina Bennett. The artists' collections explore the complexities of cultural identity, memory, and lived experience through their carefully crafted pieces.
visitors to the museum will find the collections split across two distinct spaces. Michelle Hickey Legge’s exhibition, titled What Tomorrow Inherits, is on display in the Coach House. Meanwhile, Christina Bennett’s exhibition, Tiocfaidh na Mná (The Women Will Come), is being hosted in the Blue Room.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363922.localAngle: The People's Museum of Limerick is hosting the concurrent solo exhibitions by the two Shannon artists.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363922.originalTitle: Two artists, two exhibitions at People’s Museum of Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363921.headline: Thomond Wind Ensemble and choir to headline 'Echoes of Grace' in Hospital
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363921.summary: John the Baptist Church in Hospital will host an evening of orchestral music and song on Friday, November 27, to raise funds for inclusive student spaces.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363921.story:
Music lovers in East Limerick are in for a festive treat this week as John the Baptist Church in Hospital hosts 'Echoes of Grace' on Friday, November 27.

The line-up features performances from the Thomond Wind Ensemble, tenors Shane Barriscale and Joe Roche, soprano Polly Roche, and the John the Baptist Community School (JTBCS) choir.

All proceeds raised on the night will go directly toward funding inclusive spaces for students within the school. Tickets for the festive concert can be purchased through local posters or via the school's website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363921.localAngle: The concert brings together local musicians, school choirs, and residents in Hospital to support inclusive educational spaces in the community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363921.originalTitle: ‘Echoes of Grace’ to fill John the Baptist Church with song

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364235.headline: Bord Gáis Launches Ireland's First Zero-Percent Solar Finance Scheme with €99 Deposit
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364235.summary: Bord Gáis Energy and Finance Ireland have launched the country's first 0% interest residential solar finance package, allowing homeowners to install rooftop panels with a €99 deposit and borrow up to €10,500.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364235.story:
High upfront costs and borrowing rates have long kept rooftop solar panels out of reach for many households, but a new initiative aims to clear those financial hurdles. Bord Gáis Energy has partnered with Finance Ireland to introduce Ireland's first widely available 0% APR residential solar finance solution.

Under the new scheme, homeowners can kickstart their transition to renewable energy with an initial deposit of just €99. Customers are able to borrow between €4,000 and €10,500 over a two- to four-year term with zero percent interest, as Bord Gáis Energy covers the borrowing costs. Research conducted by the energy provider indicates that nearly two-thirds of prospective solar customers cite initial expenses as their primary obstacle.

According to Valerie Hand, Bord Gáis Energy Retrofit Manager, a standard domestic solar PV system combined with Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) grant support and an appropriately sized battery can slash annual electricity bills by up to 70 per cent. Many installations take only a single day to complete, allowing households to immediately begin generating their own power and selling excess generation back to the electricity grid.

The financing option is open to all Irish homeowners, meaning applicants do not need to be existing Bord Gáis Energy customers. Additionally, customers who pay their €99 deposit between November 13 and December 31, 2026, will automatically be entered into a draw to win €2,500 off their installation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364235.localAngle: This national solar financing initiative is available to homeowners across Limerick, providing local residents with a low-cost entry point to install rooftop panels and reduce household energy bills.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364235.originalTitle: Breaking the Solar Barrier: How Irish Households Can Now Go Green for Just €99 Upfront

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364154.headline: Irish Chamber Orchestra to debut at St Joseph’s Church for Christmas concert
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364154.summary: The Irish Chamber Orchestra will perform its first-ever concert at St Joseph’s Church on O’Connell Avenue on December 16. The festive programme features soprano Ava Dodd and the Irish Youth Choir.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364154.story:
The Irish Chamber Orchestra (ICO) is bringing its annual festive programme to a new venue in the city this winter. St Joseph’s Church on O’Connell Avenue will host the orchestra for the first time for 'Christmas Magic' on Wednesday, December 16, starting at 7.30pm.

Tickets are already selling briskly for the seasonal evening of carols and classics. The orchestra will be joined on the night by soprano Ava Dodd and the Irish Youth Choir, under the direction of conductors Patrick Barrett and Lynsey Callaghan. Joel Bardolet will perform as guest leader and violin.

The musical programme opens with Corelli’s Christmas Concerto and includes Mozart’s Exsultate, Jubilate, John Rutter’s Angels’ Carol, and Humperdinck’s Evening Prayer from Hansel and Gretel. Audiences will also hear traditional favourites such as We Three Kings, Santa Lucia, Silent Night, O Holy Night, and The Wexford Carol.

Tickets for the December 16 concert are available directly through the Irish Chamber Orchestra.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364154.localAngle: The Irish Chamber Orchestra is staging its debut performance at St Joseph’s Church on O’Connell Avenue in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364154.originalTitle: ICO brings Christmas Magic to St Joseph’s Church

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363919.headline: 119 People Waiting for PrEP in Limerick and Ennis Amid Clinic Closures
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363919.summary: Senator Dee Ryan has called for urgent action after revealing that 119 people are on waiting lists for HIV prevention appointments in Limerick and Ennis, with both clinics closed to routine self-referrals.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363919.story:
A total of 119 people are currently stuck on waiting lists for vital PrEP appointments across Limerick and Ennis, according to Fianna Fáil Senator Dee Ryan. Raising the issue in the Seanad, the local politician warned that clinics in the Mid West have closed their doors to routine self-referrals and are now only accepting urgent cases.

PrEP, or pre-exposure prophylaxis, is a medication that is approximately 99 per cent effective at preventing the transmission of HIV through sex when taken as prescribed. Since the national programme was rolled out in 2019, more than 11,000 people have accessed the service nationwide.

However, Senator Ryan highlighted a stark regional disparity in access, noting that out of 50 approved GP PrEP providers in Ireland, 45 are located in Dublin, with currently zero operating across Limerick, Clare, and North Tipperary. “These are people taking a responsible step to protect their health and they should be supported in doing so,” she said.

While welcoming confirmation that a GP in Nenagh is currently undertaking training to become an approved provider, the Senator stressed that further investment and expanded services are urgently required to clear the Mid West backlog.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363919.localAngle: The story directly impacts residents in Limerick, Clare, and North Tipperary who face regional barriers and clinic restrictions when trying to access vital HIV prevention services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363919.originalTitle: Senator speaks out on long waiting lists for HIV prevention

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363917.headline: Limerick Council Eyes 2027 Funding for Parkway Roundabout Fix
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363917.summary: Limerick City and County Council hopes to secure capital funding from the National Transport Authority in 2027 to advance a permanent design solution for the busy Parkway Roundabout.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363917.story:
Limerick City and County Council's Active Travel team has engaged with the National Transport Authority (NTA) regarding a permanent solution to persistent traffic and safety issues at the Parkway Roundabout on the Dublin Road.

Providing an update at November’s Metropolitan District meeting, local authority officials informed Fine Gael Councillor Sarah Kiely that the council is hopeful capital funding will be allocated in 2027. A definitive project timeline will be established once the NTA confirms the funding.

Cllr Kiely, who raised the query, emphasized that the busy junction impacts thousands of motorists daily with delays and pedestrian safety concerns. "While there is still work to be done, this is an important development and a step in the right direction," she said after the meeting.

"I have always believed that Parkway Roundabout needs a proper, permanent solution rather than temporary measures. The congestion, frustration, and safety concerns experienced by motorists and pedestrians cannot continue indefinitely," Cllr Kiely added, vowing to keep the project on the agenda.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363917.localAngle: The proposed infrastructure project targets a major bottleneck on the Dublin Road in Limerick City, affecting thousands of local motorists and pedestrians daily.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363917.originalTitle: Limerick Council drives on with ‘proper solution’ to Parkway Roundabout congestion

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363915.headline: Cousin Slattery Demands Answers After Historic Human Bones Found in Cemetery Rubble
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363915.summary: Fianna Fáil Councillor Catherine Slattery has questioned Limerick City and County Council after mid-1800s human remains were discovered on a spoil heap at Mount Saint Lawrence Cemetery, two kilometres from their original burial place.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363915.story:
Fianna Fáil Councillor Catherine Slattery has pressed Limerick City and County Council for answers following the discovery of human remains amongst a mound of rubble at Mount Saint Lawrence Cemetery. 

The remains—which included a human skull and several other bones believed to date back to the mid-1800s—were found in September by a member of the public out walking at Mount Saint Oliver Cemetery. The startling discovery meant the bones were located two kilometres away from their original resting place, raising serious concerns over how they were unwittingly exhumed and moved.

Raising the issue at the November Metropolitan District meeting, Cllr Slattery demanded to know what safeguards the local authority is implementing to ensure such an incident does not happen again. 

In response, Limerick Council acknowledged the discovery and apologised for any distress caused to the public. The local authority explained that during the excavation of old graves by mechanical means, bone fragments can occasionally be transported away with excess material. The Council confirmed that cemetery staff are now carrying out regular inspections of excess digging material to ensure any bone fragments are sensitively removed and reinterred.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363915.localAngle: The incident involves historic human remains discovered across two prominent Limerick burial sites, Mount Saint Lawrence Cemetery and Mount Saint Oliver Cemetery.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363915.originalTitle: Councillor quizzes Council on discovery of human remains at Mount Saint Lawrence Cemetery

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364160.headline: Limerick soprano Eve Stafford to host sold-out candlelit remembrance concert for ALONE
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364160.summary: Limerick soprano Eve Stafford and C. Thompsons Funeral Directors are hosting the sold-out "Remember Me" candlelit concert at St Joseph’s Church this Sunday, November 29, to raise funds for older persons' charity ALONE.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364160.story:
A candlelit concert of remembrance offering a quiet space for families to reflect ahead of the festive season takes place at St Joseph’s Church this Sunday, November 29, at 7.30pm. Organised as a joint venture between Limerick soprano Eve Stafford and C. Thompsons Funeral Directors, all 400 complimentary seats for the "Remember Me" event were claimed within three days of release.

Proceeds from donations collected on the night will support ALONE’s services across the Mid-West. The evening's programme includes gentle classics such as Silent Night, O Holy Night, You Raise Me Up, The Room Next Door, and Patrick Cassidy’s Mise Éire. Organisers have confirmed that the concert will become an annual November tradition in Limerick, supporting a different local charity each year.

For Ms Stafford, supporting ALONE is a personal choice following five years of working with older audiences and people living with dementia through the National Concert Hall’s outreach programmes in Limerick, alongside fundraising for the charity during her 2025 tenure as President of Network Ireland Limerick. "November can be a lonely, dark month when many are carrying grief in their hearts and approaching the festive period feels difficult," she said. ALONE volunteer Caroline Conroy O’Malley will also speak during the event to share her volunteering experiences.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364160.localAngle: The concert supports local services across the Mid-West provided by the charity ALONE and is hosted at St Joseph’s Church in Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364160.originalTitle: Limerick soprano to host candlelit remembrance concert for ALONE

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364094.headline: Limerick Hurlers Featured as 'Season of Sundays' Marks 30th Edition
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364094.summary: The milestone 30th edition of the GAA photography book 'A Season of Sundays' has launched, featuring extensive pictorial coverage of Limerick's 2026 senior hurling championship success.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364094.story:
GAA followers looking for a festive gift can now purchase the 30th edition of 'A Season of Sundays', which captures Limerick's hugely successful 2026 season. The senior hurlers secured the National League alongside the Munster and All-Ireland Championships, leading to prominent pictorial coverage in the new publication.

GAA President Jarlath Burns praised the work of Sportsfile photographer Ray McManus. “Under Ray McManus, Sportsfile’s unique images that cut to the essence of our games make this publication a collector’s item and must-have for legions of Gaelic games followers, year in, year out,” he commented.

While Mayo All-Ireland winning senior football captain Jack Coyne features on the cover of the 2026 edition, Limerick has a long-standing history with the publication. The very first edition back in 1996 featured Limerick’s Stephen McDonogh alongside Tipperary's Aidan Flanagan on the cover.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364094.localAngle: The new publication highlights Limerick's senior hurlers following their 2026 championship wins, continuing a deep connection to the photography book that dates back to its first cover in 1996.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364094.originalTitle: SPORT ROUND-UP: Limerick sporting stalwarts mourned, a Season of Sundays ’26 launches, and more

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364114.headline: Garda Commissioner to Engage With Mayor Moran Over €660k Limerick CCTV Shortfall
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364114.summary: The Office of the Garda Commissioner has agreed to open discussions with Limerick Mayor John Moran regarding a €660,000 funding shortfall threatening the operation of 367 CCTV cameras across the city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364114.story:
The Office of the Garda Commissioner has vowed to engage with Limerick Mayor John Moran regarding the €660,000 shortfall required to keep CCTV cameras operational across Limerick. A total of 367 authorised CCTV cameras are currently in use across the county, including 353 approved by the Garda Commissioner, with 242 live-monitored within Regeneration areas.

Last month, staff at the Moyross CCTV operation centre were issued protective notices due to a lack of a funding commitment from the Department of Justice, raising serious safety and security concerns among Council members. Speaking at the November full meeting of Limerick Council, Mayor Moran said he recently raised the importance of the system with Tánaiste Simon Harris in Limerick and urged councillors to maintain pressure on the issue.

During the meeting, Mayor Moran received an update from the Garda Commissioner's office. "We literally just received a communication from the Office of the Commissioner that he has requested the Assistant Commissioner Denis Ferry to engage with us on the subject of CCTV and will contact us shortly," he told councillors.

Fine Gael Councillor John Sheahan noted the issue remains pressing for both Limerick city and county, pointing out that while live monitoring is vital for the Regeneration areas, significant county CCTV plans are also pending while responsibility remains unclear.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364114.localAngle: The potential loss of 367 live-monitored CCTV cameras threatens security infrastructure across Limerick city and county communities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364114.originalTitle: Office of Garda Commissioner to liaise with Mayor on Limerick CCTV issue

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364031.headline: Rathkeale Historical Society hosts talk on Shannon's origins this Friday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364031.summary: Olive Carey of the Shannon Historical Society will deliver a presentation on the development of Shannon at the Rathkeale House Hotel on November 27. Attendance is free for the public, with new memberships available on the night.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364031.story:
History enthusiasts in Rathkeale will gather this Friday, November 27, as the Rathkeale and District Historical Society hosts its monthly talk at the Rathkeale House Hotel.

Olive Carey, representing the Shannon Historical Society, is set to speak on the origins and growth of the area. Her presentation is titled 'From Riennana to the development of Shannon New Town'.

Organisers confirmed that admission to the event is free. Anyone wishing to join the society can sign up for a full membership for €15.

Ahead of the new year, the historical society is also seeking speakers for its upcoming meeting on January 29. Locals interested in delivering a 15-minute talk on any aspect of local history can register their interest by calling 083 024 6203.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364031.localAngle: The Rathkeale and District Historical Society is hosting the local heritage event at the Rathkeale House Hotel for members and the wider community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364031.originalTitle: Talk on history of Shannon to be hosted in Rathkeale

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363819.headline: Photographer captures festive scenes as Christmas season kicks off in Limerick City
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363819.summary: Photographer Brendan Gleeson has captured early festive scenes across Limerick City as locals enjoy the start of the Christmas season. A series of photographs highlights familiar faces spotted out and about in local venues.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363819.story:
The festive season is officially underway in the Treaty City, and local photographer Brendan Gleeson has been out capturing the atmosphere.

A new photo gallery published this week features residents enjoying the start of the Christmas period at city spots including Fordes and Mother Mac's. Among those snapped by the lens were Rob and Annmarie McNamara, Edel McNamara, Claire Hanly, Chloe Kiely, Killian Kilcoyne, Alessia Bascone, and Barry Kiely.

Locals who spot someone they know in the newly released images are being encouraged to share the gallery and let them know.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363819.localAngle: The gallery captures Limerick residents enjoying the festive atmosphere at popular spots across Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363819.originalTitle: LIMERICK IN PHOTOS: Out and about in Limerick City

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364324.headline: Accused Limerick woman was 'enraged' over affair but had no intent to kill, court hears
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364324.summary: The Central Criminal Court heard closing arguments in the murder trial of a 41-year-old Limerick woman accused of killing Scarlett Faulkner by joint enterprise. Her defence counsel argued she was enraged by an alleged affair with her former partner, but had no intent to kill.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364324.story:
A 41-year-old woman accused of murdering Limerick woman Scarlett Faulkner was “enraged” over an alleged relationship with her former partner rather than acting with any intent to kill, a jury has been told.

During closing arguments at the Central Criminal Court in Dublin, senior defence counsel Mark Thompson said the accused’s reaction to her former partner allegedly cheating with Ms Faulkner was “entirely understandable.” He told the court that Ms Faulkner was allegedly taking crack cocaine with the former partner and driving around Limerick in the accused’s van, leaving the accused “understandably enraged and disgraced.”

The 41-year-old has pleaded not guilty to murder by joint enterprise, denying she knew of a plan to cause serious harm and assisted or encouraged her 17-year-old co-accused. She also pleaded not guilty to separate charges of burglary and criminal damage in Tipperary, as well as burglary and assault causing harm in Limerick.

Mr Thompson questioned why a 16-year-old child would be selected to inflict wounds if a murder plan existed, and noted that while the accused's driving and pursuit of the transit van in Birdhill was “appalling,” her aggressive communications on the day of the attack were directed solely at her former partner with no mention of Ms Faulkner.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364324.localAngle: The trial centres on the killing of a Limerick woman and involves a 41-year-old local defendant facing charges related to incidents in Limerick and Tipperary.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364324.originalTitle: Older accused in Scarlett Faulkner murder trial ‘enraged’ over alleged affair but had no intent to kill

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363936.headline: Design team appointed to advance Limerick Colbert to Limerick Junction rail upgrades
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363936.summary: Iarnród Éireann has signed contracts with Jacobs and AECOM to design major capacity and journey time improvements for the 34km rail line between Limerick Colbert and Limerick Junction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363936.story:
Contracts have officially been signed to progress the Limerick Colbert to Limerick Junction Capacity Enhancement Project, marking a major step forward for regional rail infrastructure. Iarnród Éireann has appointed engineering firms Jacobs and AECOM as the design team for the route.

The project aims to deliver crucial upgrades along the 34km section of railway to increase capacity, improve journey times and reliability, and accommodate future passenger and freight demand. Key elements of the planned works include 26km of double tracking to support heavier rail traffic.

In addition to the track expansion, the development will involve level crossing safety improvements and upgrades to existing public road crossings. The scope of work also covers signalling infrastructure, line speed increases, bridge works, and drainage improvements along the entire route.

The design team's immediate goal is to develop preliminary proposals and prepare the formal planning application for the transport infrastructure project.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363936.localAngle: The project directly improves the rail link connecting Limerick Colbert station to Limerick Junction, boosting transport reliability and capacity for local commuters and freight users.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363936.originalTitle: Contracts signed to progress Colbert to Limerick Junction capacity enhancement

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53999.headline: Saxophonist Leon Buckley Named Young Irish Jazz Musician 2026 at UCH
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53999.summary: Saxophonist Leon Buckley has won the title of Young Irish Jazz Musician 2026 following a live showcase of six emerging artists at the University Concert Hall on November 22.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53999.story:
Saxophonist Leon Buckley was crowned Young Irish Jazz Musician 2026 on November 22 after competing against six emerging artists at the University Concert Hall (UCH). Organised by Limerick Jazz, the showcase featured finalists performing live alongside a professional house band before an expert judging panel and audience.

The evening opened with pianist Sylvan Mayer Whitla, followed by Buckley, whose winning performance drew inspiration from legendary saxophonists Joe Henderson and John Coltrane. His set included an arrangement of Vincent Youmans’ Without a Song and his own original ballad, Hard to Find.

Reflecting on his victory and his musical development, Buckley told the Limerick Voice: “I found genuine enjoyment in expressing myself through music and became obsessed with the art of improvising.” He added that keeping his arrangements simple helped him avoid overcomplicating his performance.

The event also featured performances from pianist Edan Bradley, vocalist Savannah Lauryn, pianist Thomas O’Donovan, and trumpeter Nayan Jayanth Levy, highlighting the breadth of emerging jazz talent taking to the UCH stage.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53999.localAngle: The event was organised by Limerick Jazz and hosted locally at the University Concert Hall.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53999.originalTitle: University Concert Hall awards Young Irish Jazz Musician 2026

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363935.headline: One Opera Square Wins Construction Project of the Year at KPMG Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363935.summary: The six-storey commercial development in Limerick City has been named Construction Project of the Year at the 2026 KPMG Property Industry Excellence Awards. As the first completed phase of the wider Opera Square regeneration, the building offers workspace alongside ground-floor retail and dining.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363935.story:
One Opera Square has secured a major national accolade, taking home the Construction Project of the Year award at the 2026 KPMG Property Industry Excellence Awards. The six-storey commercial building serves as a cornerstone of the broader Opera Square regeneration project in Limerick City and was also shortlisted in the Design Project of the Year category.

The development delivers more than 15 square metres of workspace to the city centre, complemented by ground-floor retail spaces and food and beverage outlets. The award entry for the completed first phase was submitted by the project’s main contractor, Sisk.

Limerick Twenty Thirty CEO Pat Nash welcomed the win, describing it as “a hugely welcome national recognition for One Opera Square and for the exceptionally high standards achieved by the project team.”
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363935.localAngle: The award highlights a major milestone and national recognition for the ongoing city centre regeneration project in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363935.originalTitle: Top award for One Opera Square

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364314.headline: The Waterboys and Damien Dempsey announced for Live at the Docklands
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364314.summary: The Waterboys will headline a major gig at Limerick's Live at the Docklands on Saturday, August 21, 2027, with Damien Dempsey as special guest. Tickets go on sale on Thursday, December 3 at 10am.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364314.story:
Music promoters Dolans have announced that The Waterboys will headline next summer's Live at the Docklands, with fellow acclaimed Irish singer-songwriter Damien Dempsey joining them as a special guest. The high-profile concert takes place on Saturday, August 21, 2027, on the banks of the River Shannon.

Led by Scottish singer, songwriter, and guitarist Mike Scott since the 1980s, The Waterboys bring a celebrated catalogue featuring iconic tracks like 'The Whole of the Moon', 'This Is the Sea', and 'Fisherman’s Blues'. They will be joined by Damien Dempsey, known for powerful live performances and songs such as 'Sing All Our Cares Away', 'It’s All Good', and 'Apple of My Eye'.

Mick Dolan of Dolans said the team is thrilled to welcome the acts back to the city for the riverside concert series. “We are absolutely delighted to welcome The Waterboys back to Limerick and to have Damien Dempsey join them for what promises to be a very special night at Live at the Docklands,” he said.

Tickets for the Docklands show go on sale to the public on Thursday, December 3, at 10am.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364314.localAngle: The concert brings two major musical acts to a prominent outdoor venue on the banks of the River Shannon in Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364314.originalTitle: The Waterboys and Damien Dempsey to play Live at the Docklands

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364299.headline: Radisson Blu Hotel Announces Family Santa Afternoons for December
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364299.summary: The Radisson Blu Hotel & Spa on the Ennis Road will host festive family afternoons with Santa on Sunday 13th and Sunday 20th December 2026, featuring a four-course buffet, elf entertainment, and children's activities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364299.story:
Families across Limerick can book a festive afternoon with Santa Claus this December, as the Radisson Blu Hotel & Spa on the Ennis Road prepares to host two special holiday events.

The hotel will transform its Ryan Suite into a winter wonderland on Sunday 13th and Sunday 20th December 2026. Proceedings kick off at 2:00pm with festive music, elf antics, and a four-course festive buffet for attendees.

While adults enjoy the seasonal atmosphere, children can participate in games, activities, and a Christmas disco led by the hotel's merry elves. The afternoon will also include a visit from Santa and Mrs Claus, with each child receiving a gift alongside a digital family photograph.

Tickets are priced at €45 for adults and €25 for children, with advance booking and full payment required. Organisers note that a full refund is available for cancellations made more than seven days prior to the event.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364299.localAngle: The event takes place at the Radisson Blu Hotel & Spa on the Ennis Road in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364299.originalTitle: A Magical Christmas Celebration – Festive Family Afternoon with Santa

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363932.headline: Podcast revisits 1946 Pallasgreen shooting of Garda James Byrne by Garda Dan Duff
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363932.summary: The Póilíní podcast season finale examines the September 1946 shooting of Garda James Byrne by fellow Garda Dan Duff in an orchard at Pallasgreen, and the subsequent murder trial.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363932.story:
A notorious 1946 Limerick murder that made worldwide headlines has been revisited in the latest episode of the Póilíní podcast. On a wet September night in 1946, Garda Dan Duff shot and killed fellow Garda James Byrne in an orchard in Pallasgreen while the two officers stood guard over a local family facing threats from an agitator.

Serving as the season finale, the episode follows Duff from his arrival as a newly qualified recruit into the strict routine of barracks life, nine months of night duty, and a high-stakes murder trial that left no option for a manslaughter verdict. The programme examines whether the outcome was a miscarriage of justice while looking at the human cost of policing.

The episode draws upon original National Archives files and Patrick Kelleher’s firsthand account, One Mortal Night. Presented by Dr John Reynolds—an Irish policing historian and retired Garda with 40 years of service—alongside writer and journalist Helen Moorhouse, the recording explores a justice system that operated under immense pressure with little leniency.

The podcast was produced by Daryl Moorhouse, with recording and mixing by Sean Byrne at Tinpot Productions Studios.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363932.localAngle: The episode explores a historic, high-profile murder and policing case rooted in County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363932.originalTitle: Historic Limerick murder revisited in podcast

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364146.headline: Limerick singer-songwriter Sebastian Graysen releases new piano ballad single
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364146.summary: Limerick-based artist Sebastian Graysen has released his third single, 'Living For You', a dramatic piano ballad about unrequited love and letting go.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364146.story:
Limerick-based singer-songwriter Sebastian Graysen has released his third single, ‘Living For You’, which became available to listeners on Friday, November 20.

The track is a dramatic piano ballad that puts a unique spin on the traditional love song. Rather than focusing on winning someone's affection, the song explores the reality of loving someone who does not return those feelings, and coming to terms with the fact that true love involves respecting their answer.

“I wrote ‘Living For You’ about someone I fell for who didn’t feel the same way,” Graysen explained. “Writing it was how I made sense of what I was feeling, and it helped me understand myself. Love means wanting what is best for the other person, not what is best for you. Sometimes that means respecting their space and not being with them. It isn’t an easy thing to do, but I know it to be true.”

Graysen noted that while things do not always go as planned, he hopes listeners will find a connection to their own experiences within the music.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364146.localAngle: The release marks a new musical offering from Limerick-based singer-songwriter Sebastian Graysen.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364146.originalTitle: Sebastian Graysen releases love song about letting go

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363930.headline: €90 Million Relocation Fund Unlocks Land for 1,500 Homes at Colbert Quarter
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363930.summary: Minister for Housing James Browne has announced a major €90 million funding package to relocate public services and clear state land for housing developments in Limerick and Galway. The initiative aims to unlock strategic sites, including the Colbert Quarter, to deliver over 1,500 new homes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363930.story:
A massive €90 million in state funding has been announced to relocate existing public services and clear the way for large-scale housing developments in Limerick and Galway. Minister for Housing, Local Government, and Heritage James Browne announced the relocation funding package to activate housing on key strategic sites, including the Colbert Quarter in Limerick and Sandy Quarter in Galway.

The newly announced investment will support the relocation of operations by the HSE and Limerick City and County Council, alongside Galway local authorities. These projects mark the first to be supported by the Relocation Investment Fund (RIF), which is designed to move existing operations off landholding bodies to unlock state land for home building. The latest funding will also work alongside the previously announced Housing Infrastructure Investment Fund (HIIF) to support necessary infrastructure at both locations.

Limerick TD and Minister of State Kieran O'Donnell stated that the funding will bring momentum to the regeneration of the area and support a new mixed-use city quarter. The lands at Colbert Quarter and Sandy Quarter have already been agreed by the government for transfer to the Land Development Agency to directly deliver the housing-led developments.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363930.localAngle: The funding directly impacts Limerick by clearing state land at the Colbert Quarter to make way for hundreds of new homes and urban regeneration.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363930.originalTitle: €90million to build houses in Colbert Quarter

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364185.headline: Limerick installed as 2/1 favourites to defend National Hurling League title
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364185.summary: John Kiely's side open their 2027 league campaign away to Kilkenny on January 24 as they look to retain their title. BoyleSports has installed the 15-time champions as 2/1 favourites ahead of Cork and Galway.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364185.story:
Holders Limerick have been installed as 2/1 favourites by BoyleSports to retain their National Hurling League title in 2027. John Kiely’s side lead the new betting market ahead of Cork at 3/1 and Galway at 4/1, with Tipperary and Kilkenny both priced at 13/2, Clare at 15/2, and Dublin at 14/1.

Limerick will begin their defence of the pennant competition away to Kilkenny at Nowlan Park on January 24. That opening fixture will be followed by a home game against Dublin, away trips to Cork and Galway, and further home matches against Tipperary and Clare. Fixtures against Cork, Tipperary, and Clare are all scheduled to be played under lights, with the League Final pencilled in for April 3/4.

The Shannonsiders are 15-time winners of the competition. Last year, the county achieved a rare Grand Slam by securing League, Munster, and All-Ireland honours in the same season—a feat managed only five times in Limerick's history, in 1936, 1940, 2020, 2023, and 2026.

Meanwhile, in football, Micheál Cahill’s Limerick side are preparing for their first campaign in charge in Division Four. The team will face away fixtures against Wicklow, Leitrim, Waterford, and London, alongside home games against Antrim, Tipperary, and Fermanagh. The football league decider is scheduled for the final weekend of March.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364185.localAngle: The story outlines the upcoming league fixtures and betting odds for Limerick's senior hurling and football teams.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364185.originalTitle: Limerick installed as favourites in NHL

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364370.headline: Tredwell Electrical marks 35 years with new 18,000 sq ft Shannon facility
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364370.summary: Founded in a Limerick garage in 1991, Tredwell Electrical has expanded its operations with a new manufacturing facility in Clare, bringing its total footprint to 37,200 square feet.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364370.story:
Tredwell Electrical is celebrating its 35th anniversary by opening a new 18,000 square-foot manufacturing facility in Shannon, County Clare. The company, which specializes in electrical control panels and system integration, was originally founded by Stefan Uhlemann in a humble garage in Limerick in 1991.

Minister of State Timmy Dooley TD officially opened the new site at the Shannon Airport Business Park, which is supported by The Shannon Airport Group. The new facility complements Tredwell’s existing 19,200 square-foot operation in Limerick, bringing the company's total manufacturing footprint to 37,200 square feet.

Glenn Bain, General Manager of Tredwell Electrical, said: “আমরা very excited to open the new state of the art facility in Shannon, to help meet future expansion and production requirements.”

The expansion significantly increases the firm's production capacity to support future growth. The investment in the Shannon Airport Business Park—home to over 300 companies and 10,000 employees—reinforces the wider Mid West region's reputation as a center for engineering and advanced manufacturing while supporting local employment.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364370.localAngle: The company was originally founded in Limerick in 1991 and maintains its existing 19,200sq/ft operation in the city alongside its new Clare facility.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364370.originalTitle: Tredwell going from strength to strength

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363673.headline: Limerick Man Handed Suspended Sentence After Walking into Garda Station with Taped Knife
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363673.summary: David Kelly walked into Henry Street Garda Station asking for an ambulance with a Stanley knife taped to his arm. He pleaded guilty to weapons and theft charges at Limerick District Court and received a four-week suspended sentence.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363673.story:
A 42-year-old man who walked into Henry Street Garda Station with a Stanley knife strapped to his arm told Gardaí he was carrying it for his own protection, a court has heard. David Kelly, of no fixed abode, appeared before Limerick District Court where he pleaded guilty to a charge under the Firearms Act for possession of the knife on March 28.

During the hearing, evidence was presented that Mr Kelly had entered the city centre Garda station seeking help and stating that he required an ambulance. A Garda witness told Judge Patricia Harney that the defendant had the knife taped directly to his arm, and when questioned about it, replied that it was for self-protection.

Alongside the weapons charge, Mr Kelly also entered guilty pleas for two separate retail thefts in the city. He admitted to stealing €45 worth of goods from Mace on William Street and €190 worth of goods from Dunnes Stores on March 26.

The court heard that Mr Kelly has 27 previous convictions on his record, which include seven for theft, one for handling stolen goods, and one for burglary. His solicitor informed the judge that his client is currently undertaking a course with Slaintecare. Judge Harney sentenced Mr Kelly to four weeks in prison, which was suspended for a full year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363673.localAngle: The incident occurred at Henry Street Garda Station and involved retail thefts on William Street and at Dunnes Stores in Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363673.originalTitle: Court hears man had knife taped to arm for own protection

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364330.headline: Revenue and Gardaí seize €140,000 in herbal cannabis at Shannon Airport
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364330.summary: Customs officers seized 10kg of herbal cannabis originating from the USA during routine operations at Shannon Airport on Friday. The illicit shipment, valued at €140,000, was destined for an address in the west of the country.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364330.story:
Revenue Customs officers and Gardaí intercepted a large shipment of illegal drugs at Shannon Airport on Friday (November 27), seizing 10kg of herbal cannabis with an estimated street value of €140,000.

The discovery was made during routine operations carried out by Revenue personnel at the airport, who were assisted by colleagues based in Galway. According to authorities, the drug shipment originated in the United States and was addressed for delivery to the west of Ireland.

Revenue confirmed that investigations into the seizure are currently ongoing. The interception forms part of ongoing operations by customs authorities aimed at targeting the illegal importation of drugs into the country.

Authorities have appealed to members of the public and businesses who may have information regarding drug smuggling to come forward. Informants can contact Revenue in confidence through their confidential phone line at 1800 295 295.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364330.localAngle: The significant drug seizure was made at Shannon Airport, a key international transport hub serving the Limerick and Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=364330.originalTitle: Shipment of cannabis from USA seized at Shannon Airport

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363937.headline: Community Finance Ireland Marks 25 Years with €1.9m Invested in Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363937.summary: Community Finance Ireland has celebrated its 25th anniversary by revealing that nearly €2 million has been distributed to community-led groups, sports clubs, and social enterprises across County Limerick since 2001.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363937.story:
Community Finance Ireland (CFI) has marked a quarter of a century in operation by highlighting a total of €1.9 million invested into community-led organisations, sports clubs, and social enterprises across County Limerick over the last two decades.

Originally established in 2001 as the Ulster Community Investment Trust (UCIT), the organisation has grown from its initial Northern Ireland-focused roots to become the only all-island social finance provider. Across the country, CFI has distributed a total of €134 million to various community initiatives.

Local groups in Limerick looking to access similar funding are being directed to the organisation's website to find out if a social finance loan could benefit their specific community organisation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363937.localAngle: The funding highlights two decades of financial support distributed directly to community groups, sports clubs, and social enterprises across County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=363937.originalTitle: Community Finance Ireland celebrates €2m in funding for Limerick at 25th anniversary
